# Rask

> Rask is the full-stack .NET web framework — for a team of one or fifty. UI, data, auth, background
> work, realtime and deploy, all in C#, in one codebase built on standard ASP.NET Core and EF Core.
> The stack: Rask.Data (aggregates, audit stamps, soft delete, concurrency, domain events, multi-tenancy,
> full-text search) on SQLite by default or PostgreSQL / SQL Server; source-generated Rask.Cqrs and the
> cached Rask.Query layer; authentication with accounts out of the box; background jobs, transactional
> email, an outbox, cache and file storage (disk, S3 or Azure) on the app's own database — no broker, no
> Redis; realtime subscriptions pushed to open pages; a durable log store and the `/_rask` operator
> console; and the `rask` CLI — `rask new`, `rask db`, and `rask deploy`, which builds and runs the app
> over SSH with zero-downtime blue-green releases, a health-gated cutover, auto-HTTPS via Caddy, and
> bare-VPS provisioning. Production SQLite comes with WAL pragmas and continuous backup.
> The UI is plain C# components (a Roslyn generator, scoped CSS/TypeScript, routing) whose same code runs
> server-rendered over WebSockets or client-side on WebAssembly; markup is a chain — you name the
> component and set properties on it (`Div.Class("panel")[Span["hi"]]`), with anything a component
> requires asked for first, so an incomplete component is a compile error rather than a null. Rask is a
> superset of the other front ends rather than a rival: React/Preact/Solid/Vue/Svelte/Angular/Lit
> components and real Blazor components (Rask.Blazor) run inside Rask pages as islands.

This file helps AI coding assistants build apps with Rask. Start with [docs/ai-agents.md](docs/ai-agents.md)
for app-authoring conventions, then the docs below (the repo-root AGENTS.md is for contributors to Rask itself).
Reading the web rather than this checkout? The published index is https://rask.sh/llms.txt, every
guide in one file is https://rask.sh/llms-full.txt, and each guide's Markdown is its page's URL plus
`.md` (https://rask.sh/docs/guides/cqrs.md).

## Docs
- [The One Person Framework](docs/one-person-framework.md): the philosophy — a whole product from one C# codebase on one server, SQLite-first, for one developer or a team; links the batteries + roadmap.
- [Installing Rask](docs/installation.md): the one-line installer, `curl -sSL https://rask.sh/rask.sh | sh` (Windows: `irm https://rask.sh/rask.ps1 | iex`). `rask.sh` and `rask.ps1` live at the repo ROOT and are published to GitHub Pages by `pages.yml`. They install the .NET SDK into `~/.dotnet` (via Microsoft's dotnet-install.sh, run with BASH — it is a bash script, and `sh` silently works on macOS then dies on Debian), `Rask.Cli`, `dotnet-ef`, the `wasm-tools` workload and Node LTS (SHA-256 verified against nodejs.org's SHASUMS256.txt) into `~/.local/share/rask/node`, then run `rask doctor`. Everything under `$HOME` — no sudo, no distro package manager; an SDK already present is DETECTED AND LEFT ALONE (any major ≥ 10, because `RollForward=Major`). Docker is detected and reported, NEVER installed — only `rask deploy` needs it. Re-running upgrades and rewrites its `PATH` block rather than appending. Flags: `--version <v>`, `--prerelease`, `--no-sdk|-ef|-wasm-tools|-node|-path`, `--dry-run`, `--quiet`, `--help`; through a pipe use `sh -s -- --flag`; an unknown flag exits 2. TRUNCATION SAFETY is structural, not a warning: every statement is inside a function and the file's last line is the only call, so a dropped `curl | sh` runs nothing — `scripts/tests/install-script.test.sh` proves it by executing prefixes of the real file, and also pins the install URL byte-identically across all nine files that carry it. `scripts/run-install-e2e-local.sh` runs the script in containers with no .NET/Node at all (run by CI before a release). A missing ICU is diagnosed by name — dotnet-install.sh unpacks a tarball and installs no native dependencies, so on a slim image the SDK installs and then cannot run.
- NAMES (how every chain entry is reached): `using Rask;` (every template's GlobalUsings.cs) + `using static Rask.Markup;` and `Rask.Core.Routing`/`.Forms`/`.Browser`/`.Live`/`.Authentication` (the server/wasm/wasm-hosted templates'), so a scaffolded page writes no `using` for `[Route]`, forms, `IIndexedDb` or `IAuth`. Elements and markup primitives are BARE (`Div`, `Text`, `Raw`, `Outlet`) — a component inherits them, any other class gets them from `using static Rask.Markup`; the `<html>` element is `Html`; `Markup.Footer` reaches a tag your own member hid. FAMILIES are reached through a group class and never take a bare name: `Ui.Button`/`Ui.Tone` (the UI kit, component TYPES stay `UiButton`), `Trigger.Fullscreen` (browser capabilities), `Validation.Message`/`.Summary`/`.Indicator` (form feedback), `Mui.Button` (an npm package declared with `Mui : ReactPackage`). The kit lives in namespace `Rask`, not `Rask.Ui`.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, first app, project layout; the root component (`TApp`) renders into `<body>` and Rask composes the document around it — doctype, `<html lang>` from the `HtmlLang` override, a `<head>` collected from every mounted component's `HeadAssets` override plus the charset, viewport, kit stylesheet, `Styles/app.css` and scoped CSS/JS, and a `<body>` (class from `BodyClass`) holding the render output and the auto-appended runtime `<script>`; `Shell(head, body)` is the escape hatch for a custom document (it takes the framework's `<head>` and the rendered body as parameters, runs once per render BEFORE `Render()`, and dropping `head` loses every head asset). A root that renders `Doctype`/`Html`/`Head`/`Body` itself is RASK021 — the nested document is silently unwrapped by the parser, so there is no runtime check, only the analyzer.
- **[`Rask.Server` + `RaskApp`](docs/getting-started.md)**: the ONE reference a server application takes. `Rask.Server` is the ASP.NET host PLUS every battery (data, cqrs+query, auth, jobs, mail, cache, storage, outbox, dashboard, logging, webpush, sqlite snapshots+litestream), and it carries `RaskApp`/`RaskAppOptions`; `Rask.Wasm` is the browser host plus the client halves; `Rask` is the shared core both depend on (components, the chain, routing, forms, browser APIs, the generators) — a component library references `Rask` alone. **`var app = RaskApp.Create(args); app.Run<App>();` is a complete app with EVERY BATTERY ON** — referencing the package is what turns them on, there is nothing to opt into and no `AddRaskX` to write, so a `Program.cs` with no `Configure` block means "all of them" and only the EXCEPTIONS are written: `app.Configure(c => { c.Jobs.Off(); c.Mail.Configure(o => o.From = "…"); })`. A schedule goes straight on the battery (`c.Jobs.Run<Cleanup>().Every(1.Hour)`), the host is tuned the same way (`c.Live.Configure(o => …)`, `c.Server.Configure(o => …)` — calls add up), and an appsettings section is named by the SAME word as the code: `c.Logs` ↔ `Rask:Logs`, `c.Push` ↔ `Rask:Push`, `c.Ops` ↔ `Rask:Ops`, `c.Cultures` ↔ `Rask:Cultures` (a plain list: `"Cultures": ["en", "hu"]`). Turning one off takes its dependents with it (`c.Data.Off()` drops jobs/mail/cache/storage/outbox/snapshots/ops; `c.Cqrs.Off()` drops data; Logs owns its own file and is never dropped). Battery configuration is RECORDED AND REPLAYED onto the battery's own options instance, which is what lets `c.Mail.Configure(…)` sit beside `c.Jobs.Off()` while every options type stays `sealed`. **Nothing has to be turned off in order to configure it**: the automatic wiring runs LAST (from `Build`, after every `Configure` and after everything `Program.cs` registered) and every `AddRaskX` is idempotent — keeping the FIRST registration's options and, because `AddHostedService` uses `TryAddEnumerable`, exactly one worker — so a direct `app.Services.AddRaskMail<Ctx>(…)` simply wins. **There is no DbContext to write**: with none registered, `RaskApp` registers `IDbContextFactory<RaskAppDbContext>` — every `Aggregate<TId>` the app declares plus every battery's tables, migrations in the app's assembly — and binds the model surface and every DB-backed battery to it (inject `IDbContextFactory<RaskAppDbContext>` where code needs the context). **A `RaskApp` APPLIES ITS PENDING MIGRATIONS WHEN IT STARTS** (to RaskAppDbContext or the app's own registered context), in an IHostedLifecycleService.StartingAsync — before every battery worker and before Kestrel listens, so /health is never Healthy over an un-migrated database; `dotnet run` alone works on a fresh clone or deploy, no `rask db update`. No migrations yet → a warning naming `rask db add Init`, nothing created (never EnsureCreated); a model changed since the last migration → the start FAILS naming `rask db add <Name>`; concurrent instances rely on EF Core's migration lock. Opt out with `app.Configure(c => c.MigrateOnStart = false)` or `Rask:Database:MigrateOnStart=false` (code wins); a hand-wired host never migrates. An app that outgrows it registers `IDbContextFactory<TheirContext>` and the type is read off that registration rather than discovered or declared (this deleted an earlier source generator and its `[ModuleInitializer]` bridge entirely). `RaskApp` also owns the middleware order once instead of in four scaffolder emitters: forwarded headers (opt-in via `Rask:BehindProxy=true` — which `rask deploy --domain` sets because Caddy is in front — or `c.BehindProxy = true`; trusting them from an arbitrary client lets it forge its own IP), `/health` BEFORE `UseHttpsRedirection` (else `rask deploy`'s plain-HTTP probe 307s to a dead port), HSTS/exception handler outside Development, static assets (SKIPPED WITH A WARNING when the build produced no manifest, which is every non-Web-SDK host — it otherwise throws), `RunBeforeDatabaseOpens` (a Litestream restore that runs after the first query has already lost), `UseAuthentication`/`UseAuthorization` ONLY when a scheme is registered (it throws otherwise) and always before `MapRask` (RASK024), then `MapEndpoints` — a named seam, because an endpoint mapped after `MapRask`'s catch-all never runs AND never errors, it renders the app where the author expected JSON — then `MapRask<TApp>`. There is no `c.Wasm`: WebAssembly is a single-page app, served by `MapRaskSpa()` from `Rask.Spa.Hosting`, never a render mode. **A wasm-hosted server is `RaskApp.Create(args).Serve();`** — `Run<App>` WITHOUT a root: the same batteries and middleware, then `AddRaskCqrsServer`/`MapRaskCqrs` (Cqrs on), the mounted apps only (`/_rask` console, devtools — no host catch-all), storage + push routes, and `MapRaskSpa()` LAST as the fallback for every other path; the PWA is the client's (`host.UsePwa`), so `Serve` maps no server-side `rask-sw.js`. `Rask.Server` carries `Rask.Cqrs.Server` and `Rask.Spa.Hosting` for it. `c.Cultures` names the languages; **`AddRask` is called from `Build`, not `Create`**, because its options register with `TryAddSingleton` so the first call wins — calling it eagerly would freeze the culture list before `Configure` ran and ship an app with no languages while `Program.cs` listed some. **Every battery reads its own `Rask:<Area>` section of appsettings.json** (docs/configuration.md), and the settings a battery cannot boot without get DEVELOPMENT DEFAULTS, added as the LOWEST-precedence configuration source so appsettings.json, the environment and every `Configure` callback still win: `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App=Data Source=app.db`, `Rask:ConnectionStrings:Logs=Data Source=logs.db`, `Rask:Sqlite:StrictTables=true`, `Rask:Mail:From=no-reply@example.com` (IANA-reserved, so an app that never sets it cannot send as a real domain), `Rask:Mail:PickupDirectory=mail-pickup`, `Rask:Snapshots:DestinationDirectory=snapshots`; `RaskAppOptions.ConnectionString` set in code beats configuration. Consequence of on-by-default: a running app writes `app.db`, `logs.db`, `mail-pickup/` and `snapshots/` beside itself (gitignored by `rask new`). A battery the app does without is switched off in code (`c.Jobs.Off()`); its package stays referenced, and a DB-backed battery keeps its table mapped so switching it back on is not a destructive migration. `Rask:Database:Provider` (sqlite default | postgres | sqlserver) picks the app database at `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`: `RaskApp` reads it at registration, and an app-owned context uses `.UseRaskDatabase(sp)` (one opening another provider fails at start). On postgres/sqlserver there is NO app.db fallback (a missing App string throws naming the key), the durable log goes to the app database (`RaskAppDbContext` maps `RaskLog` only there), default Snapshots is skipped, and configured Snapshots or a Litestream ReplicaUrl REFUSE the start.
- [Tutorial: zero to deploy](docs/tutorial/00-overview.md): a step-by-step build of a "Shop" app that adds every OPF pillar in order — scaffold (`rask new`), first DB-backed feature (the chapter writes the aggregate and its pages as code — nothing to register, `RaskAppDbContext` maps it — then `rask db add/update`), auth (`[Authorize]` + the `Authorize` component), background jobs (`IJob` + a handler + `Jobs.Enqueue`; a schedule is `app.Configure(c => c.Jobs.Run<T>().Every(…))`), transactional email (a body component + `Mail.Send`), cache (`Cache.Remember(key, load).For(…)`), domain events/outbox (an `IEvent` + an `IDurableHandler<T>`), production SQLite (the WAL pragmas, snapshots, Litestream on `Rask:Litestream:ReplicaUrl`), Web Push (`Push.Subscribe` from a component, `await Push.Send(…).To(order.CustomerId)` from the outbox handler, `Push.Fake()` in a test), and `rask deploy --host --domain` to one box. 11 chapters under docs/tutorial/, each the code to write + a verify step; ch1 scaffolds with a plain `rask new Shop` (every battery is on by default, accounts included) so every later chapter teaches what a pillar is FOR rather than how to wire it, ch10 = an /ops page over every pillar's table (then points at the built-in `Rask.Dashboard` that ships the finished version), ch11 = deploy. You build the app as you go; there is no committed copy to read ahead in.
- [The `rask` CLI](docs/cli.md): the optional `Rask.Cli` .NET tool (`curl -sSL https://rask.sh/rask.sh | sh` installs it together with the .NET SDK, dotnet-ef, the wasm-tools workload and Node, all under $HOME with no sudo — `rask.ps1` is the Windows twin, `dotnet tool install -g Rask.Cli` the SDK-already-present path, and docs/installation.md the reference) — a thin wrapper over the SDK with two package references: SQLite (for `rask db backup`, which needs the Online Backup API to copy a live WAL database without tearing it) and Spectre.Console (the whole terminal surface — help pages, `deploy status`/`doctor` tables, spinners, and the `rask new` wizard). Piped output carries no escape codes and is never reflowed, and spinners write nothing at all off a terminal, so `rask doctor | grep` and CI logs read exactly as before; `NO_COLOR` strips every escape while keeping the cursor control the prompts need. **`rask` with no arguments opens the new-project wizard on a terminal** (piped, it still prints the command list): a name and an arrow-key project type, nothing else — filling gaps rather than re-asking, so anything already on the command line is kept and its question skipped. **BATTERIES ARE INCLUDED**: `rask new <name> [--template server|wasm|wasm-hosted|react] [--islands <runtime>…] [--no-pwa] [--no-cqrs] [--no-data] [--no-jobs] [--no-mail] [--no-cache] [--no-storage] [--no-push] [--no-snapshots] [--no-logs] [--no-ops] [--no-docker] [--no-tests] [--no-git] [--no-restore] [--output] [--dry-run [--json]]` turns on EVERY battery the chosen template supports and generates the project directly (the CLI owns all scaffolding — no `dotnet new`, no separate templates package); server is the default template. **A new `server` or `wasm` app has a test project**: `<Name>.Tests/` (referencing the app, `Rask.Testing` and xUnit v3, listed in `<Name>.slnx`) with one passing test, `Home_page_greets_the_visitor` — a `RaskMarkup`-derived class rendering `Page.Render(() => HomePage)` — so `dotnet test` is green from the first commit; the app's csproj keeps the folder out of its globs (`DefaultItemExcludes` + `RaskScopedSourceExclude`), the wasm one compiles the app's sources a second time since a test cannot reference a browser app, and `--no-tests` leaves it out. Every scaffolded setting lives in appsettings.json under `Rask` (connection strings, `Sqlite:StrictTables`, `Litestream:ReplicaUrl` left `""`, `Mail:From`/`PickupDirectory`, `Snapshots`, `Push:Subject`, `Cultures`) and **the `server` template's Program.cs is ONE LINE — `RaskApp.Create(args).Run<App>();`** — with ONE host reference in the csproj (`Rask.Server`, which carries every battery, plus the dev-only `Rask.DevTools`) and NO `AppDbContext`: `RaskAppDbContext` (namespace `Rask`) maps every `Aggregate<TId>` plus every battery's tables, and code that needs the context injects `IDbContextFactory<RaskAppDbContext>`. `RaskApp` gates Litestream on `Rask:Litestream:ReplicaUrl` and the Web Push sender on `Rask:Push:VapidKeys:PublicKey`/`PrivateKey` (`rask new` mints a development pair into the gitignored appsettings.Development.json). The default set is literally `template.SupportedFlags` intersected with the battery list, so nobody maintains a per-template default list. **`OptInFlags` is gone** (#854): localization was its only member and it stopped being a flag at all — languages are configured in appsettings.json (`Rask:Cultures`, the first entry the default; a `configureCulture` callback on AddRask appends to that list), never on the command line, because a flag would only restate at scaffold time what the file goes on being the truth about. A server app starts with `"Cultures": [ "en" ]` and adding another is an entry there; a browser-WASM app registers none, since a language in the browser means shipping ICU (~1 MB, +32% on the showcase) and <RaskGlobalization> is an MSBuild property Program.cs cannot reach — it is scaffolded COMMENTED OUT with the reason beside it. `--culture` and `--no-localization` are REFUSED by name, not ignored: --culture took a value, so swallowing it would scaffold English while the command line said Hungarian. **The wizard asks only a name and a project type** — where the UI runs is the project type (`server`, `wasm`, `wasm-hosted`), batteries are included rather than offered as a checklist, and dropping one is `--no-<battery>` on the command line. `--auth` is GONE and refused by name: accounts are a battery like the rest, on by default, and `app.Configure(c => c.Auth.Off())` is how an app declines. `--template wasm-hosted` writes a WebAssembly app into one project on an ASP.NET host: `Client/` holds the browser app (its own `Client/Program.cs` entry point, `App`, pages, `Client/wwwroot/index.html`), `Shared/` holds what both halves compile (message records), and everything else is server-only (handlers, the database). The server renders NO pages: its Program.cs is ONE LINE — `RaskApp.Create(args).Serve();` — which serves the client build beside the API/CQRS endpoints and the `/_rask` dashboard (a hand-wired host writes `AddRaskSpaHost()`, `app.MapRaskSpa()` and `MapRaskServer<RaskDashboardShell>("/_rask/{**path}")` itself). The build generates the browser project into obj/rask-client from Client/ + Shared/ (switched on by the presence of Client/Program.cs, off with `<RaskClient>false</RaskClient>`; the server excludes Client/**); `dotnet publish` publishes it into wwwroot, and every other build (dotnet build/run, rask dev) BUILDS the client so that in Development MapRaskSpa serves its build output (a Client/ edit rebuilds and restarts; it is not hot-applied). Browser-only references are `RaskClientPackageReference` / `RaskClientUsing` / `RaskClientProjectReference`. Known gaps: Rask.Auth's sign-in pages are server-rendered, so the browser app has none; and Client/ files are compiled only by the generated project, which an IDE does not load. Every battery has a `--no-<battery>` to leave it out — on `server` it removes NO package but writes the off-switch into Program.cs (`var app = RaskApp.Create(args); app.Configure(c => c.Jobs.Off()); app.Run<App>();`, several as a `c => { c.Jobs.Off(); c.Mail.Off(); }` block) — and turning one off takes its dependents with it (`--no-data` also drops jobs/mail/cache/storage/outbox/snapshots/ops; `--no-cqrs` also drops data; `--no-pwa` also drops push; `--no-logs` drops nothing, since the log store owns its own file). **The positive flags are REMOVED, not kept as no-ops** — `--data`, `--jobs`, `--all-batteries` etc. fail with a message naming the `--no-` replacement, because an accepted-and-disregarded flag is this repo's most expensive bug class. `--no-<battery>` for something the template never had is a usage error naming what it does support. **`rask new` also CREATES AND APPLIES THE FIRST MIGRATION** (delegating to `rask db`, so it installs dotnet-ef and adds Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design exactly as `rask db add` would), because the DB-backed pillars are hosted services and one that cannot find its table STOPS THE HOST — without it the first `dotnet run` of every new project would exit rather than warn; `--no-restore` skips it and a failure is a warning plus the two manual commands, never a failed scaffold. The database (implies cqrs) is SQLite at `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App` — `Data Source=app.db` in the scaffolded appsettings.json, and `rask db` reads the same key (JSONC-aware) — opened with `UseRaskSqlite` (WAL/`busy_timeout`) because `Rask:Database:Provider` defaults to `sqlite`, so your first aggregate is immediately runnable with `rask db add`/`update`; the **batteries** are each ON inside `RaskApp` with no line in the app — jobs/mail/cache/storage/outbox (all need the database, so `--no-data` drops them), Web Push (needs the PWA, so `--no-pwa` drops it; a `PushSubscriber` table + `Push.Send(…)` + `/_rask/push/{key,subscribe,unsubscribe}`), snapshots (scheduled Online-Backup-API copies; continuous Litestream backup rides the database, config-gated on `Rask:Litestream:ReplicaUrl`, with `RaskLitestreamDownload=false` so builds stay offline), ops (the `/_rask` operator dashboard — needs the database; gated by a `RaskDashboardPolicies.Access` policy requiring the `admin` ROLE (RaskApp adds it unless the app names the policy itself) — not merely an authenticated user, which with open registration would let anybody who signs up read the operator console; on `wasm-hosted`, `Serve()` mounts it at `/_rask/{**path}` above the SPA fallback, so the dashboard is server-rendered while the client keeps every other route); no template wires its host by hand any more, and a host you wire yourself keeps the load-bearing order (`ApplyRaskConventions()` AFTER the entity configurations since it walks the model as it stands — the outbox no longer has to precede the DbContext factory, since that callback runs when the factory is first resolved and so sees every registration whenever it was made) and **`AddRaskData()` is written BARE**: the outbox and the data interceptor read the same raised events, and each handler chooses in memory (`IEventHandler<T>`) or durable (`IDurableHandler<T>`), so there is nothing to hand over and no order to get wrong; **`wasm-hosted` WIRES REMOTE DISPATCH, always** (`--no-cqrs` is refused there) — `Serve()` registers and maps the dispatch endpoints on the server (`AddRaskCqrsServer()` + `MapRaskCqrs()` by hand), Rask.Cqrs.Client as a BROWSER-ONLY reference (`RaskClientPackageReference`, so the client transport never reaches the process that answers its endpoints) registered with `host.Services.AddRaskCqrsClient()` in Client/Program.cs; message records go in Shared/ and handlers stay out of the download by living outside Client/ and Shared/. Without a DATABASE it sets `Rask:Cqrs:Server:RequireAuthenticatedUser=false` in appsettings.json with a comment saying why — accounts live in the database, so without one there is no authentication to require and the secure default left on would make every message answer 401; `--output` overrides the target directory; **every** template also writes a `.gitignore`, an `.editorconfig`, a `<Name>.slnx` and a `global.json` pinning the .NET 10 SDK band (`10.0.0` + `rollForward: latestFeature` — the band FLOOR, because a pin naming a real release resolves nothing while that band is still a release candidate, and `latestMajor` would keep selecting the preview SDK this exists to avoid), and initializes a git repository with one commit AFTER the first migration, so `Migrations/` is in it (`--no-git` opts out; skipped automatically inside an existing repo) — the things whose absence is paid for later by someone else. **Styling is not a decision: Tailwind is built in** — there is no flag, no package to add and no off switch. Every template scaffolds a `Styles/app.css` holding one `@import "tailwindcss"` (no config file, no content array, no PostCSS — v4 detects the sources itself, C# string literals included) and the host package compiles it at build time. There is no `Rask.Bootstrap` any more. `rask db <add|remove|list|update|drop|backup|restore> [<name|file>] [--project/-p] [--startup-project/-s] [--context/-c] [--output/-o] [--remote] [--host] [--app] [--yes/-y] [-- ef args]` wraps `dotnet ef` for the migration lifecycle (add/remove/list migrations, update/drop the database), resolving the project from the single .csproj at/above the CWD and installing `dotnet-ef` globally on first use if missing; `backup`/`restore` never touch EF — a file copy of a live SQLite database is NOT a backup (with WAL on, committed transactions sit in the -wal sidecar until a checkpoint, so the .db alone is torn or stale), so both go through SQLite: locally via Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's Online Backup API, remotely via `VACUUM INTO` inside a throwaway `alpine` container mounted on the app's `<slug>-data` volume, fetched with `docker cp` over the existing `docker -H ssh://` connection (nothing installed on the host; host/app default from `.rask/deploy.json`, `--host`/`--app` override, and the host string goes through the same SshTarget parser so a leading-`-` value can never reach ssh as an option). an app whose Rask.Storage files live on the disk provider gets them archived beside the copy (`<name>.files.tgz`, after the database, spool excluded) and put back by `restore` when that archive is beside the file named, unpacked before the database is touched, with any row whose bytes are missing named at the end; `restore` behaves like `drop` — prompts unless `--yes`, refuses when there is no terminal — and `--remote` STOPS the app first and starts it after, deleting the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars with the old file, because replacing a database under a live writer (or leaving a stale WAL beside it) yields a corrupted hybrid; `rask dev [--project] [--urls] [--launch-profile] [--open|--no-open] [--no-hot-reload] [--no-restart] [--once] [--no-banner] [--dry-run [--json]] [-- app args]` runs `dotnet watch run`, resolving the project itself (the `.Server` host in a client-plus-host solution), serving it on its own **`https://<name>.test`** name — real name, real HTTPS, no port, set up on first run (a local CA trusted once, a hosts entry, and on macOS a pf redirect from 443, since only macOS reserves ports below 1024) — and **OPENING that name in your browser without being asked**: `--open` stays opt-in for a plain localhost run, whose URL is only a guess out of a launch profile, while the `.test` name is one the command just configured and issued a certificate for; `--no-open` stops both, and a `launchSettings.json` profile with `"launchBrowser": true` keeps the browser instead (dotnet watch honours that itself and .NET 10 does not let you suppress it from the environment, so opening as well would mean two tabs every run — which is why every scaffolded template sets it `false`). That certificate covers `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` as well as the name and `*.<name>.test`, because Kestrel binds loopback and a bookmark, an IDE's run button or `--no-host` all reach the same app — covering the name alone turned each of them into a name-mismatch interstitial on a page that IS the app. It also sets `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development` when unset and the `HotReloadAutoRestart` MSBuild property so an edit hot reload cannot apply restarts instead of stalling on watch's interactive prompt (`--no-restart` to be asked); `--no-hot-reload` keeps watching and restarts on change (`--once` is a plain `dotnet run`). Component `Render()` bodies, scoped `.css`/`.ts`, `[Route]` templates, CQRS handlers and job/outbox registrations all hot-reload; adding a type or changing a signature is a rude edit that restarts. In Development the browser shows a brief "Hot reload applied" pill and a restart reloads the page in ~250ms, and a build that FAILS is reported as a build failure rather than as a lost connection — `rask dev` reads watch's output and serves the compiler errors from a loopback status endpoint it owns (stamped onto every page as `data-rask-dev-status`, so the browser can still ask after the app process is gone), which the client polls on a drop and paints in a corner panel instead of "Reconnecting…" over a "Retry now" that cannot work; the reconnect backoff keeps running underneath, so fixing the code brings the app back on its own. **F5 in VS Code debugs the dev loop**: every template with an ASP.NET host scaffolds `.vscode/` (launch/tasks/extensions, committed by the scaffold's `.gitignore`), whose build task passes `RaskDevSession=true` — the one MSBuild switch `rask dev` also passes, which each package expands (WASM build output, islands from Vite) — and whose launch runs the dll under the C# debugger with Just My Code on. Edits need a restart under the debugger (Ctrl+Shift+F5): the runtime refuses hot-reload updates while a debugger is attached and C# Dev Kit's debug hot reload reports itself unavailable for this launch, so `rask dev` stays the live-edit loop. Under F5 the app does what `rask dev` would have: starts its own islands dev server (ending one a hard stop orphaned), serves on `https://<name>.test` only if `rask dev` already set that name up (never prompting), and prints `Rask dev: open <url>` for VS Code to open; a throwing handler stops the debugger once on its throw line (Just My Code reports it user-unhandled) and a throwing async lifecycle hook does too through `Debugger.BreakForUserUnhandledException`, since a faulted task is otherwise invisible to it, and dev error panel stack frames link to `vscode://file`. **Browser-side code is debugged too**: the `wasm` template's `.vscode/` runs its dev server in the background and launches Chrome under VS Code's JavaScript debugger with an `inspectUri` through the WebAssembly debug proxy at `/_framework/debug`; `wasm-hosted` starts that browser session once the host is up, through the proxy `MapRaskSpa` maps in Development (BrowserDebugHost.dll, located by the client's build, loopback only); a Debug build emits inline source maps for scoped `.ts`, served as an index map at `/_rask/a/{hash}.js.map`, so breakpoints bind in `.cs` and `.ts` files; `rask deploy [--host user@host] [--domain app.example.com] [--port] [--app] [--project] [--dockerfile] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--env-file] [--health-path] [--no-health-check] [--github-actions] [--dry-run] [--setup-host|--no-setup-host] [--deploy-user <name>|--no-deploy-user] [--no-firewall] [--no-harden-ssh]` builds+runs the app on a single host over SSH (every *deploy* op is `docker -H ssh://host …` — no registry/local daemon; builds on the box), remembering host/domain in `.rask/deploy.json` (never secrets); `--domain` fronts it with a shared auto-HTTPS Caddy proxy (Let's Encrypt) and deploys are zero-downtime blue-green, gated on an HTTP health check (`GET /health` — scaffolded by `rask new`; `--health-path` overrides, `--no-health-check` skips) so a container that starts but fails its probe never takes traffic, with multiple apps sharing one box (routing regenerated from each container's `rask.*` labels), no `--domain` publishes `--port` (default 8080) for your own proxy. Every deploy mounts a per-app named Docker volume for the SQLite database (`-v <slug>-data:/data` + `Rask__ConnectionStrings__App=Data Source=/data/app.db` and `Rask__ConnectionStrings__Logs=Data Source=/data/logs.db` — upgrade the CLI and the packages together, since an older app reads the un-prefixed names and a newer one does not) so the DB survives container replacement across redeploys, and stops the retiring container gracefully (SIGTERM, `docker stop -t 20`) before removing it so its Litestream replicator flushes and SQLite checkpoints the WAL (a plain `rm -f`/SIGKILL would drop the last frames); the `rask new` Dockerfile prepares a writable `/data` owned by the non-root runtime user (`mkdir -p /data && chown $APP_UID`), which a custom Dockerfile must replicate. **Handed a bare VPS it sets the box up first** (the one non-docker remote path — installing Docker over `docker -H ssh://` is chicken-and-egg, so setup shells out to plain `ssh`): one read-only probe reports what the box has, then after showing the list and asking once (`--setup-host` skips the prompt, required when there's no terminal; `--no-setup-host` refuses to touch the host) it installs Docker from get.docker.com, creates a non-root `deploy` login with your `authorized_keys` + docker group + NOPASSWD sudo (`--deploy-user`/`--no-deploy-user`) and rewrites the remembered host to it, enables ufw (sshd's real ports read off the box + 80/443 or `--port`, default-deny inbound; `--no-firewall`) and puts Docker's published ports behind it — Docker's own iptables rules are reached through FORWARD and never meet ufw's INPUT rules, so a stock box serves every `-p` port to the internet while `ufw status` calls it denied; Rask writes a fenced block into `/etc/ufw/after.rules` (so it survives a reboot) that default-denies anything forwarded into a Docker bridge except the container port this deploy publishes, with `ufw route allow` as the way to open more, and hardens sshd via `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-rask.conf` (`--no-harden-ssh`). Idempotent — a ready box is left alone with no prompt. Safety: nothing that can revoke access runs until a *fresh* connection (`ControlPath=none`) proves the new login drives docker; root login is only disabled once a non-root one exists; firewall+hardening run behind a `systemd-run` rollback timer on the host that reverts both after ~5min unless disarmed, so a lockout heals even if the CLI dies; and anything unprovable is skipped loudly (no sshd port readable → no firewall). `--github-actions` writes `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (push to main → same `rask deploy`, `--no-setup-host` so CI never provisions) + prints the two `gh secret set` lines (`RASK_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`, `RASK_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS`); host/domain come from the committed `.rask/deploy.json`. `rask info` reports CLI/SDK/OS (`--json` for scripts); `rask doctor` runs every environment probe the other commands own — SDK, dotnet-ef, Docker, project/template/provider detection, and the `.rask/*.json` configs — read-only, warnings not failures, `--json` for CI; `rask --version`. Tailwind reaches EVERY template including browser-WASM (it ships inside the host packages, build-only — no runtime assembly — and on wasm the stylesheet belongs to the browser project, because Tailwind v4 detects sources relative to where it runs). Rask.Query rides along with the dispatcher rather than having a flag of its own (reference AND `AddRaskQuery()`), and stays its own package depending on BOTH Rask.Cqrs and Rask.Core because it is the composition of them — Rask.Cqrs.Server and Rask.Spa.Hosting reference no Rask.Core at all. `rask deploy --env "Rask:Litestream:ReplicaUrl=…"` takes the key as appsettings writes it — the colons become the `__` the environment needs.
- [Best practices](docs/best-practices.md): production patterns + common pitfalls across components, state, forms, data, security, accessibility, performance, testing (each links the deep dive).
- [Building components](docs/building-components.md): how markup is written — naming a component and chaining onto it; the properties a component demands BEFORE it exists (required ones are steps, in any order, and the component appears only once none are outstanding); bound (`Input.Bind(() => m.Name)`) versus controlled (`Input.Value(v)`) form controls, which are mutually exclusive by construction — both openings live on the chain's entry and nowhere else, so taking one hands back the control and the other is not a member of it; the steps that follow are not gated (`Validate` on a controlled control compiles and does nothing); type arguments always inferred from the opening step; and an event declared as a non-nullable `Callback<T>` (`public Callback<int> OnRate { get; set; }`) and fired with `await OnRate.Invoke(n)` — unset is a no-op and never a required step — whose chain step shares the property's name and takes a sync or an async handler. **Short forms every chain has:** a flag step needs no argument (`Ui.Button.Square().Disabled()` — `Disabled(false)` still turns it off); `Class` takes parts and joins them with one space, skipping null and blank ones (`Div.Class("p-4 rounded", wide ? "w-full" : null)`); and a handler that only forwards an event returns the call instead of awaiting it (`.OnClick(() => OnRate.Invoke(i))`).
- [Elements & the DSL](docs/elements.md): the render surface — the primitives (`Text` HTML-encodes, `Raw` is verbatim, `Doctype` — for documents you build by hand, since an app's own shell is the framework's) and the `[...]` collection expression for sibling fragments; a generator-emitted chain entry for every HTML and SVG element; the universal props on every tag (`Id`/`Class`/`Style`/`Title`/`Data`/`Role`/`TabIndex`/`Aria`, the rest of HTML's global attributes — `Lang`/`Dir`/`Hidden`/`Inert`/`Popover`/`ContentEditable`/`Spellcheck`/`Translate`/`Draggable` — and `Attributes`, the verbatim escape hatch for anything unnamed, in a fixed attribute render order); INLINE STYLE IS TYPED CSS — `Style` takes text or a `Css` value, which has a step for every CSS property two engines ship, generated from MDN's data: `Div.Style(Css.Position().Sticky.Top(0.Px).Width(50.Percent))`; a property's EMPTY call offers its keywords (`Css.Display().Grid`, `Css.Width().MinContent`), a typed value is taken as its type (`Css.Height(40.Px)`, `Css.Opacity(0.5)`, `Css.TransitionDuration(150.Milliseconds)`), any other CSS is text (`Css.Width("calc(100% - 2rem)")`, and `null` declares nothing); lengths are unit literals (`12.Px`, `1.5.Rem`, `2.Em`, `60.Ch`, `100.Vw`/`Vh`/`Dvw`/`Dvh`, `50.Percent`); KEYWORD ATTRIBUTES ARE ENUMS generated from the spec's keyword lists — `Img.Loading(Loading.Lazy)`, `Div.Dir(Dir.Rtl)`, `Div.Popover(Popover.Auto)`, `Input.Of<string>().InputMode(InputMode.Numeric)`, `A.ReferrerPolicy(ReferrerPolicy.NoReferrer)`, `Button.Type(ButtonType.Submit)`, `Th.Scope(ThScope.Col)` (a string there does not compile); named after the step, after the tag where one tag owns it or tags disagree (`ButtonType`, `ThScope`, `TrackKind`), after the IDL enum where the DOM has one (`ReferrerPolicy`); open sets stay strings (`Rel`, `Target`, `Autocomplete`, `Meta.Name`, `Ol.Type`, MIME types); SVG generated from MDN the same way — every SVG element that ships, as MDN's type with MDN's inheritance (`Circle` is an `SVGCircleElement : SVGGeometryElement : SVGGraphicsElement : SVGElement`), entries named after the tag and `Svg`-prefixed where HTML has the tag or the name clashes (`SvgA`, `SvgPath`, `SvgText`), presentation attributes (`Fill`, `Stroke`, …) on `SVGElement` (no `Raw()`); and the full HTML-element catalog by category.
- [Routing](docs/routing.md): `[Route]`, params, `Router`/`Outlet`, navigation. ONE generated `Routes` class per project, in its root namespace, so `Routes.HomePage()` works from any folder with no using; pages sharing a type name nest by the folder that differs (`Routes.Admin.HomePage()`, `Routes.Shop.HomePage()`), and a page named like such a folder is RASK097. NAVIGATING: nothing is injected — `Routes.UserPage(42).Go()`, `Go.To("/x")`, `.Replacing()` to replace the history entry, `Go.With("page","2")`/`Go.Without("page")`/`Go.Without()` for the current query, `Download.File(name, bytes|stream)` for a file; all from an event handler (or initial render). The old injected `Navigator` service is internal (MDN's `Navigator` global is Rask.Web's). A PAGE'S TITLE: a routed page declares `protected override string? PageTitle => _order is { } o ? $"Order {o.Number}" : null;` and its layout reads the injected `RouteState`'s `route.Title` — a breadcrumb (`route.Title is { } t ? Ui.BreadcrumbsItem[t] : null`) and its one `HeadAssets` line (`Title[route.Title is { } t ? $"{t} | Acme" : "Acme"]`; Rask writes no `<title>` itself). A page is still mounted where its layout places the `Outlet` (after the layout rendered, and not at all when the layout withholds it); when its title turns out to have changed, the components that read `route.Title` render once more BEFORE anything is sent, so the first HTML already carries the title and a navigation changes page, crumb and `<title>` in one frame — one more layout render when the title changes, none when it does not, and the page itself is not rendered again. It is re-read every render (a title from loaded data, a rename in place), `null` means no title, the deepest page declaring one wins (a leaf with none takes the nearest layout's), a title loaded after a real `await` is `null` for the one frame a live navigation shows the page's placeholder, and there is no service to write into and no event to subscribe to.
- [Lifecycle](docs/lifecycle.md): OnMount/OnUpdated/OnFirstRender/OnRendered/OnUnmount — five hooks, one per moment, each a `Task`.
- [Authentication](docs/authentication.md): **NO ASP.NET CORE IDENTITY — RASK.AUTH HAS ITS OWN ACCOUNTS.** **YOUR APP DECLARES THE USER; RASK SHIPS NONE.** `rask new` writes `Features/Shared/User.cs` — `public sealed class User : Authenticatable { DisplayName… }` — and a source generator finds the ONE `Rask.Auth.Authenticatable` subclass and emits a [ModuleInitializer] naming it to `Rask.Auth.AuthUser`, so `AddRaskAuth()` and `modelBuilder.AddRaskAuth()` take NO type argument (TWO = RASK074, auth unwired; NONE = no accounts). `Authenticatable : Aggregate<Guid>` carries Email (trimmed+lower-cased, unique), EmailConfirmedAt, PasswordChangedAt, Roles (IReadOnlyList<string>, JSON column; GrantRole/RevokeRole/IsInRole) and an INTERNAL PasswordHash that no serializer of public properties can carry — so User IS AN AGGREGATE ROOT: `User.Where(u => u.Id == id)`, `User.Update(id, u => u.GrantRole("editor"))`, a generated `UserModel` that NEVER has the credentials (the model generator stops at Authenticatable), Version, soft delete, domain events (UserRegistered, EmailConfirmed, PasswordReset, SignedIn, SignedOut). Other aggregates reference a user by `Guid` id. `IAuth.Register(email, password, (User u) => u.Rename(name), returnUrl)` sets the app's own columns in the same insert. **SESSION ROWS**: every sign-in starts a Rask-owned `Session : Aggregate<Guid>` (UserId, IpAddress, UserAgent, LastSeenAt, ExpiresAt sliding over ExpireTimeSpan=14d, Persistent) and the cookie carries only its `sid`; the cookie handler's events start the row on SignIn (every host signs in through HttpContext.SignInAsync — /api/auth and the Server redeem relay alike), end it on SignOut, and RESUME it on every request (claims rebuilt from the User, cached ≤30 s per process), so a role change applies without re-login. `IAuth.SignOutOtherDevices()` / `SignOutEverywhere()` (and POST /api/auth/logout-other-devices, /logout-everywhere) end rows; a password reset ends EVERY session of the account; a live Server page re-checks its session through `ISessionRevalidator` before a dispatch at most every 30 s, so an ended session signs the open page out on its next handler. Bearer JWTs carry `sid` and are rejected once the session ends. List devices with `Session.Where(s => s.UserId == me)` — Rask.Auth.Api declares Session/Passkey and builds with `<RaskReadFacesOnly>true</RaskReadFacesOnly>`, which emits the READ FACES ONLY: no form model, no `Create(model)` (nothing should mint a passkey from a form) and NO registry contribution, since the registry is applied by a [ModuleInitializer] and would map auth tables into every app — `c.Auth.Off()` included — and a second time for one calling AddRaskAuth; `ClaimsPrincipal.UserId()` → Guid? and `.SessionId()` → Guid?. Remember me reaches the Server relay (`IAuthSignIn.SignIn(principal, returnUrl, scheme, persistent)`). **PASSWORDS**: PBKDF2-SHA256 600k iterations by default (BCL), or `o.PasswordHashing = PasswordHashing.Bcrypt` (+ `BcryptWorkFactor`, default 12; BCrypt.Net-Next). EVERY format is read — Rask PBKDF2, bcrypt $2a$/$2b$/$2y$ (hashes from other web stacks import), ASP.NET Identity V3 — and a successful sign-in rehashes to the configured one; bcrypt refuses >72-byte passwords instead of truncating. **THROTTLE, NEVER LOCKOUT**: `SignInAttemptsPerMinute` (5) failures per address+client → `AuthError.TooManyAttempts` (HTTP 429; renamed from LockedOut); the owner on another client is unaffected; registration and reset requests throttled too; run UseForwardedHeaders behind a proxy. Reset/confirm links are STATELESS Data Protection tokens (expiry inside the payload, checked against TimeProvider) fingerprinted on the state they change (password hash / email+confirmation), so single-use and killed by any password change; `TokenLifetime` default 1 h. **PASSKEYS (WebAuthn) — ANOTHER WAY IN, NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR THE PASSWORD**: `o.Passkeys` ON by default; `IAuth.AddPasskey(name)` / `SignInWithPasskey(remember, returnUrl)` / `RemovePasskey(id)` on every host (TypeScript: `addPasskey`/`signInWithPasskey`/`removePasskey`/`passkeysSupported()` in the auth module) — CALL THEM FROM A CLICK HANDLER (browsers show the dialog only for a real gesture); a dismissed dialog answers `AuthError.PasskeyRejected`, never throws. Rask-owned `Passkey : Aggregate<Guid>` in table RaskAuthPasskey (UserId, UNIQUE CredentialId, COSE PublicKey, Algorithm, SignCount, Name, Transports, BackedUp, LastUsedAt), read like sessions — `Passkey.Where(p => p.UserId == me)` — events PasskeyAdded/PasskeyRemoved. **VERIFIED BY RASK ON THE BCL, NO FIDO LIBRARY**: System.Formats.Cbor + ECDsa/RSA, attestation "none", ES256(-7)/RS256(-257) ONLY. The challenge is a Data-Protection-sealed state (5 min, redeemable ONCE, so a captured ceremony cannot be replayed); the origin must be in `PasskeyOrigins` when it is configured (EXACT match); with none configured — development, or a socket handler that cannot see a request — the origin's HOST must equal the rpId or be a subdomain of it (WebAuthn's own rule, so a port never matters and rask.test.evil.com is still refused); the rpIdHash must match `PasskeyRelyingPartyId` (default the HOST of PublicOrigin — a BARE DOMAIN, no scheme and no port; **CHANGING IT INVALIDATES EVERY PASSKEY**, set it to the parent domain to share one across subdomains); UP **and** UV are both required (the device AND the biometric/PIN = two factors); a signature counter that fails to advance is refused as a CLONE, while 0/0 is accepted because a synced passkey keeps no counter. A passkey sign-in starts an ordinary Session row and appears on /devices; every failure is throttled per client and answers InvalidCredentials, exactly as a wrong password does. Endpoints: POST {prefix}/passkeys/register-options|register|login-options|login|remove behind the same X-Rask-Auth header. **PAGES ARE SCAFFOLDED, NOT SHIPPED**: `rask new` (server template, data on, not wasm) writes Features/Auth/{AuthPage, AuthMessages, LoginPage, RegisterPage, LogoutPage, ForgotPasswordPage, ResetPasswordPage, ConfirmEmailPage, DevicesPage}.cs — ordinary app components on IAuth, daisyUI classes compiled by the app's own Tailwind (LoginPage offers "Sign in with a passkey" when `IWebAuthn.IsSupported()` says so, DevicesPage lists/adds/removes passkeys); Rask.Auth no longer embeds a stylesheet or registers page routes. **TWO PACKAGES, ONE BATTERY**: `Rask.Auth.Api` = accounts, sessions, `/api/auth`, the cookie, NO `Rask.Core`, for hosts that render no components; `Rask.Auth` = that plus `IAuth` for components and component email bodies. Same `Rask.Auth` namespace and `AddRaskAuth`/`MapRaskAuth` either way — reference ONE (Rask.Auth contains Rask.Auth.Api). the wire contract (`AuthApi`, request/response records, `AuthResult`/`AuthError`) lives in `Rask.Wire`. **ON BY DEFAULT** — `app.Configure(c => c.Auth.Off())` declines. **THE FIRST ACCOUNT TO REGISTER BECOMES `admin`**, the rest `user`, `/_rask` gated on it; single winner via a constant-PK row (RaskAuthInstanceClaim, AdminUserId Guid); the FIRST registration alone needs the one-time token from the startup log (`o.RequireFirstRunToken = false` drops it). Confirmation and reset go out through the MAIL battery (IMail resolved at send time; no mail battery → told, not silently dropped). `RequireConfirmedEmail` OFF by default; confirmation always sent. **Set `PublicOrigin` (Rask:Auth:PublicOrigin) in production** — outside Development a link is NEVER built from the request (its Host header is attacker-chosen): unset, no confirm/reset email goes out and the log says why; `rask deploy --domain` sets it. A password reset removes EVERY passkey on the account, adding a passkey needs a confirmed address (else `AuthError.EmailNotConfirmed`), and with `RequireConfirmedEmail` on registering signs nobody in. No answer is a membership oracle (unknown address costs a hash, reset answers alike, 'confirm your email' only after the right password). Every `/api/auth` call needs the `X-Rask-Auth` header (CSRF defence over SameSite=Lax). The battery OWNS the cookie scheme (registers it whatever the app did, applies AuthOptions last). External providers (Keycloak/OIDC) compose as a CHALLENGE scheme beside the cookie. The `Authorize` component gates by role with `Authorize.Role("admin")` or `Authorize.Roles("admin", "editor")`.
- [Live pages](docs/render-modes.md): EVERY Rask.Server page is live — there are no render modes, no `[RenderMode]`, no static pages and no WebAssembly handover. The GET creates the session (a `503` when `MaxSessions` is full; one that never connects is released after `UnconnectedSessionGracePeriod`), renders, and answers `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private`. The initial GET waits for async data in waves up to `o.QuiescenceTimeout` (default 5 s, `Zero` disables; JS-blocked work and detached loops are not waited on; `Rask.Query` queries are); `IPageResponse.SetStatus` for a real 404; redirect on load via `Go.To` becomes a 302. TRANSPORT: WebSocket first, with an automatic, unconfigurable fallback to plain HTTP for networks that block sockets — `GET /_rask/stream/{session}` (Server-Sent Events, 15 s heartbeat) down, `POST /_rask/send/{session}` (a JSON array of frames, one POST in flight) up, `POST /_rask/leave/{session}` on pagehide; same protocol, session, limits and guards. A tab switches when the socket errors before open, is not open within 5 s, or dies within 5 s of opening three times running, and remembers HTTP in sessionStorage only once an HTTP stream actually opened. Multi-host: the stream and its POSTs need affinity. A WebAssembly app is a separate SPA served by `MapRaskSpa()`.
- [Subscriptions](docs/subscriptions.md): **FIRST, THE CRUD CASE NEEDS NO SUBSCRIPTION AT ALL** — a save already refreshes the SAVING session's screen for free (`IDataChanges`), and a query REFETCHES when ANYONE ELSE writes what it reads: no event type, no `ISubscription` record, no watch policy, and the query's own authorization already says who may see it. **DECLARED, NEVER AT THE CALL SITE** — `[Live(typeof(Order))] public sealed record GetOrders(int Page) : IQuery<...>;` and `Render` is untouched (`QueryClient.Query(new GetOrders(Page))`); it is the READ-SIDE MIRROR of `[Invalidates]`, needed for the same reason (a message query is keyed by ITSELF, so a write cannot know which messages read the table). A query keyed by the thing it reads — `QueryKey.For<Order>(…)`, a Rask.Data read face — needs NO attribute. The publishing half is one const on the entity, beside Writes/Stamps/Deletes/Checks/Scope: `public const Broadcasts Broadcast = Broadcasts.OnCommit;` (default `Never`; announced after commit, never on rollback; needs NO session, so a BACKGROUND JOB's write reaches open pages where `IDataChanges` cannot). One listener per session however many live queries; the change replayed at open is IGNORED, so a page load costs no second fetch. **PUBLISH WITH NOTHING INJECTED: `Dispatcher.Publish(new ReportReady(id), ct)`** — one line to announce something happened; `IDispatcher` is transient and reaches handlers through the provider that built it, so publishing from a singleton (a `BackgroundService`) otherwise meant opening a scope by hand. Same publish (subscribers first, then handlers); inside work in progress it uses that work's scope, outside any it opens one of its own, disposed once the handlers finish — `Dispatcher.Send`/`Query` likewise; `Notify` is GONE; injecting `IDispatcher` where one is to hand stays right. Subscriptions proper are for what is GENUINELY AN EVENT (chat, price tick, job progress, "your export is ready") where there is no query to refresh: tRPC-style subscriptions over CQRS — **`IBroadcast`/`Topic<T>` ARE GONE; AN EVENT IS THE MESSAGE.** `IDispatcher.Publish(event)` runs its `IEventHandler`s AND hands it to every open subscription, so a command handler, a job, a Rask.Data domain event (after commit) or an outbox relay all reach screens. In a component: `QueryClient.Subscribe<OrderPlaced>()` in `Render` → `Subscription<T>` with `Data` (latest), `Items` (with `.Keep(n)`, oldest first), `Status` Connecting/Live/Reconnecting/Ended/Error, `IsLoading`/`IsLive`/`IsReconnecting`/`IsEnded`/`IsError`, `Error`; each value re-renders; closes with the component that read it — no OnMount, no dispose. `.Into(query, (data, e) => …)` patches a query's cache (idempotent patches; refetched after a reconnect). Function stream: `QueryClient.Subscribe(input, (i, ct) => IAsyncEnumerable<T>)`. Outside a component: `dispatcher.Subscribe<T>(ct)` → `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`. **TO WATCH ONE THING, WRITE AN `ISubscription<T>` RECORD — the FOURTH message shape** (there is NO `[For<T>]` and NO `object key`): `record WatchOrder(Guid OrderId) : ISubscription<OrderShipped> { public bool Matches(OrderShipped e) => e.OrderId == OrderId; }`, then `QueryClient.Subscribe(new WatchOrder(Id))`, `field ??= QueryClient.Subscribe<OrderShipped>(() => Id is {} id ? new WatchOrder(id) : null)` (null waits), or `dispatcher.Subscribe(new WatchOrder(id), ct)`. `Matches` runs per published event on the PUBLISHER'S THREAD — no db, no await; the DB check belongs in the policy. Who may open it: `IWatchPolicy<WatchOrder>.CanWatch(WatchOrder, ct)` — generator-registered, asked ONCE at the open, in the subscriber's scope — **NO POLICY = NOBODY** (fails closed, `UnauthorizedAccessException` → Status Error). Records compare structurally, so building one per render costs nothing. Starts with the LAST matching value published (only for types someone subscribed to; ≤4096 kept), in order, 256-value buffer drop-oldest, reconnect with backoff 0.5–30 s. WASM client (`AddRaskCqrsClient`): subscriptions open ON THE SERVER — `GET /_rask/cqrs/request/events/{name}?m={json}` (the record travels as a query's message does), server-sent events (`ready` event, 15 s keep-alive, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`), mapped by `MapRaskCqrs()`; closed unless opened: an `ISubscription<T>` record → its policy; an event watched BY TYPE → the RECORD must carry `[Authorize]`/`[AllowAnonymous]`, else 404. IN-MEMORY, ONE PROCESS (nothing to configure, and no backplane: a process hears what it published; another instance's pages catch up on their next refetch). Knobs, all from `Rask:Cqrs` (config first, code wins): ReplayCapacity 4096, SubscriptionBuffer 256, SubscriptionReconnectDelay 00:00:00.500, SubscriptionReconnectCeiling 00:00:30; the server stream's keep-alive is `Rask:Cqrs:Server:EventKeepAlive` (15 s).
- [Composition](docs/composition.md): the three component tiers (static method vs stateless vs stateful component), children, context (provide/consume), callbacks, toast messages (`Toast.Success("Saved")`, nothing injected — scoped-per-session, consumed-once transient messages that survive a client-side navigation; drained by a headless `ToastOutlet`, which a toast outlet of your own renders), every element event GENERATED FROM MDN (MDN's `GlobalEventHandlers`, one `OnX` per event named as MDN names it — `OnDblClick`, not OnDoubleClick — carrying MDN's event type with its inheritance: `OnClick(e => e.ShiftKey)` gets a `PointerEvent : MouseEvent`, `OnKeyDown` a `KeyboardEvent` (`Key`, `CtrlKey`) whose values are the generated `Keys`/`Codes` constants from UI Events (`e.Key is Keys.Escape`, `case Keys.ArrowDown:`, `e.Code is Codes.KeyQ`; a printable key reports its character, which no constant names), `OnToggle` a `ToggleEvent` (`NewState == "open"`); every event also takes `() => …`, sync or async; scroll and media state are the target's: `e.Target!.ScrollTop`, `e.Target!.CurrentTime`; there are NO `*EventArgs` types), headless primitives (`Virtualize.Items<T>`, the one method-call entry point on the surface because its `T` comes from the render delegate rather than an opening chain step), drag-and-drop, and hosting a component the app built itself (a runtime-chosen type, a plugin, code compiled in the browser) by putting the instance in the tree like any other child — the render walk notices an instance nothing registered and registers it under the component whose subtree it sits in, so it gets the whole lifecycle (`OnMount`/`OnUpdated`/`OnFirstRender`/`OnRendered`/`OnUnmount`) and a handle to re-render through, with no wrapper to remember.
- [Forms](docs/forms.md): binding, validation written INLINE beside the field — `Input.Bind(() => m.Email).Validate(v => v.Contains('@') ? [] : ["Email looks wrong."])`, `Form.Model(m).Validate(m => …)` for a rule across fields (runs on submit, shows in `Validation.Summary`), either one sync or `async` (a field's async rule runs on every change and the latest value wins — the next change cancels the check in flight through `Current.Cancellation`; an expensive check belongs in the form-level rule, which runs once on submit), a second `.Validate(b)` ADDS a rule instead of replacing the first (they run in the order written and `b` is not asked about a value `a` rejected), a text field binds LIVE on every keystroke unless it says `.Blur()` (bind + validate on leaving the field) or `.Debounce(300.Milliseconds)` (once typing pauses; the pause is counted in the browser, so nothing is sent before it, and Enter, a button, a handled key or leaving the field send the typed value first) — `Ui.Input.Bind(() => m.Name).Debounce(300.Milliseconds).Validate(DestinationName.Validate).Validate(NameIsFree)`, on `Input`/`Textarea`/`Ui.Input`/`Ui.Textarea` only — and a field's simple rules (required, length, format) kept in a VALUE OBJECT as `public static IEnumerable<string> Validate(string value)` and named from the field: `Ui.Input.Bind(() => m.Name).MaxLength(DestinationName.MaxLength).Validate(DestinationName.Validate)`; a rule only the STORE can check needs no try/catch: a submit handler that throws an exception implementing `IFieldFailures` (`Rask.Wire`: `Failures` of `new FieldFailure("That name is taken.", ["Name"])`, paths as the form's model names them — `Price.Amount`, `Lines[2].ValidFrom`; `Marked:` names fields that turn invalid with no text) gets each message under its bound field like a rule's, cleared from every field of the failure when one is edited, and is not a fault; for a model whose data layer REGISTERED rules there is NO step to write: `RaskValidation.RegisterFieldRules(typeof(M), property => rule)` makes a bound field run the rule its property's type carries FIRST (same timing as an inline `.Validate`, written steps run after it), and `RaskValidation.RegisterStoreRules(typeof(M), services => IStoreRules)` has the form ask the store (`Check(model, fieldPath, token)` → `FieldFailure`s) when a field is COMMITTED (change / `.Debounce` pause / `.Blur`) and on submit before the save — never per keystroke, never for a value a rule rejected — shown like a refused save; neither is switched off by `AutoValidate = false`; DataAnnotations and FluentValidation are also supported (next entry) — EditContext, `Form.Model(m).OnSubmit(Save).ConfirmLeave("Leave without saving?")[ … ]` (an unsaved-changes guard: asks before an in-app link, Back/Forward or closing the tab once anything was typed; clean again after an accepted submit; a `Go.To(…)` from the handler never asks; put `Ui.ConfirmLeave.Stay("No").Leave("Yes")` once in the layout and it asks in that `Ui.Modal` instead of `window.confirm`), building form components — implement `IFormControl<T>` (Rask.Core.Forms) on a generic component and the generator synthesizes its controlled + bound chains, or use the public binding API directly (`ExpressionAccessor`/`BindingHelpers`/`RegisterFieldValidator`). `IFormControl<T>` is the framework primitive; ready-made typed radio-group/checkbox-group/multi-select controls are yours to build (docs/building-form-controls.md walks one). A bound form control auto-wires `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` + a `role="alert"` error region when its field is invalid.
- [Validation](docs/validation.md): a form's rules are written inline with `.Validate(…)` (previous entry); a rule that must also hold on a dispatched request or a posted HTTP body lives on the type, and that path is ALSO SUPPORTED, built in and on — put `[Required]` on a model or write an `AbstractValidator<T>` and the rules run, in a `Form.Model(m)` as the user types (after the inline rules) and again on the server before a dispatched request reaches its handler. There is NO package for DataAnnotations (it lives in `Rask.Core`, which every host bundles) and NOTHING is declared in the form — the old `DataAnnotationsValidator` / `FluentValidationValidator` components are DELETED. FluentValidation stays the `Rask.Validation.FluentValidation` package, referenced by BOTH hosts (`Rask.Server` and `Rask.Wasm`); declaring an `AbstractValidator<T>` IS its registration, found at compile time by a generator in `Rask.Generators` that emits a `[ModuleInitializer]` — no assembly scan, so a WASM app keeps it and still publishes trimmed. A validator with constructor parameters is resolved from the render scope, so the uniqueness-check validator needs no wiring; one public constructor is the rule (RASKVAL002), one validator per model (RASKVAL001), and a `private` nested validator is skipped rather than emitted as inaccessible generated code. Both passes run with ATTRIBUTES FIRST — DataAnnotations is the sync `IFieldValidator` stage and the discovered validator the async `IAsyncFieldValidator` one, so `EditContext`'s existing order and per-field first-error-wins gating already produce that with nothing reordered. `HTMLFormElement<TModel>`'s type parameter is `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers(PublicProperties)]`-annotated AND the chain generator now propagates type-parameter annotations into the seed/stage/`Of` declarations it emits — without that the annotation is unsatisfiable at every call site (IL2091), since the chain is the only way to build a component. Off switch: `app.Configure(c => c.Validation.Off())`, `RaskValidation.AutoValidate = false` (works on any host, incl. WASM), or `Form.Model(m).AutoValidate(false)` for one form; the global off wins, and inline `.Validate(…)` rules keep running — the switch stops only the automatic validators. **Requests**: `AddRaskCqrs` registers a `ValidationBehavior` OUTERMOST, so an invalid request never reaches a transaction, a log line or the handler; every validator runs and failures are collected (deliberately NOT the form's first-error-wins — a caller fixing a request wants the whole list). Custom rules are `IRequestValidator<TRequest>`, async by construction. A failure is a `RaskValidationException`; over remote dispatch it is 400 `application/problem+json` with a stable `type` and an `errors` object — the ONE failure whose text crosses the wire, because a validation message is written for the caller while a handler exception names tables and credentials. The client parses `errors` (its `ReadProblem` skipped unknown members, so they would have been silently dropped) onto `RemoteDispatchException.Errors`, and validates BEFORE sending so an invalid command costs a message rather than a round trip — the server runs the same rules again and remains the authority. **HTTP endpoints** (#988): a controller action and a minimal API endpoint run the SAME two passes as a form — the bound body's DataAnnotations attributes, then the discovered `AbstractValidator<T>`, ASYNC rules included. Controllers get a global `IAsyncActionFilter` merging its findings with `ModelState` (MVC's own `ModelStateInvalidFilter` is suppressed, because it answers at order -2000 before any async rule could run and is a second failure shape for the same event); minimal APIs get an endpoint filter, attached to everything mapped through `app.MapEndpoints(e => ...)` and available as `.RequireRaskValidation()` elsewhere — ASP.NET has NO global endpoint filter, so a convention reaches only what is mapped into the group carrying it. Only what the CALLER sent is validated: `IServiceProviderIsService` plus a namespace test keeps a DbContext or an HttpContext from being walked. The rejection is the SAME 400 problem+json remote dispatch sends, under the same stable `type`, and `ApiException.Errors` carries the field map the way `RemoteDispatchException.Errors` does. .NET 10's `AddValidation()` is deliberately NOT switched on: its filter is OUTERMOST — outside every filter a group or route can add — so it short-circuits before the async pass runs, and it answers `application/json` carrying neither `status` nor `type`, with no supported hook to reshape it; running the attribute pass through `DataAnnotationsFieldValidator` gives one merged document instead of two rival ones. `c.Validation.Off()` turns the Rask pass off on both seams and leaves ASP.NET's own `ModelState` behaviour intact.
- [Building form controls](docs/building-form-controls.md): end-to-end guide to authoring a custom control with `IFormControl<T>` — the interface, a complete worked example, the default-method helpers, and the bound-vs-controlled / stateless-helper-vs-Component trade-offs.
- [HTTP & files](docs/http-and-files.md): data & file *transfer* — a DI'd `HttpClient` (constructor-injected, `BaseAddress` at the app origin; fetch in `OnMount` with cancel/retry/error handling), the typed file-picker input (`Input.Of<string>().Type(InputType.File).OnFiles(…)` + `IRaskFile` metadata; multipart on Server, JS chunked reads on WASM), and `Download.File` (event-handler-only; served from `/_rask/download/…` on Server, base64 to JS on WASM).
- [Data access](docs/data-access.md): EF Core + SQLite, IDbContextFactory, loading in the lifecycle, vertical slices, DDD value objects, decimal on SQLite (invariant collation).
- [SQLite production pragmas](docs/sqlite.md): the `Rask.SQLite` package (in `Rask.Server`, on by default) — applies a production SQLite pragma set (journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, cache_size=2000 pages, mmap_size=128MiB, journal_size_limit=64MiB; temp_store opt-in) to every connection. Raw ADO.NET: `services.AddRaskSqlite(configure?)` + inject `ISqlite` (connection string from `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`, pragmas from `Rask:Sqlite` then the callback; a missing connection string throws naming the key). Per-connection pragmas are re-applied on every pooled open (only journal_mode=WAL persists in the file); each option is overridable or nullable-to-skip via `SqlitePragmaOptions`. CONCURRENT WRITES: `factory.InImmediateTransaction(async (conn, ct) => …)` runs the work in a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction and acquires the write lock through the raw sqlite3 handle with the native busy handler off — the only wait is an `await Task.Delay` at a CONSTANT 1ms fair interval (not exponential backoff) that FREES the thread rather than blocking it inside native code; `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes the write lock up front, converting the otherwise UNRETRYABLE deferred read-then-write dead-lock into a plain waitable wait. The work delegate runs AT LEAST ONCE, not exactly once: SQLite may roll a transaction back itself when a contended COMMIT is answered with SQLITE_BUSY (sqlite3_get_autocommit is the only way to detect it), so the whole transaction is re-run from BEGIN — retrying the COMMIT alone would only meet the non-retryable "cannot commit - no transaction is active". Re-running is bounded by the same Timeout measured from entry, then surfaces SQLITE_ABORT_ROLLBACK. Keep the delegate re-runnable, put non-repeatable side effects outside it, and never issue COMMIT/ROLLBACK/END inside it (a transaction that ends during the delegate is reported, not retried, because kept-vs-discarded cannot be told apart). Also `connection.BeginImmediate()` (returns a SqliteTransaction; spells out at the call site what BeginTransaction() already does by default, so it cannot quietly become deferred; its wait blocks the thread inside Microsoft.Data.Sqlite) and `connection.InImmediateTransaction(retry, work)`. `SqliteBusyRetryOptions` (Timeout=5s, PollInterval=1ms) via `SqliteOptions.Retry` (`Rask:Sqlite:Retry`). Base package depends ONLY on Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and is reflection-free → works server-side and under trimming/AOT. NOT for the browser/WASM — but only because its PRAGMAS don't apply there (one connection, no concurrency to tame), not because SQLite can't run: it does. Browser companion `Rask.SQLite.Browser` (docs/sqlite.md#rasksqlitebrowser--keeping-a-browser-database): `services.AddRaskBrowserSqlite("app")` + `o.UseSqlite(BrowserSqlite.ConnectionString("app"))` gives a WASM app a real, reload-surviving SQLite database — restored from IndexedDB inside a hosted service's StartAsync (so anything registered after it opens a populated file), written back on SnapshotInterval (default 30s) and on pagehide via the Online Backup API, single-owner across tabs via a Web Lock. The native e_sqlite3 needs NO wiring: the pinned SQLitePCLRaw 3.x bundle resolves to a native package that ships runtimes/browser-wasm/e_sqlite3.a and adds the NativeFileReference itself when RuntimeIdentifier=browser-wasm. HARD CONSTRAINTS: publish WITHOUT -p:WasmBuildNative=false (no relink => no SQLite => boots fine then fails every DB call), and, in a trimmed publish, EF Core's three assemblies rooted (`TrimmerRootAssembly` Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore, .Relational, .Sqlite) with EF's own IL2026;IL2104 suppressed (unrooted, EF Core dies in the trimmer: MissingMethodException on EntryCurrentValueComparer<int>; Rask.Data, Rask.SQLite.EntityFrameworkCore and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite are trim-safe — IsTrimmable, analyzer-checked — and need nothing), plus NoWarn=WASM0001 for the varargs sqlite3_config natives. Durability window = the snapshot interval, NOT the pagehide flush (the browser does not wait for it). Non-owner tabs get their own EMPTY, unpersisted database — not a view of the owner's; promotion and write-proxying are not implemented. Use journal_mode=DELETE not WAL (one connection, and DELETE leaves the file consistent at rest, which is what makes its bytes shippable). For a JS-native client DB, the sqlite-wasm+OPFS stack in a Web Worker is still the only way to read/write OPFS pages directly. EF Core integration is a SEPARATE package `Rask.SQLite.EntityFrameworkCore`: `AddDbContextFactory<T>((sp, o) => o.UseRaskSqlite(sp, configure?))` (drop-in for UseSqlite; connection string from `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`, options from `Rask:Sqlite`; ConnectionOpened interceptor; pulls in Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite) — split out so the base stays EF-free for mobile/AOT. Setting `Retry.Enabled` (`Rask:Sqlite:Retry:Enabled`) registers a fair-interval `RaskSqliteExecutionStrategy` so SaveChanges/queries retry on SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED (turns busy_timeout=0 and lowers Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's command timeout so the async strategy owns the wait; each EF command still routes through the driver's synchronous busy-retry so a contended attempt can block ~1s before the strategy takes over — the raw InImmediateTransaction path has no such floor; EVERY transaction EF opens on SQLite is ALREADY BEGIN IMMEDIATE — the implicit SaveChanges one and Database.BeginTransaction[Async]() alike — because Microsoft.Data.Sqlite emits BEGIN IMMEDIATE for ADO.NET's default Serializable isolation and EF's Unspecified normalises to it; nothing needs wrapping, and the only deferred trapdoor is asking for it (IsolationLevel.ReadUncommitted, or the deferred:true overload). Pinned by RaskSqliteTransactionModeTests. The real EF read-then-write hazard is a LOST UPDATE — the read usually happens OUTSIDE any transaction, so the fix is a concurrency token, not a transaction mode). Backup companion `Rask.SQLite.Litestream` (docs/sqlite.md#continuous-backup-with-litestream): managed Litestream supervisor — `services.AddRaskSqliteLitestream(configure?)` reading `Rask:Litestream` (`ReplicaUrl`="s3://…"|"gcs://…"|"abs://…"|"file://…"; `ConfigPath`?; `RestoreOnStartup`=true; `ShutdownGracePeriod`=10s; `DatabasePath` defaults to the file behind `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`; env `Rask__Litestream__ReplicaUrl`) registers a hosted BackgroundService that runs `litestream replicate` for the process lifetime (graceful SIGINT flush on shutdown), plus `await app.Services.RestoreSqliteFromLitestream()` to restore from the replica before opening the DB (no-op if the file exists). Runs the litestream binary via CliWrap (set ExecutablePath if not on PATH). Single-writer only; DB on local disk not a network share; ideal for ephemeral containers / Azure App Service Linux (DB on local disk, replicate to abs://, single instance, Always On). Backup failures log Critical, never crash the app. Resolve the `LitestreamStatus` singleton to read replication liveness in code (`Current.IsReplicating`/`LastStartedAt`/`LastExitedAt`/`RestartCount`/`LastExitCode`/`LastError`) — a clean shutdown clears IsReplicating without counting a restart, so a climbing RestartCount means backups are flapping. RESTORABILITY IS A DIFFERENT FACT from liveness, and every field above describes only the local child process: a replica writing to the wrong prefix, credentials rotated to read-only, or a -config file naming a database nobody writes to any more all keep IsReplicating true until the restore. `o.Verification` (OFF by default) runs a real round trip on a schedule — upsert a sentinel row into `__rask_backup_probe` on the live DB (through Rask.SQLite's non-blocking busy-retry), wait `ReplicationGrace` (10s), `litestream restore` to a TEMP path (never beside the live DB; deleted on every path) and check the sentinel came back — publishing `status.Verification` (`Outcome`/`LastVerifiedAt`/`LastAttemptedAt`/`ReplicationLag`/`LastError`). Knobs: `Enabled=false`, `Interval=24h`, `VerifyOnStartup=false`, `ReplicationGrace=10s`, `PollInterval=15s`, `Timeout=2min`, `TempDirectory`, `BusyRetry`. THREE outcomes, not two: `Inconclusive` = the sentinel had not shipped yet (LAG, never page on it — alert on a `LastVerifiedAt` that stops moving), `Failed` = the restore failed or came back without the sentinel (THE alert), `Skipped` = no DatabasePath (config mode can manage several DBs, same choice Restore makes). EVERY PASS COSTS A RESTORE — a real download and real egress — which is why it is opt-in, daily by default, and must not be wired to a pollable health endpoint; `ISqliteBackupVerifier` is registered either way for on-demand passes. The verification restore passes `-o` (added in both URL and -config mode — config mode emitted none before, so it would have overwritten the live DB with a copy of itself) and DELIBERATELY OMITS `-if-replica-exists`, which would turn "no replica at all" into a silent pass. End-to-end proof against real MinIO in Docker: `scripts/verify-litestream-minio.sh`. Snapshot companion `Rask.SQLite.Snapshots` (docs/sqlite.md#scheduled-snapshots): scheduled CONSISTENT full-file backups via SQLite Online Backup API (`SqliteConnection.BackupDatabase`) — NO external binary, works on minimal/distroless + Alpine images. `services.AddRaskSqliteSnapshots(configure?)` reading `Rask:Snapshots` (`DestinationDirectory`; `Interval`=6h; `Retain`=7; `SnapshotOnStartup`=false; `BusyTimeout`=30s; `DatabasePath` defaults to the file behind `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`) runs a hosted BackgroundService (PeriodicTimer) that snapshots + prunes to newest N; or inject `ISqliteSnapshotter` for on-demand `Snapshot()`. Swap the `ISqliteSnapshotStore` (default DirectorySnapshotStore) for object storage; `store.List(ct)` reports what's held (name/size/timestamp, newest first, scoped to the store's search pattern) — a default interface impl returns empty, so a custom store must override it to be listable. Complements Litestream (streaming) or stands alone. Docker: mount a volume for DestinationDirectory or snapshots are lost on container removal; DB on local/named-volume not NFS/CIFS (WAL locking). FULL-TEXT SEARCH (EF Core, FTS5 — compiled into the SQLite 3.53.4 bundle on server AND browser-wasm): UseRaskSqlite implements Rask.Data's HasFullTextSearch/Search/FullText.Highlight/Snippet, and `.UseRaskFullTextSearch()` adds the same to a PLAIN UseSqlite — a browser app's over Rask.SQLite.Browser — without the pragmas — see docs/full-text-search.md. JSON PATH INDEXES: UseRaskSqlite also creates Rask.Data's `HasJsonIndex(o => o.Meta.Status)`, an expression index spelled exactly as EF writes the ToJson() filter, via migrations.
- [CQRS](docs/cqrs.md): the `Rask.Cqrs` package (in both hosts; it also stands alone) — a source-generated, reflection-free CQRS/mediator. IQuery<T>/ICommand/ICommand<T>/IEvent + their handlers, dispatched via a single IDispatcher — Query for a query, Send for a command (response type inferred either way) and Publish for events; register with AddRaskCqrs(). Handlers are wired by a Roslyn generator (no runtime reflection, no assembly scanning, [DynamicDependency]-preserved ctors) so it publishes clean under the WASM/AOT trimmer. Pipeline behaviors (IPipelineBehavior<TRequest,TResult>, registered via AddOpenBehavior / AddBehavior) are the decorator hook for logging/transactions/caching; ONE ships — a ValidationBehavior registered outermost by AddRaskCqrs, which rejects an invalid request with RaskValidationException before its handler runs (400 problem+json with an errors object over remote dispatch). Events fan out Sequential or WhenAll. Diagnostics RASK028 (ambiguous handler) / RASK029 (unregisterable handler). Depends only on Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions. **Remote dispatch** — the companion `Rask.Cqrs.Client` / `Rask.Cqrs.Server` packages let a WASM-hosted app reach its server through the SAME IDispatcher call it makes in-process: no HttpClient at the call site, no /api/* endpoints to write, and nothing on a message marks it remote (you write a record and a handler, and where the project sits decides where it runs).
