One line each — AddRaskCqrsClient() in the browser, AddRaskCqrsServer() + MapRaskCqrs() on the host — and neither half references the other, so a browser bundle cannot compile the endpoint code and the server never carries the browser transport; put the messages where both halves compile them — a Shared project, or one file Compile-linked into the host — and the handlers in the server only, which is what keeps a connection string or a pricing rule out of a download anybody can read. A client is a PURE client: every request message it dispatches travels, so a handler sitting in the client project is BYPASSED and the server answers 404 for a name it has no handler for — [LocalOnly] is the only way to keep a message in-process, and it is what a browser-local counter or offline queue needs; events are the deliberate exception, fanning out locally AND travelling, exactly once each. The wire is TWO endpoints, not one per message — GET and POST on /_rask/cqrs/request/{name}, the verb carrying what IQuery and ICommand already declare, so a command is 405 on GET and cannot be triggered by a URL, a prefetch or a link scanner (a query too long for a URL falls back to POST with an identical result); the literal route segments outrank the dashboard's /_rask catch-all and the SPA fallback, the name being a route segment gives logs/metrics/rate-limit partitions the message name for free, and MapRaskCqrs() returns the endpoint group for .RequireRateLimiting(...)/CORS/output caching. It fails closed: authenticated-by-default with [AllowAnonymous] the only way past, [Authorize] supplying a policy AND roles (both enforced), an anonymous caller getting the same answer for a real message name as for a typo so the endpoint cannot be walked to enumerate the app's messages, both verbs requiring the X-Rask-Cqrs header no cross-site markup can set, and handler exceptions becoming RFC 9457 problem+json with no exception text unless IncludeExceptionDetail is opted into. Failure to ARRIVE is the one thing remote dispatch adds — RemoteDispatchException, whose null StatusCode means the request never reached the server. [LocalOnly] on an INTERFACE covers a whole family, which matters because IJob derives from ICommand — without it every job payload would become an internet-reachable endpoint. Mark DOMAIN EVENTS [LocalOnly] too: events travel from a browser like any message, so an unmarked OrderPlaced could be forged by a signed-in user. Files go both directions with no adapter at the call site: a message declares an IRaskFile directly and it uploads as multipart, a query returning FileDownload streams back with an attachment disposition, a safe-leaf filename and nosniff (Download.File(download) saves it); bounded by MaxUploadBytes/MaxFileCount, with chunked upload above ChunkedUploadThreshold, shipped in #764 — the server echoes X-Rask-Upload-Offset and answers 409 with its own offset on a mismatch, which the client reads and resumes from (#907, bounded per file). The two directions are NOT symmetric in the browser and the docs say which is which (#894): fetch has no request streaming, so a single-shot multipart upload costs its own size in the tab and ChunkedUploadThreshold is what bounds that — load-bearing, not a tuning knob; the download direction is streamed because the client asks for ResponseHeadersRead AND the WASM SDK defaults WasmEnableStreamingResponse to true, which the browser-rung publish gate now asserts on the shipped boot module because the default is the SDK's rather than Rask's. The two halves are put in front of EACH OTHER in tests/Rask.Cqrs.Transport.Tests — the only compilation that references both — and over a real browser fetch (#896); note that AddRaskCqrsClient() installs its remote invokers into the PROCESS-WIDE CqrsRegistry the endpoint also dispatches through, so one process cannot host both halves. The wire codecs are source-generated Utf8JsonWriter/Utf8JsonReader code, not reflection, so remote dispatch publishes clean under the WASM/AOT trimmer; RASK053 reports a shape with no wire encoding and reaches no existing code, because codecs are generated only for a compilation referencing one of the two transport packages. `rask new --template wasm-hosted` scaffolds the whole arrangement in one project (its server's Program.cs is `RaskApp.Create(args).Serve();`): the message records live in `Shared/`, which both halves compile; the browser app in `Client/` registers `AddRaskCqrsClient()` in its own `Client/Program.cs`; and `RaskClientPackageReference` (a reference the browser app gets and the server does not) is what keeps the two transports apart. **`[Authorize]` ON A HANDLER HOLDS IN-PROCESS TOO**: `Dispatcher.Send` from a server page throws `ForbiddenException` (`IsAuthenticated` tells signed-out from not-permitted) before validation; jobs, durable handlers and hosted services run as the system. Static `Mail.Send`/`Jobs.Enqueue`/`Cache`/`Files`/`Dispatcher` work INSIDE a job, a durable handler and a custom mail sender, and `Current.UserId` there is the user who started the work.
- [Query](docs/query.md): the `Rask.Query` package (in both hosts) — TanStack Query's model in C# over the CQRS dispatcher: request dedup, staleness (StaleTime 0 / GcTime 5 min), background refetch, retry, polling, keep-previous-data and prefix invalidation, one cache per live session (scoped; never process-wide). The static `QueryClient` reaches the session's cache with nothing injected, and a query follows its inputs in all three places it can be declared: in `Render` from current values (`var o = QueryClient.Query(new GetOrders(Page))` — the same call returns the same query every render, keyed by call site and occurrence so loops and `if`s are safe), in a `field ??=` property or the constructor from a lambda (`QueryClient.Query(() => new GetOrders(Page))`, re-run at every read, first run at the first read; returning null pauses it), or injected `IQueryClient` where there is no component. THE MESSAGE IS THE KEY (records compare structurally); `QueryKey.For<Person>(parts)` keys a function query over data with a type but no message, and a function query is handed the input its key was built from. Commands: `[Invalidates(typeof(GetOrders))]` on the command record, `QueryClient.Send(cmd)` (throws) or a renderable `QueryClient.Command<T>()` whose `Send` never throws (Status Idle/Pending/Success/Error with IsIdle/IsPending/IsSuccess/IsError, Error, `Variables` = the command last sent, `Data` on a value-returning command, `Reset()`; `key:` per row in a loop). OPTIMISTIC UPDATES ARE PER SEND, aimed at the query handle: `ship.Send(new ShipOrder(id)).Optimistically(orders.Optimistic(list => [.. list.Where(o => o.Id != id)]))` — shown at once, snapshotted before the send, replaced by the refetch on success, restored in reverse on failure; works for function queries and function commands too; a function command is `QueryClient.Command(invalidates: typeof(Person))` sent with `Send(ct => Person.Create(...))`. There is no SetMessage and no OnUpdated re-pointing. A RASK.DATA WRITE INVALIDATES BY ITSELF: once a save commits (after an explicit transaction's commit; never on rollback), every query about the types it wrote — `QueryKey.For<Person>(…)`, i.e. what `Invalidate<Person>()` reaches; a child entity counts as its aggregate — refetches in the session that made it (never another session, nothing outside a session). A message query like GetPeople still needs `[Invalidates(typeof(GetPeople))]` on the command. The hook is Rask.Data's scoped `IDataChanges`, which the Rask host implements with the session's IQueryClient — and which, IN A WEBASSEMBLY APP, Rask.Data's browser build wires itself from `AddRaskData<AppDbContext>()` (plus `AddRaskQuery()`): no `Db.Configure`, no `Db.UseScope`, no IDataChanges of your own.
- [HTTP APIs](docs/api-endpoints.md): ordinary ASP.NET API controllers and minimal API endpoints, first-class. `Rask.Api` (AddRaskApi/MapRaskApi) maps controllers and — the actual defect — answers an UNMATCHED request under ApiOptions.Prefix (default /api) with an RFC 9457 404 instead of letting the catch-all render the app with a 200, which made a mistyped route fail as a JSON parse error far from its cause. Ordering is NOT the problem and never was: endpoint routing matches on precedence, so a route mapped after MapRask always ran. The guard is an ordinary endpoint at the default order, not a fallback (a fallback sits at int.MaxValue and loses to the catch-all). `Rask.Api.Client` generates one typed client per controller from the declaration itself — PostsController -> PostsClient, `await posts.Get(3)` with no URL, verb or response type restated — using the same reflection-free WireCodecEmitter as the CQRS wire; minimal APIs are read from the MapGet/MapPost invocations and grouped by route (/api/widgets -> WidgetsClient, .WithName overrides the derived method name), and TypedResults (Ok<T>, Results<Ok<T>, NotFound>, NoContent) carry the response type. Optional parameters keep the SERVER's default (emitting `= default` would send page=0 and override it), and the client sends Accept: application/json (a string action otherwise answers text/plain). RASK067-070 report what gets no client method and why. **Validated like everything else** (#988): `[Required]` and the discovered `AbstractValidator<T>` — async rules included — run on both a controller action and a minimal API, rejecting with the 400 documented at docs/validation.md#rejected, which `ApiException.Errors` surfaces. Choose this over CQRS when someone other than your own browser code has to call you.
- [Web APIs from MDN](docs/web-apis.md): the `Rask.Web` package — every web API the browser ships, generated from MDN's data into C#, imported for you in every Server and WASM app (the package adds `global using Rask.Web;` plus the alias `global using Types = Rask.Web.Types;`, so `private Types.IntersectionObserver? _io;`; `Rask.Web.Types` itself is never imported — its interfaces share the globals' names; a library referencing `Rask` alone gets neither; where a global is named like a Rask type, Rask's keeps the bare name by global alias — `EditContext`, `FormData`, `DataTransfer`, `EventTarget`, `Touch` are Rask's; MDN's are `Rask.Web.FormData`, `Types.EditContext`). MDN's globals by the window's own names (`Window`, `Navigator`, `Document`, `LocalStorage`, `Performance`, `Crypto`, …) and every interface they reach as a type in `Rask.Web.Types`; MDN's dictionaries and enums as records and enums. A chain is a path run in one round trip per `await` (`await Navigator.Clipboard.WriteText("hi")`, `await Window.MatchMedia(q).Matches`), an awaited object is kept as a disposable handle (`await using var q = await Window.MatchMedia(…)`), `Set{Name}` writes, `IsSupported` asks the browser. Bytes are `byte[]` both ways (`await Crypto.Subtle.Digest("SHA-256", bytes)`, `await Crypto.GetRandomValues(new byte[16])` answers with the filled array); MDN's `any` is your own type (`await channel.PostMessage(msg)` is `PostMessage<TMessage>`, `await response.Json<Order>()`, a MessageEvent's `e.Data<T>()`); a sequence of live objects is an array of kept objects, each disposed of on its own (`await Navigator.Usb.GetDevices()`, `Navigator.GetGamepads()` is `Gamepad?[]`); an argument MDN types as `object` takes the dictionary its page documents (`await Navigator.Permissions.Query(new() { Name = "geolocation" })`); a writable attribute holding an object takes one you kept, or null (`await Navigator.MediaSession.SetMetadata(await MediaMetadata.Create(new() { Title = "Song" }))`). A web API is generated once ONE engine ships it, so Chromium-only device APIs are there too (`Navigator.Usb`, `Navigator.Hid`, `Navigator.Bluetooth`, `Navigator.GetBattery()`, `Navigator.Connection`, `Navigator.Vibrate`, `EyeDropper`, `IdleDetector`), their doc comment opening with "Chromium only." — guard them with `IsSupported`; elements stay cross-engine. Opt-in build check: `<RaskBrowserTargets>safari >= 16; firefox >= 115</RaskBrowserTargets>` makes a call to a member MDN says one of those browsers lacks warning RASK098 (silent inside `if (await X.IsSupported)` or after `if (!await X.IsSupported) return;`; a bad entry is RASK099). Call from a handler or OnRendered; nothing touching DOM nodes is generated (use a typed element ref); `new X(…)` is `await X.Create(…)` (kept), statics are `X.Member(…)`; events are `On{Event}` subscriptions to dispose of (`await Window.MatchMedia(q).OnChange(e => …)`, payload = MDN's event type), a callback argument is a C# handler and an element argument your ElementRef (`await using var io = await IntersectionObserver.Create(entries => …); await io.Observe(_card);`, `await Navigator.Locks.Request("x", async lk => …)` holds the lock until the handler returns); what a callback hands you that is only data (IntersectionObserverEntry, ResizeObserverEntry, MutationRecord, Lock) is a record under MDN's name with MDN's nullability (`e.IsIntersecting` is a bool); either must belong to a component (it re-renders it), and disposing of an observer drops its handlers. Tests fake any web object with `Fake()` (`using var c = Navigator.Clipboard.Fake(); c.Returns(x => x.ReadText(), "hi"); c.Calls; c.Raise("change", e)`), scoped to the test's flow. HOSTS: what needs the user's click in progress (Navigator.Share, Notification.RequestPermission, MediaDevices.GetDisplayMedia, ScreenOrientation.Lock, PaymentRequest.Show; element refs' RequestFullscreen/RequestPointerLock/ShowPicker) and the per-frame families (WebGL + its OES_/EXT_/WEBGL_ extension objects, WebGPU, AudioWorklet) are generated into Rask.Wasm ONLY, as C# 14 extension members of Rask.Web's types (`WasmMembers`, `WasmElementRefMembers`) — the same call in a WASM app, a compile error in a server app. The globals are sealed classes (not static) so they can be extended. Doc comments say "Secure contexts only" from MDN's [SecureContext].
- [Browser APIs](docs/browser-apis.md): the map of the typed Web-API wrappers (6: 5 shared + 1 WASM-only — IIndexedDb, ISignaling, IViewTransitions, IWebAuthn, IWebRtc, and IBackgroundSync on WASM; everything else the browser ships is MDN's own surface in Rask.Web) — shared vs WASM-only, one-shot vs subscription, with the inject-from-ctor pattern and the push/[JSInvokable] mechanism. Every element component and every wrapper carries an XML `<summary>` that names its MDN reference page, and the generator forwards it (plus a `<param>` per documented property) onto the chain's entry and steps, so the documentation appears at the CALL SITE — hovering `Video` — not only on the type. BACKGROUND SYNC: `IBackgroundSync` (WASM only) wraps SyncManager + PeriodicSyncManager. The boundary is the whole design: the browser fires the sync even with the tab CLOSED, but the .NET runtime lives in the PAGE, not the service worker, so C# runs only while a client is open — Rask SW forwards the tag to every open client and the registration is otherwise consumed unseen. Hence: re-request tags at boot, keep the work in IIndexedDb/OPFS and let the sync be the NUDGE to drain it, and expect the win on a backgrounded tab rather than a closed one. Its SW handler deliberately stays out of rask-sw-shared.ts so the Server SW does not advertise a capability that cannot fire there. Periodic sync has no request API — check GetPeriodicPermission, do not ask. ANIMATION, SPEECH, FULLSCREEN, PICTURE-IN-PICTURE, WAKE LOCK, INSTALL PROMPT: no wrappers — Rask.Web (docs/web-apis.md): `await using var fade = await _box.Animate([new() { ["opacity"] = 0 }, new() { ["opacity"] = 1 }], 300); await fade.Finished;`, `await using var u = await SpeechSynthesisUtterance.Create("Hello"); await SpeechSynthesis.Speak(u);`, and on WASM `await _stage.RequestFullscreen()` / `await Document.ExitFullscreen()` and `await using var pip = await _video.RequestPictureInPicture()`; `await Document.FullscreenElement == _stage` says whether it is yours. Dictation: `_rec = await SpeechRecognition.Create(); await _rec.SetContinuous(true); await _rec.OnResult(e => { for (var i = e.ResultIndex; i < e.Results.Length; i++) if (e.Results[i].IsFinal) _text += e.Results[i][0].Transcript; }); await _rec.Start();` — a data-only list (SpeechRecognitionResultList) crosses as a record with an indexer, `Length` and `Items`. Wake lock: `_sentinel = await Navigator.WakeLock.Request(WakeLockType.Screen)` (both hosts), `await _sentinel.Release()` then dispose — disposing alone does NOT release. Install button: `Window.OnBeforeInstallPrompt(e => _prompt = e)`, then `(await _prompt.Prompt()).UserChoice == AppBannerPromptOutcome.Accepted` (WASM, in the click; `Trigger.Install` on Server). Three named runtime patches in src/Rask.Core/Resources/rask-web-patches.ts cover where a browser falls short: the webkitSpeechRecognition fallback (Chromium <139, Safari), the wake lock re-acquired when the page is visible again, and beforeinstallprompt kept from boot and replayed to later subscribers (Chromium's `{outcome}` normalised to MDN's `{userChoice}`). Reduced motion is the APP's call for its own animations. VIEW TRANSITIONS: `IViewTransitions` is the one wrapper an app could not have written itself — a same-document transition must WRAP the DOM mutation, and the mutation is the framework's morph, so enabling it routes the live runtime's own commit (diff and full-document, both hosts) through `document.startViewTransition`. Off by default, and off is byte-for-byte the previous timing; `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured in the runtime because the animation is the browser's own default with no stylesheet of ours to switch off. REALTIME: `IWebRtc` (peer connections + data channels, every host), a stream crosses as an `IJSObjectReference` (`Trigger.MediaCapture`'s `OnStream`, `IPeerConnection.AddStream`, `RtcHandlers.OnTrack`) and Rask.Web's `MediaStream.From(stream)` keeps it (`await _video.SetSrcObject(MediaStream.From(stream))`, `GetTracks()` → `Stop()`), and `ISignaling` + the opt-in standalone `Rask.Signaling` package on the server (`AddRaskSignaling()` + `MapRaskSignaling()`, which needs `UseWebSockets()` or every upgrade 400s). The relay authenticates by default, answers 403 to a WebSocket upgrade from another origin (`Rask:Signaling:AllowedOrigins` lists the app when the relay runs on a different host), mints peer ids server-side (never trusting the client's), delivers only within the sender's own room, and treats the payload as an opaque string end to end — it never parses an SDP or an ICE candidate.
- [JS interop](docs/js-interop.md): scoped CSS/TypeScript (a `.js` sibling is RASK055; tsgo compiles it, no npm) — the owning component calls each `export function` (or arrow in an `export const`)/`export class` of its `.ts` as a typed private method (`await Width(_box)`, `NewChart(el)`; callbacks as sync/async overloads, interfaces as nested records, a whole tuple `[x: number, y: string]` as `(double X, string Y)`, `number` is always `double`; an export with no C# shape is RASK094), element refs (typed to the MDN interface they carry its generated DOM members — `new ElementRef<HTMLDialogElement>()`, `await _dialog.ShowModal()`, `await _dialog.Open`, no IJSRuntime or Async suffix), IJSRuntime, typed browser APIs — shared (both transports) in Rask.Core.Browser (IIndexedDb/IWebAuthn/ISignaling/IWebRtc/IViewTransitions — speech recognition, the wake lock, live media streams, storage, cookies (`await Document.SetCookie("k=v; path=/")`, `await Document.Cookie`, or CookieStore.Get/Set/Delete in a secure context), clipboard, geolocation, matchMedia, screen, battery, network, vibration, performance, page visibility, crypto, permissions, BroadcastChannel, media session, Web Locks (`await Navigator.Locks.Request("sync", async lk => …)`, held until the handler returns), the storage estimate (Navigator.Storage.Estimate/Persist/Persisted), device orientation and motion (`await Window.OnDeviceOrientation(e => _angle = e.Alpha, every: 100.Milliseconds)`, throttled in the browser; iOS asks `DeviceOrientationEvent.RequestPermission()`, WASM), the camera and microphone (`await Navigator.MediaDevices.GetUserMedia(new() { Video = new() { Width = 640 } })`, then `await _video.SetSrcObject(stream)`), speech synthesis (SpeechSynthesis.Speak), animations (an element ref's Animate), the observers, gamepads (Navigator.GetGamepads), file pickers (Window.ShowOpenFilePicker, WASM), the origin private file system (Navigator.Storage.GetDirectory), notifications (Notification.Create), Web Push subscription (`await using var w = await Navigator.ServiceWorker.Ready; await w.PushManager.Subscribe(new() { UserVisibleOnly = true, ApplicationServerKey = bytes })`, then `ToJSON()`) and the app badge (Navigator.SetAppBadge) are MDN's own surface in Rask.Web (docs/web-apis.md), not wrappers — and the all-host headless Shareable — OS share sheet, attaches data-rask-share to your element and fires navigator.share in the click gesture so it works on Server too, plus the all-host Trigger.Gesture family — Trigger.Fullscreen/Trigger.ScreenOrientation/Trigger.EyeDropper/Trigger.Install/Trigger.MediaCapture/Trigger.PictureInPicture, headless data-rask-gesture components that run activation-gated WASM-only APIs inside the click gesture so they reach the Server host declaratively); WASM-only in Rask.Wasm.Browser (IBackgroundSync; the install event's `Prompt()`, code-driven share, screen capture (Navigator.MediaDevices.GetDisplayMedia), RequestFullscreen()/RequestPictureInPicture() on an element ref, orientation lock, EyeDropper, IdleDetector permission, WebUSB (Navigator.Usb), WebHID (Navigator.Hid), Web Serial (Navigator.Serial.RequestPort) and Web Bluetooth (Navigator.Bluetooth.RequestDevice) are Rask.Web members generated into Rask.Wasm only).
- [AOT compilation](docs/aot.md): opt-in full WASM AOT via `-p:RaskWasmAot=true` (default keeps the Mono interpreter; needs the wasm-tools workload). A reflection-free `TypedParserRegistry` seeds every BCL `IParsable` primitive and resolves route/query/form string values with no runtime generics; the RoutesGenerator auto-registers custom `IParsable` route/query param types; `RaskBinding.RegisterParsable<T>()` registers custom form-model value types; `InvokeAsync<T>` needs a `JsonSerializerContext` for custom T. Runtime builds under `IsAotCompatible` and `src/Rask.Site` under `EnableAotAnalyzer`, so every warnings-as-errors build enforces AOT-safety; the full AOT publish runs nightly. Mono WASM AOT is mixed-mode (interpreter stays), so the win is a clean bundle + faster binding, not crash-avoidance.
- [Prerendering](docs/prerendering.md): a standalone WASM app has no server, so every visitor AND every crawler gets the boot shell — a spinner and the word "Loading" — because the real markup does not exist until megabytes of runtime have downloaded. `<RaskPrerender>true</RaskPrerender>` renders each route to real HTML at PUBLISH (build is untouched) and writes it beside the bundle as a DIRECTORY per route (`/about` → `about/index.html`), so a static host serves it at the URL the app routes to with no rewrite rule. Pages go through the same root boundary and the same wave loop a server's first response uses, each in its own DI scope — so a page whose `OnMount` loads build-time data writes THE DATA, not its placeholder. A route is prerenderable when EVERY segment is a literal, decided on the parsed segments rather than by looking for a brace (the two agree today; only one keeps agreeing if the syntax grows a construct carrying no brace, or a literal containing one). **Skipped routes are reported by name, and reported even when the list is empty** — a parameterised route cannot be enumerated without the values and a catch-all is a 404 at best, so a pass that quietly covered a site's static half would read exactly like one that covered all of it. **A route that throws or does not settle is deliberately NOT written**: both still return perfectly ordinary HTML (an error document; the placeholder that was on screen when the budget ran out), and writing either publishes it under the route's own name with nothing saying so — a baked spinner is worse than no prerender because it LOOKS prerendered. The bundle still serves those routes at runtime, so it costs an optimisation rather than breaking the page; the usual cause is a page injecting a browser-only API. A pass that writes NO pages raises a build warning, asked of the OUTPUT rather than the exit code, because "it ran" and "it produced something" are different questions. HOW: a browser-wasm assembly cannot execute on the desktop, so the app's own sources compile a SECOND time for the app's own server target (net10.0) into a companion in `obj/rask-prerender/` carrying the app's own project and package references — including `Program.cs`, deliberately, because that is where services are registered and `WasmHostBuilder.Run` prerenders instead of booting when `RASK_PRERENDER_OUT` is set, so the app's REAL entry point drives the pass and there is no second place to keep registrations in sync. Engine is public for direct use: `RaskPrerender.PlanRoutes()` (`.Paths`/`.Skipped`) and `RaskPrerender.RenderDocument(app, services, budget)`, which takes no route on purpose — the caller holds the route table and seeds `RouteState.Path`. Check `Faulted`/`TimedOut` before writing. Each page is SPLICED into the boot shell (its import map, preload and scripts are kept), and the shell's `<head>` COMMENTS are dropped from the published page while staying in the source — `<script>`/`<style>` raw text, conditional comments and `<!--!`/`@license`/`@preserve` are kept (rask.sh saved 1,697 B raw / 769 B gzip). WASM only; per-page budget 30s.
- [PostgreSQL](docs/data.md#postgresql): the `Rask.Postgres` package (in `Rask.Server`; chosen with `Rask:Database:Provider`) — SQLite stays the default. `o.UseRaskPostgres(sp, configure?)` (connection string from `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`, options from `Rask:Postgres` then the callback) is a drop-in for `UseNpgsql` that puts production session timeouts into the connection string as STARTUP PARAMETERS (`Options=-c statement_timeout=…`) — they become the session DEFAULTS, so they survive the pool's DISCARD ALL, cost NO round trip per query (a SET per open would), and reach code that opens the DbConnection directly; a `-c` already in the connection string wins; PgBouncer transaction mode needs `options` in ignore_startup_parameters (or Zero timeouts + role settings): `PostgresOptions.StatementTimeout`=30s, `LockTimeout`=10s (VALIDATED to be below StatementTimeout — otherwise lock contention reports as a slow query), `IdleInTransactionSessionTimeout`=1m; TimeSpan.Zero leaves a setting to the server; values are rounded UP to whole ms (0 means no limit) and refused above int32 ms. `o.Retry` (`PostgresRetryOptions`: Enabled=true, MaxCount=6, MaxDelay=30s) drives Npgsql's own EnableRetryOnFailure — which, like every EF retrying strategy, REFUSES a transaction opened outside it: wrap hand-written BeginTransaction in CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync(...) or turn retry off. Rask's batteries (jobs/mail/outbox/cache leased claims, bulk insert) and multi-tenancy need nothing. FULL-TEXT SEARCH works here too: Rask.Data's HasFullTextSearch/Search/FullText.Highlight/Snippet become a STORED GENERATED tsvector column + GIN index (no triggers; PostgreSQL keeps it current), `@@ to_tsquery` ranked by ts_rank_cd, ts_headline highlights (docs/full-text-search.md#postgresql). HasJsonIndex and HasNonOverlappingRange are SQLite-only and refused at boot here. Litestream/snapshots do not apply (they copy a file). Real-server proof: tests/Rask.Providers.E2E.Tests via scripts/run-providers-local.sh (Docker).
- [SQL Server](docs/data.md#sql-server): the `Rask.SqlServer` package (in `Rask.Server`; chosen with `Rask:Database:Provider`). `o.UseRaskSqlServer(sp, configure?)` (connection string from `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`, options from `Rask:SqlServer` then the callback) is a drop-in for `UseSqlServer`: `SqlServerOptions.CommandTimeout`=30s (the ONLY ceiling — SQL Server has no server-side statement timeout; rounded UP to whole seconds because SqlClient reads 0 as wait-forever), `LockTimeout`=10s (validated below CommandTimeout; Zero = wait indefinitely; rounded UP because LOCK_TIMEOUT 0 means do-not-wait), `AbortOnError`=true (SET XACT_ABORT ON), `o.Retry` (Enabled/MaxCount=6/MaxDelay=30s → EnableRetryOnFailure). NOT like Postgres: SQL Server takes no session settings in the connection string, so XACT_ABORT+LOCK_TIMEOUT are ONE batch sent by a connection interceptor on EVERY EF open (SqlClient's sp_reset_connection clears them) — a round trip per open, and a DbConnection opened directly skips it (open through context.Database.OpenConnectionAsync). CACHE KEY: SQL Server's 900-byte index key = 450 nvarchar chars, Rask.Cache configures CacheEntry.Key at 512 → UseRaskSqlServer registers an IConventionSetPlugin (via its own options extension) whose finalizing convention caps THAT key at 450 — matched by type name "Rask.Caching.CacheEntry" (no Rask.Cache dependency; a test pins the name), no other entity resized, no SQLite migration; a key over the mapped length (450 SQL Server, 512 PostgreSQL) still cannot be stored and RaskDistributedCache now throws ArgumentException naming the limit instead of a truncation DbUpdateException (SQLite never enforces it). Settings live on the options extension, so calling UseRaskSqlServer twice keeps ONE interceptor and the LAST call's settings. Real-server E2E runs only on amd64 (the mssql image segfaults under emulation on Apple Silicon) or with RASK_MSSQL_TEST_DB.
- [Data layer](docs/data.md): the `Rask.Data` package — DECLARE AGGREGATES AND NOTHING ELSE. DDD BASES, BUILT IN: `Entity<TId>` (Id, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt) and `Aggregate<TId> : Entity<TId>` (+ Version concurrency token, Raise/DomainEvents/ClearDomainEvents). **FIVE CONSTS CHOOSE WHAT A TABLE CARRIES**, each read at COMPILE time (a wrong value is an error at the declaration; absent means the default, so an entity that says nothing is unchanged): `ModelWrites Writes` (default All) the form model and the writes taking one; `Timestamps Stamps` (All) CreatedAt/UpdatedAt; `Deletion Deletes` (**Hard** — CHANGED, soft delete is opt-in now) DeletedAt + the query filter, or `Deletion.None` = NO `Delete` generated at all (an invoice, a ledger entry, an order that is cancelled not deleted — calling it is a compile error); `Concurrency Checks` (Version) the concurrency token. **SOFT DELETE IS OFF BY DEFAULT**: a stamped row still occupies its UNIQUE constraints (delete a@b.com, re-register, constraint violation on a row nobody can see), "delete my account" must be able to mean delete, and Rask already ships snapshots+Litestream for recovery — so `Delete(id)` REMOVES the row unless the aggregate declares `public const Deletion Deletes = Deletion.Soft;`. **UPGRADING: add that const or the DeletedAt column is dropped and every previously soft-deleted row COMES BACK.** The version check deliberately did NOT move with it — a lost delete is visible, a lost update is not — so Checks stays on and is declined with `Concurrency.None`. Read at compile time and emitted as a registration, NEVER reflected over: a const is inlined at every use site and the field is trimmable, so a reflected read would fall back to the default in a trimmed publish. **MULTI-TENANCY, the fifth const**: `public const Tenancy Scope = Tenancy.PerTenant;` gives a table a TenantId column, a query filter nothing can compose away, and TenantId PREFIXED onto every index (otherwise `HasIndex(p => p.Sku).IsUnique()` silently means "no two tenants may ever use the same SKU"). A CHILD takes its root's answer and carries the column itself, because its own read face is queryable alone. The tenant is an OUTCOME OF AUTHENTICATION, not routing: it rides on the ClaimsPrincipal as the `rask:tenant` claim and the data layer reads it back, so a page filters with nothing passed to it; a restored session carries it too. `Tenant.Use(id)` / `Tenant.Across()` override, and an explicit scope always beats the principal. **THE CURRENT USER WITH NOTHING INJECTED IS `Current`**: `Current.UserId` / `Current.RequiredUserId` (Guid, from the NameIdentifier claim), `Current.Principal` (ClaimsPrincipal), `Current.Tenant` / `Current.RequiredTenant` — for a static `Product.Create(…)` factory or any code with no constructor to inject into. Set for a live session, every HTTP request (minimal API, controller, CQRS endpoint) and a background job, which records `UserId` at enqueue and runs as that user; `Current.UseUser(id)` scopes it by hand. An id, never the `User` row — load that yourself. Components still inject `IUserProvider` (it raises `Changed`). **A TENANT-SCOPED READ WITH NO TENANT THROWS** — returning nothing is indistinguishable from an empty database and returning everything is the leak. **`IgnoreQueryFilters()` DOES NOT CROSS TENANTS**: it means "include soft-deleted" and leaves the tenant filter standing (EF Core 10 named filters), so an existing call never quietly becomes a cross-tenant read. Writes stamp the tenant and REFUSE to move a row between tenants; it is never on the form model. TWO tables carry a tenant WITHOUT being partitioned: ACCOUNTS (an admin belongs to no tenant, and a partitioned row is refused without one — so Rask.Auth maps it itself and an address is unique WITHIN a tenant) and QUEUES (outbox/job/mail record the tenant at enqueue and the runner re-enters it; they must not be filtered or the drain would miss other tenants' work). The accounts index is over a TenantKey that folds a null tenant to Guid.Empty, NOT over the nullable tenant, because NULL in a unique index is not portable — SQLite and PostgreSQL treat two NULLs as distinct (any number of admins could share an address) while SQL Server treats them as equal. The context must call `modelBuilder.ApplyRaskConventions(this)`: a query filter lives in EF's CACHED model, so reading the tenant through a static is inlined as a literal and the first tenant's id would be pinned for everyone — passing the context makes EF lift it to a parameter. Verified on all three providers. Anything per-property or expression-shaped (column name, index, converter, length) stays in `static Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<T>)` — those consts are the whole family. `Entity<TId>` also has a `protected void Stamp(DateTime at)` for an entity whose package writes it and knows when; the auditing interceptor fills CreatedAt only when still unset, so a row in a package that does not own the DbContext cannot end up at 0001-01-01 (Rask.Storage found this the hard way: its CreatedAt is an orphan sweep cutoff AND the Last-Modified of every file response); ITimestamped/IVersioned/ISoftDeletable/IValueObject/[SkipModel] and the non-generic Model are GONE. **RASK'S OWN BATTERY TABLES ARE ENTITIES**: OutboxMessage, Job, QueuedMail, CacheEntry, StoredFile and RecurringJobState derive from `Entity<TId>` (NOT Aggregate — a soft-delete filter would hide rows from the drain queries and a second concurrency token would fight the ClaimToken lease) and get read faces under `<RaskReadFacesOnly>true</RaskReadFacesOnly>`, which emits the read faces and NOTHING else — no form surface, and no registry contribution, since the registry's [ModuleInitializer] would map those tables into every app referencing the package and a second time for one calling AddRaskX. Rask.Jobs/Mail/Cache/Storage therefore now depend on Rask.Data; StoredFile is a CLASS rather than a record (a record can only derive from a record); CacheEntry and RecurringJobState took a surrogate Id keeping their old key as a UNIQUE index (nothing looked either up by primary key, nothing holds a foreign key to them); Rask.Logging's table is deliberately unchanged because it is internal, so a read face would be too. **CHILDREN**: a collection of `Entity<TId>` kept in a field and handed out as a read-only view IS PART OF the aggregate — nothing configured (no HasMany, no FK, no key generation). **COLLECTIONS OF VALUES**: the same shape whose element is NOT an entity is ONE COLUMN, not a table — a PRIMITIVE COLLECTION for plain values (`IReadOnlyList<string> Tags`), a JSON column for value objects (`IReadOnlyList<Stop> Stops`) — carried on the form model AND the read face, and filtered in SQL (`Trip.Where(t => t.Stops.Any(s => s.City == "Vienna"))`). Both were broken before and neither failed loudly: a value-object collection made EF take the element for an entity and refuse the model with "requires a primary key", and a plain-value collection behind a read-only view was NOT MAPPED AT ALL (green build, no diagnostic, data gone on the next read). VALUES ARE REPLACED WHOLESALE, never reconciled — no id to match a posted row against — so what the form posts is what the aggregate holds, and an empty list clears it. Per provider: SQLite `json_each` both, PostgreSQL native `text[]` + `jsonb`, SQL Server `OPENJSON`; only PostgreSQL can index over EVERY element (GIN), SQLite can index a FIXED path via a generated column but has no multi-valued index, so a hot any-element filter on SQLite wants `Entity<TId>` children instead. `byte[]` stays one BLOB; a Dictionary or anything Rask has no column for is left to `Configure`, as is a collection `Configure` already mapped. LOADING ONE ROOT LOADS IT WHOLE (every id-based write, `Order.Model(id)` and `db.Orders.FindAsync(id)` include the children; a QUERY does NOT — `Order.Where(…)` leaves them empty, so listing roots stays cheap, and `.Include(o => o.Lines)` asks for them). A CHANGE TO ANY PART IS A CHANGE TO THE WHOLE: a child add/edit/remove stamps the root's UpdatedAt and bumps its Version (only those two columns are written, so a bump never reverts another writer), making the AGGREGATE the unit of concurrency. THE FORM MODEL CARRIES THEM: `OrderModel.Lines` is a `List<OrderLineModel>`, each child model has an `Id`, and `Update(id, model)` SYNCS — no Id = added, matching Id = updated, **a stored child in none of the posted rows is REMOVED** (an empty list deletes them all, so bind the WHOLE collection or use a domain method instead of a partial model); an Id matching nothing in that aggregate lands as a NEW child, so a posted id can never reach another aggregate's row. A child gets a table, timestamps, a model and a READ FACE of its own (`OrderLine.Where(…)`, with a navigation back to its root — the read side has no borders), but NO WRITES of its own, NO Version, NO soft delete. **THE WRITE-SIDE BORDER IS ID VISIBILITY: an aggregate may hold another aggregate's ID AND NOTHING ELSE.** A property whose type is another `Aggregate<TId>` — ONE of them or a COLLECTION of them — is **RASK087, an ERROR** (it was a collection-only warning before): hold `Guid CustomerId` and the generated read face gives you `OrderRead.Customer` back, inferred from that very id. A single reference becomes an id on THIS side, a collection an id on the OTHER. A child collection Rask cannot write is RASK088. Every `Entity<TId>` is mapped; an `Aggregate<TId>` is also queryable, writable and form-bound with NO DbContext class, NO DbSet property, NO IEntityTypeConfiguration, NO registration, and no IDbContextFactory injected to read a row. A source generator (ModelRegistryGenerator, in Rask.Batteries.Generators) finds every Entity<TId> at compile time and emits a ModuleInitializer contributing to `ModelRegistry`, which `RaskDbContext` replays in OnModelCreating — GENERATED CALLS, NEVER REFLECTION, so a trimmed publish cannot drop an entity and leave a missing table behind a green build. **QUERIES RETURN A GENERATED READ FACE, NOT THE AGGREGATE — `Product.Where(p => …)` is called on the aggregate TYPE, but `p` and the rows are `ProductRead`.** **TO CHANGE ONE: `var p = await Product.Find(id);` (`Product?` — the AGGREGATE whole with its children, untracked, through a FILTERED query by key, not EF Find, so a soft-deleted or other tenant's row is null) → call its domain methods → `await p.Save();`.** `Save()` (generated on every aggregate; `db:` only STAGES, the caller saves) INSERTS an aggregate with no row yet and otherwise writes over its row: only changed columns, children synced by id (new → insert, missing → delete), domain events raised, `Version` compared to the version READ (stale → DbUpdateConcurrencyException); a row soft-deleted since it was read → KeyNotFoundException. `Find`/`Save` exist under `Writes = ModelWrites.None` too — that const only drops the FORM surface. Every mapped entity (children included) gets a `{Entity}Read` type, queried OFF THE TYPE ITSELF — there is NO `Product.Read` any more (C# 14 static extension members): `Product.Where(…)/OrderBy/OrderByDescending/Include/Select/Skip/Take/IgnoreQueryFilters/AsSplitQuery/Search` return a deferred `ModelQuery<ProductRead>` that holds NO context open while composing (the terminal call — awaiting the query itself for the list, or First/Single/Count/LongCount/Any/AsAsyncEnumerable/Query — opens a context, runs, and disposes it). **THE READ FACE IS PRIMITIVES**: a value object FLATTENS to its columns (`Money Price` → `decimal PriceAmount`, `string PriceCurrency`, mapping to the unchanged `Price_Amount` column, so NO MIGRATION), an enum stays one column, computed and `[NotMapped]` members and every method are DROPPED. **NAVIGATIONS ARE INFERRED FROM THE IDS** — a `{X}Id` whose type is aggregate `X`'s key wires a navigation named after the PROPERTY (`CustomerId` → `Customer`, `ShippedByUserId` → `ShippedByUser?` by longest-suffix match); no match, a key-type mismatch or an ambiguous one wires nothing (the last two are RASK089) — so a cross-aggregate join is one expression on the read side while the write side stays id-only. The read faces live in their own `RaskReadDbContext` (two EF entity types cannot map one table in one context), so `db.Add(productRead)` DOES NOT COMPILE and there is nothing there to save. `Db.Configure(services)` points BOTH halves. **THERE IS NO `Read.FindAsync(id)` ON PURPOSE**: EF's `Find` bypasses query filters, so it would return a soft-deleted row that `Where` hides — by id is `Product.Where(p => p.Id == id).First()`. EVERY READ IS UNTRACKED, ALWAYS — there is no AsTracking/AsNoTracking: a Rask page outlives any safe DbContext, so nothing holds one between calls, and mutating a row you read saves NOTHING. A member declared on the model itself always wins over an extension member, so your own static `Read`/`Create` is untouched. `Product.AsQueryable()` (and `Product.Where(…).AsQueryable()`) is a STANDARD IQueryable<ProductRead> that holds NO context and opens one PER EXECUTION (a sync Count()/ToList() and an awaited ToListAsync() alike) — made for `Ui.DataGrid.Data(Product.AsQueryable()).RowKey(p => p.Id)`, which sorts and pages in SQL and is safe in a page field, and a grid spanning TWO aggregates is now possible because the face carries the navigation; EF-only operators (Include, IgnoreQueryFilters, AsSplitQuery) MUST go on the model query BEFORE .AsQueryable(), because EF silently ignores them on a non-EF provider. WRITES LIVE ON THE MODEL TYPE TOO: `Product.Create(model)` (key: new version-7 Guid, a Guid-backed strongly-typed id, or the store identity for an integer), `Product.Create(p => ...)` (no form — mirrors Update(id, p => ...), same key rules), `Product.Create(id, model)` and `Product.Create(id, p => ...)` (the only creates for a key nothing can produce; NOT generated for a store-generated integer key), `Product.Create(entity)` (an entity built by its own factory), `Product.Update(id, model)` (loads the row, writes the model onto it through generated [UnsafeAccessor]s — private setters fine, no reflection — saves ONLY changed columns, checks the model's Version, a null Version skips the check), `Product.Update(id, p => ...)` (no form; optional `version:`) and `Product.Delete(id)` (loads then removes — the row goes, or DeletedAt is stamped for an aggregate declaring `Deletes = Deletion.Soft`, and `Deletion.None` generates no Delete; optional `version:`). Every model-taking write has an optional `Action<TEntity>? apply` run AFTER the model's values (values the form does not carry: a timestamp, the current user) and **EVERY write has an optional `DbContext? db`, and `db:` STAGES RATHER THAN SAVES** (changed): given a context the write applies its change and RETURNS — the CALLER saves — so several writes on one context are ONE transaction with no `BeginTransactionAsync` to write (`await Order.Create(m, db: db); await Stock.Update(id, s => s.Reserve(n), db: db); await db.SaveChangesAsync();` = both rows or neither); omitted, the write opens a context from Db, saves and disposes, and IS its own transaction. A staged `Create` returns an entity not yet persisted (a Guid key is already set; a store-generated int key is 0 until the caller saves); the `Version` check still pins the original and is compared at the caller's save. A missing or soft-deleted row is KeyNotFoundException; a stale Version is DbUpdateConcurrencyException. AGGREGATES DECLARE NO CONSTRUCTOR: the implicit one serves EF, Create and the model's defaults, and domain creation goes in a static factory; one declaring a constructor with arguments gets no Create — RASK086 (warning); RASK081 is RETIRED. `Product.Model(id)` is the FORM LOOP's fill — the edit shape by id, null when no row has it — and `product.ToModel()` fills one from an aggregate already in hand. It is NOT a read-face query: the read face is flat primitives while the form model keeps value objects NESTED and children as child MODELS, so `Model` loads the aggregate whole and reuses the generated fill (one mapping, nothing to drift). It is a query, not EF `Find`, so a soft-deleted row does not open an edit form. There is NO ExecuteUpdateAsync/ExecuteDeleteAsync on the model query. A static Create/Update/Delete declared on the entity replaces the generated one at every call site; the generated one stays reachable as `ProductModelExtensions.Create(...)`. A GENERATED FORM MODEL STAYS: every namespace-level aggregate gets `{Aggregate}Model` (ProductModel) beside it, and FORMS ALWAYS BIND IT, NEVER THE AGGREGATE — a mutable `sealed partial` class with a settable, NULLABLE copy of every mapped property, `new ProductModel()` holding the aggregate's own defaults, the entity's DataAnnotations/ValidationAttributes copied (not [Key]/[ConcurrencyCheck]/[Timestamp]), `Version` carried, and NEVER the Id (overposting) nor CreatedAt/UpdatedAt/DeletedAt/DomainEvents/navigations/collections/computed properties; a value object becomes a nested `{ValueObject}Model?` (filled by new/ToModel; bind `() => _m.Price!.Amount`), and a ONE-VALUE value object (record Email(string Value)) is carried as its value. It is the MASS-ASSIGNMENT WHITELIST: bind it with Form.Model(model), then `Product.Create(model)` / `Product.Update(id, model)` — the id always comes from the caller (route), never the form — or send a command carrying it. SAVE RULE (form-first): a null CLEARS a property the aggregate declares nullable and LEAVES a non-nullable one unchanged; a nested value-object model merges over the current value object; a model save writes through the private setters and does NOT call domain methods (use the apply lambda or Update(id, p => ...) for those). There is NO [SkipModel]: every mapped property is on the model. **AN AGGREGATE CAN DECLINE THE FORM SURFACE**: `public const ModelWrites Writes = ModelWrites.None;` on the entity drops `{X}Model`, `Create(model)`, `Update(id, model)`, `Model(id)` and `ToModel()` — for a row a form has no business creating (a passkey minted by a WebAuthn ceremony, a session started by signing in). `[Flags] enum ModelWrites { None = 0, Create = 1, Update = 2, All = Create | Update }`; NO Delete member because Delete(id) never took a model; ABSENT const == All, so nothing existing changes. It reaches the FORM surface ONLY — the behaviour writes `Create(x => …)`, `Update(id, x => …)` and `Delete(id)` are ALWAYS generated, and so are the READ-FACE QUERIES (`X.Where(…)`), which is not negotiable since querying works through read models. A `const` rather than an attribute or a static property because C# refuses a non-constant initializer, so the generator can never quietly fail to read it and emit everything anyway. A CHILD takes its ROOT's answer (its model is an element of the root's list), so a child declaring its own Writes is RASK091 (warning) and is ignored. A hand-written non-partial `ProductModel` beside `Product` is RASK082 (error); a `partial` one merges in; a nested aggregate is RASK083 (warning, no model). CQRS codecs, API clients, island props, component props and validators all recognise the generated model although it is generated; on the wire its properties are camelCase. NO PUBLIC SETTERS: RASK084 is an ERROR (+ code fix to private) for a public `set`, a hand-written public `init` or a public non-readonly field on an aggregate, an entity (and the app's abstract bases between them) or a value object one of them holds (a positional record's parameters are exempt); RASK085 (warning + code fix) reports an entity exposing a mutable collection of other entities — expose `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` over `private readonly List<T> _items` and mutate through a method. EVERYTHING RICHER THAN THOSE WRITES IS PLAIN EF CORE — there is NO Db.Begin()/UnitOfWork/Db.Current/Db.HasCurrent/Db.CurrentUnitOfWork/Db.Set<T>()/Db.Entry()/Db.SaveChangesAsync(), NO Product.Add/AddRange/Update/UpdateRange/Remove/RemoveRange/Attach/Entry/Set: a behaviour method such as `order.Cancel()` is followed by `await order.Save()`, and multi-entity work injects the context and calls SaveChangesAsync. On a LIVE PAGE (it outlives a DI scope) inject `IDbContextFactory<RaskAppDbContext>` and create a context per operation; a CQRS HANDLER ALSO injects IDbContextFactory<T> and creates a context per `Handle`, because a command dispatched in-process from a live page resolves its handler from that page's SESSION scope (Dispatcher captures the session provider), so a scoped context injected into a handler would be shared across the whole session; only a plain ASP.NET endpoint may inject the scoped context. A form binds the generated `ProductModel` or a COMMAND (a class with settable props + DataAnnotations, validated by Form and again by the dispatcher's ValidationBehavior), and the handler calls `Product.Create`/`Update` or loads the entity, calls its method and SaveChangesAsync. `RaskAppDbContext` is `Rask.RaskAppDbContext` and declares NO DbSet properties, but **EVERY MAPPED ENTITY GETS A NAMED SET AS AN EXTENSION MEMBER ON `DbContext` ITSELF** — `db.Orders`, `db.OrderLines` (children too) — beside the `db.Set<Order>()` that still works, so an app bringing its OWN context gets them without being `partial`. The name follows ONE documented rule and nothing cleverer (`+s`; `+es` after s/x/z/ch/sh; consonant+`y` → `ies`), so `Person` → `db.Persons` and `Quiz` → `db.Quizes`; a name two entities want, or one `DbContext` already declares, is RASK090 (warning) and generates NEITHER accessor rather than guessing. `Db` has ONLY Configure(IServiceProvider) / Configure(IDbContextFactory<T>) / Configure(Func<DbContext>), UseScope(IServiceProvider), IsConfigured and Reset(); Db.Configure(IServiceProvider) is called by the host (RaskApp.Build after builder.Build()) so an app configures nothing. MAPPING RULES live in a plain `public static void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<T> builder)` ON THE MODEL — no attribute, no interface, no separate class — matched BY SIGNATURE and run LAST (after ApplyRaskConventions) so it can overrule the conventions; a near miss (instance method, private, wrong builder type) is RASK072 rather than silence. VALUE OBJECTS need NO MARKER — any class/record/struct an entity holds that is not an entity, a collection, abstract, generic or a System/Microsoft type — and map as EF COMPLEX TYPES (a one-value one the entity holds is ONE column named after the property — a CONVERTED SCALAR, so it takes `HasIndex(…).IsUnique("…")` and `Property(c => c.Email).HasMaxLength(…)`; on the aggregate a query compares the whole value, `c.Email == new Email("…")`, and cannot reach `.Value` — the read face has it as the primitive) (part of the row) rather than owned entities (a joined table with hidden identity), nested ones included — but a value object CONTAINING another needs a parameterless ctor + settable (private) properties, because EF cannot bind a nested complex type to a constructor parameter (a positional record is fine when it holds only scalars). STRONGLY-TYPED IDS need nothing declared: `Aggregate<ProductId>` where ProductId is a user-defined single-value type gets a generated ValueConverter registered ONCE PER TYPE in ConfigureConventions, so the key, foreign keys and nullable occurrences are all converted; one the generator cannot convert is RASK073. BATCH (on a context, db.Set<T>().Where(...)): EF Core's ExecuteUpdateAsync(s => s.SetProperty(...)) and ExecuteDeleteAsync() are set-based single statements that BYPASS THE INTERCEPTORS (no UpdatedAt, no Version bump, no domain events) — a batch SOFT delete is an ExecuteUpdateAsync of DeletedAt, because ExecuteDeleteAsync really deletes an aggregate's row. TESTING: behaviour that only changes the model needs no database at all (assert on DomainEvents); behaviour that reads one gets `await TestDatabase.Start(o => o.UseSqlite(...), timeProvider)` — builds the generated model, creates the schema, wires the auditing + soft-delete interceptors, resets Db on dispose, seed through database.Context, provider-agnostic so Rask.Data gains no provider dependency. OPTING OUT IS NOT DERIVING FROM Entity<TId>: a class that does not is an ordinary EF Core entity used exactly as before, and registering an IDbContextFactory<YourContext> binds the model surface and every battery to your context so RaskAppDbContext (the generated model + every battery's tables, in `Rask.Server`) is never constructed. The framework columns are REAL BASE-CLASS PROPERTIES with private setters (written through the change tracker), so they are readable, sortable and filterable with no declaration. Three ISaveChangesInterceptors: AuditingInterceptor (stamps timestamps, bumps Version), SoftDeleteInterceptor (for an aggregate declaring `Deletes = Deletion.Soft` only: rewrites a Deleted entry to Modified + sets DeletedAt so db.Remove soft-deletes; global query filter DeletedAt==null hides it — use IgnoreQueryFilters() to see/restore), DomainEventInterceptor (after commit, publishes each entity's events via Rask.Cqrs IDispatcher.Publish in a fresh scope, so every IEventHandler<T> runs IN MEMORY, then clears them; an IDurableHandler<T> is NOT run here — the outbox stored its row in the save's own transaction; events are cleared only after the commit, so the two interceptors work in either order; no AddRaskCqrs = nothing published). `RaskApp` wires all of this; a hand-wired host writes services.AddRaskData() (registers the interceptors + a TimeProvider) + o.AddInterceptors(sp.GetServices<ISaveChangesInterceptor>()) on the DbContext + modelBuilder.ApplyRaskConventions(this) in OnModelCreating (adds the query filter + IsConcurrencyToken). Optimistic concurrency: the edit command carries Version; in the handler, set db.Entry(x).Property(e=>e.Version).OriginalValue to the caller's version before SaveChanges → DbUpdateConcurrencyException on a stale save. BULK INSERT: `db.BulkInsert(entities, o => o.BatchSize = 5000)` (also on DbSet<T>) fills the gap EF Core leaves — ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete exist but bulk INSERT is explicitly out of EF's scope. Runs THROUGH the context so the interceptors still stamp/publish per row; batches the adds, turns AutoDetectChanges off, CLEARS the change tracker between batches (keeps a large load flat instead of quadratic — 100k rows: 942ms/1.16GB batched vs 1.25s/1.37GB for AddRange+SaveChanges vs 5.2s/2.59GB save-per-row). EACH BATCH COMMITS ON ITS OWN by default (SQLite has one write lock — a single transaction over a long import makes every other writer wait and the WAL hold every uncommitted page; the cost is that a failure leaves the committed batches). `o.SingleTransaction = true` makes the load all-or-nothing. THAT MODE, AND ANY AMBIENT TRANSACTION, REJECTS ENTITIES CARRYING DOMAIN EVENTS: DomainEventInterceptor publishes in SavedChanges, which inside a transaction runs BEFORE the commit, so a load failing at batch 7 would already have announced batches 1-6 — clear the events, drop the transaction, or use Rask.Outbox (same-transaction messages, drained after commit). FAST PATH `o.SkipChangeTracking = true`: writes the rows with ONE prepared single-row INSERT, parameters rebound per row, no entity entry ever materialised. OPT-IN because NO ISaveChangesInterceptor runs — not Rask's, not yours. The writer stamps CreatedAt/UpdatedAt itself from the SAME TimeProvider the AuditingInterceptor resolves (a frozen test clock agrees across both paths), but nothing stands in for the rest: entities carrying domain events are REJECTED, and an outbox never sees the load. Refuses-with-a-reason rather than writing wrong rows for: store-assigned integer keys, store-computed columns, shadow properties, navigations (nothing walks the graph), inheritance hierarchies, and a value-generated key left unset. A Guid key the entity assigns itself (the Aggregate<Guid> shape) is fine — Rask.Data's convention marks every non-integer Entity<TId> key ValueGeneratedNever — but one still left at Guid.Empty is REFUSED rather than written, since nothing on this path assigns it and the second such row would collide. DO NOT use a multi-row INSERT ... VALUES (..),(..) here: each distinct row count is a new statement to parse and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite binds by parameter NAME, so packing to the 32,766-parameter limit is quadratic (measured 192ms/7.2s/2.07min at 1k/10k/100k) and even a modest 200-row packing loses badly to prepared reuse. Throws if the context has pending changes (it clears the tracker, so it refuses rather than discard them); joins an ambient transaction instead of committing itself; under a retrying strategy a SingleTransaction load is one retryable unit with the sequence buffered for re-enumeration, while per-batch lets EF retry each batch with no replay. FULL-TEXT SEARCH: `modelBuilder.Entity<Post>().HasFullTextSearch(p => new { p.Title, p.Body }, tokenizer?)` declares an index (FullTextTokenizer.Unicode default = word boundaries, case- AND diacritic-insensitive, so keres finds kérés; .English adds Porter stemming). READ with `Post.Search(text)`, `Post.Where(...).Search(text)` (ModelQuery) or `db.Set<Post>().Search(text)` (any EF IQueryable): every typed word must match, the LAST word also as a prefix, BEST MATCH FIRST (bm25), and the result KEEPS COMPOSING — Where/Skip/Take/CountAsync apply to the matches and a later OrderBy REPLACES rank order (so `Ui.DataGrid.Data(Post.Search(q).AsQueryable())` sorts and pages in the DB). Text is ALWAYS WORDS, NEVER FTS5 SYNTAX: Search compiles it to quoted phrases, so `"`, OR, NEAR(, title: cannot break or change the query; null/blank/punctuation-only text filters NOTHING (returns the source unchanged). `FullText.Highlight(p.Title)` / `FullText.Snippet(p.Body, words = 12)` inside a Select on a query that calls Search return the value/best passage with matches between FullText.MatchStart (U+E000) and FullText.MatchEnd (U+E001) — NOT HTML; render with `Ui.Highlight.Text(value)` (encodes, wraps matches in <mark>); calling them without Search, or on a non-indexed property, throws naming the fix. THREE PROVIDERS, one declaration and one query. SQLITE: Rask.SQLite.EntityFrameworkCore's UseRaskSqlite, or a PLAIN UseSqlite + `.UseRaskFullTextSearch()` (only the migration SQL + query rewrite, none of UseRaskSqlite's connection string/pragmas/retry; after UseRaskSqlite it keeps that call's generator, STRICT included) — which is also THE BROWSER: `UseSqlite(BrowserSqlite.ConnectionString("app")).UseRaskFullTextSearch()` over Rask.SQLite.Browser, FTS5 in the WASM bundle (index built by a MIGRATION — Database.MigrateAsync(), never EnsureCreated). On SQLite migrations emit an FTS5 virtual table + AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers (raw SQL and other processes are indexed too; trusted_schema=OFF-safe); adding the declaration to an EXISTING table is its own migration (the spec is reported as a TABLE annotation) that FILLS the index; any migration touching the table rebuilds it. The index `{Table}_fts` KEEPS ITS OWN COPY of the indexed text (external content cannot forget the row an INSERT OR REPLACE replaces — no AFTER DELETE fires — so every trigger clears a row's entry by id first; REPLACE/upsert/key changes stay correct). A single integer key (strongly-typed ids included) is the entry id; Guid/string/composite keys go through a `{Table}_fts_keys` key map (implicit rowid is not VACUUM-stable); the layout is recorded as a `Rask:FullTextSearch:Layout` model annotation so a migration run from its saved model matches the queries. `Post.Search(text).ThenBy(k)` breaks ties; after an EMPTY search ThenBy is the ordering (no throw). POSTGRESQL: UseRaskPostgres — a STORED GENERATED tsvector column + GIN index (no triggers, Npgsql's own migrations), `@@ to_tsquery` ranked by ts_rank_cd, Highlight/Snippet via ts_headline in the same markers; English → `english`, Unicode → `rask_unicode` (simple + unaccent, created by the first migration that needs it: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS unaccent); a PG snippet has no … at its cut ends. SQL SERVER, or a plain UseSqlite WITHOUT UseRaskFullTextSearch(): AddRaskData<TContext> REFUSES TO BOOT a context declaring an index. JSON PATH INDEX: `builder.HasJsonIndex(o => o.Meta.Status)` on a ToJson() owned type adds an expression index spelled EXACTLY as EF writes the filter (top-level `'Status'` vs nested `'$.Address.City'`), through migrations — SQLite-only for now, refused at boot elsewhere. Guide: docs/full-text-search.md. NON-OVERLAPPING RANGES: `modelBuilder.Entity<Booking>().HasNonOverlappingRange(x => x.StartsAt, x => x.EndsAt, partitionBy: x => x.RoomId)` declares that two rows may not cover the same point of a half-open [lo, hi) range — the booking/lease/price-period rule. SQLite has NO exclusion constraint and a UNIQUE index only stops IDENTICAL rows (100-200 and 150-250 both pass), so the rule is carried as provider-agnostic model metadata (a RangeExclusionSpec annotation naming PROPERTIES, resolved to columns by the provider so HasColumnName is honoured) and Rask.SQLite.EntityFrameworkCore's UseRaskSqlite emits an index + a BEFORE INSERT/BEFORE UPDATE trigger pair that RAISE(ABORT)s. HALF-OPEN is load-bearing: 100-200 and 200-300 are NEIGHBOURS, not a conflict; pair with a lo<hi check constraint since the rule assumes well-formed ranges. partitionBy scopes it (x => x.RoomId, or x => new { x.Sku, x.Region }); omit for table-wide. ignoreSoftDeleted defaults to TRUE for an aggregate that declares Deletes = Deletion.Soft so a deleted row frees its slot, and to false for everything else (a hard-delete aggregate has no DeletedAt column); ignoreSoftDeleted: true on such an entity throws ArgumentException. A violating save throws RangeOverlapException naming the table, translated from SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_TRIGGER (1811) by an interceptor, instead of a raw code buried in DbUpdateException. Enforcement is IN THE DATABASE, so raw SQL/other processes are bound too — and a check-then-insert in app code would race. THE DDL IS RE-EMITTED AT THE END OF EVERY MIGRATION THAT TOUCHES THE TABLE, drop-then-create: SQLite cannot ALTER most things in place, so EF rebuilds the table (ef_temp_* -> copy -> DROP TABLE -> rename) and the DROP takes the triggers with it — attaching the DDL to CreateTable would silently retire the constraint on the next schema change. Arrives via migrations only: an existing table gains it from the next migration, EnsureCreated does not get it. A PROVIDER THAT DOES NOT EMIT THAT DDL (a plain UseSqlite, or any other provider) WOULD SILENTLY ACCEPT OVERLAPS, so AddRaskData<TContext> registers a boot check (IHostedService, reads the model + the context's IMigrationsSqlGenerator, no connection) that REFUSES TO START naming the entity, the provider and UseRaskSqlite. The SkipChangeTracking writer spells table/column/parameter names through EF Core's ISqlGenerationHelper (MySQL rejects hard-coded "…" identifiers) and awaits each row on client-server providers, staying synchronous only on SQLite. Depends on Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore + Rask.Cqrs; runs on the server and, over Rask.SQLite.Browser, in a WebAssembly app. The base the soft-delete/concurrency/domain-event conventions build on. A write needs no token: `await Product.Create(model)`, `p.Save()`, `Product.Delete(id)` are cancelled with the request (`Current.Cancellation`) unless one is passed.
- [Multi-tenancy](docs/multi-tenancy.md): one database, each customer's rows kept apart — OPT-IN per table with the fifth const, `public const Tenancy Scope = Tenancy.PerTenant;` (default `Tenancy.Shared`): a `TenantId` column (a SHADOW column — NOT a property of `Entity<TId>`; an entity that reads it declares `public Guid? TenantId { get; private set; }` — or `int?` / `long?` for NUMBERED tenants, and the declared type is then the column's, the filter's and the stamp's; `Tenant.Use(42)` opens one by number, carried in the Guid as eight zero bytes then the number big-endian, so 42 is `00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000002a`), a query filter no read can compose away, and TenantId PREFIXED onto every index that does not already name it (in `Configure`, by `[Index]` or in your own context; an index that names `TenantId` ANYWHERE is left exactly as declared — how an existing table keeps `(Name, TenantId)`). The tenant is the SIGNED-IN USER'S (the `rask:tenant` claim, `Tenant.ClaimType`), on a live session, every HTTP request (controller, minimal API, CQRS endpoint) and a restored session; `Current.Tenant`/`Current.RequiredTenant` read it (explicit `Tenant.Use(id)` first, then the claim, null inside `Tenant.Across()`); `Tenant.None()` clears it. An app that knows its tenant another way registers a RESOLVER — `services.AddRaskTenant(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<ICurrentRequest>().TenantId)` (`Guid?`, `int?` or `long?`) — which REPLACES the claim, is asked ONCE per scope and kept (as a request starts, as a live session opens), loses to an explicit `Tenant.Use`/`Across`, refuses (`ForbiddenException`) a user whose claim names another tenant, and when it returns null makes a tenant-scoped table read EMPTY and every write throw `MissingTenantException` (never all tenants; without a resolver a read with no tenant still THROWS). Existing tables with no migration: [Mapping tables that already exist](docs/data.md#mapping-tables-that-already-exist) — on a host wired by hand (`AddRask()` + `MapRask<App>()`, not `RaskApp`) data is two calls from Rask.Server, `builder.Services.AddRaskData<DomainContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(cs))` and `app.UseRaskData()` after `UseAuthentication()`, which create and migrate NOTHING. A user joins a tenant through the protected `RecordTenant(id)` every entity has (e.g. `public void JoinTenant(Guid t) => RecordTenant(t);` on `User`, called from the `Register` lambda). An ADMIN has no tenant, carries no claim, and a tenant-scoped read THROWS until `Tenant.Use(chosen)` — reading everything is a deliberate, greppable `Tenant.Across()`. A tenant-scoped read with no tenant THROWS; `IgnoreQueryFilters()` never crosses tenants; creates stamp the tenant, an update that moves a row is refused, an insert inside Across() needs TenantId set. BATTERIES carry the tenant as DATA, not a filter: jobs/mail/outbox record it at enqueue and the runner re-enters it (a job also records `UserId`, so `Current.UserId` answers in its handler — upgrading needs `rask db add AddJobUser && rask db update`); the CACHE scopes the stored key per tenant (the DB-backed store only; anonymous keys untouched); a STORED FILE belongs to the tenant that saved it and lookups/opens/temporary URLs/deletes are scoped; ACCOUNTS: an address is unique WITHIN a tenant (index over TenantKey, which folds null to Guid.Empty so it means the same on SQLite/PostgreSQL/SQL Server) and sign-in REFUSES an address two tenants hold. The context must call `modelBuilder.ApplyRaskConventions(this)` and implement `ITenantScoped` (RaskDbContext does); a host of your own registers a scoped `IPrincipalSource` and opens `Db.UseScope(requestServices)` per request.
- [Full-text search](docs/full-text-search.md): ranked, word-aware, diacritic-insensitive search from LINQ — `builder.HasFullTextSearch(p => new { p.Title, p.Body }, tokenizer?)` then `Post.Search(text)` / `db.Set<Post>().Search(text)`, best match first, keeps composing (a later OrderBy replaces rank), typed text is ALWAYS WORDS (never query syntax), `FullText.Highlight`/`Snippet` rendered by `Ui.Highlight.Text`. Runs on SQLITE (`UseRaskSqlite`, or plain `UseSqlite` + `.UseRaskFullTextSearch()`: FTS5 + triggers), IN THE BROWSER (Rask.SQLite.Browser + `.UseRaskFullTextSearch()`, apply migrations) and on POSTGRESQL (`UseRaskPostgres`: stored generated tsvector + GIN, ts_rank_cd, ts_headline, `rask_unicode` over unaccent); SQL Server and a plain UseSqlite without the call REFUSE TO BOOT a context declaring an index. The index arrives by MIGRATION (EnsureCreated creates none) and the database keeps it current.
- [Transactional outbox](docs/outbox.md): `Rask.Outbox`, ALWAYS ON while data is (no `c.Outbox.Off()` — settings only: `c.Outbox.Configure(o => …)` / `Rask:Outbox`). **THE HANDLER CHOOSES DURABILITY, NOT THE EVENT**: an event is a plain `IEvent`; `IEventHandler<T>` runs in memory right after the commit (fast, lost on a crash), `IDurableHandler<T>` gets its OWN `OutboxMessage` row (Handler column) written in the SAME transaction as the change that raised it, run after the commit, retried to MaxAttempts, dead-lettered alone — one row PER durable handler, so a failing SendReceipt never re-runs ChargeCard. `IOutboxEvent` and `RaskDataOptions.DispatchDomainEventsInProcess` are GONE. A bare `dispatcher.Publish(e)` (no save) stores its durable rows in a transaction of its own; with no outbox (browser, Cqrs alone) durable handlers run in memory. The processor is WOKEN by every save that wrote rows (poll = safety net). **MARK DOMAIN EVENTS `[LocalOnly]`**: events travel from a browser like any message, so an unmarked OrderPlaced could be forged by a signed-in user and run SendReceipt. The Rask.Cqrs generator records each durable handler beside its event (no Type.GetType/scanning); a renamed handler dead-letters its old rows with a message; `OutboxSerializerRegistry.RegisterEvent("Old.Name", typeof(E))` keeps a renamed EVENT readable. Rows record the tenant and the processor re-enters it. Each outcome is saved on its own; retention purges PUBLISHED rows hourly in pages, never dead letters. MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE (leases; at-least-once stays the contract — make durable handlers idempotent). UPGRADING: `rask db add AddOutboxHandler && rask db update` for the Handler column (the processor logs exactly that until you do); a pre-upgrade row runs every handler of its event once. Hand-wired: `AddRaskCqrs()` + `AddRaskOutbox<AppDbContext>()` (brings AddRaskData) + `.AddInterceptors(sp.GetServices<ISaveChangesInterceptor>())` + `modelBuilder.AddRaskOutbox()`. The tutorial's chapter 7 registers nothing — it writes the event and an `IDurableHandler<T>`.
- [Pillar metrics](docs/observability.md): each DB-backed pillar owns an OpenTelemetry-compatible `Meter` registered by its `AddRaskX` call — `Rask.Jobs`/`Rask.Outbox`/`Rask.Mail`, alongside the existing `Rask.Server`. Per pillar: `rask.<pillar>.processed|sent` + `.failed` (EVERY attempt, not every item) + `.deadlettered` (once, on the attempt that exhausts MaxAttempts) counters, a `.duration` histogram (ms), and `.pending`/`.deadletters` observable gauges. **`rask.*.deadletters` is the alert** — at-least-once with backoff means a pillar retrying itself to death still shows a healthy processed rate. Jobs/outbox tag by `job.type`/`message.type` (a closed set fixed at build time by the source generator); MAIL IS UNTAGGED ON PURPOSE (subject/recipient are unbounded → a time series per email). Queue-depth gauges are sampled on the processor's existing poll and ONLY while `metrics.WantsQueueDepth` (i.e. a listener subscribed) — never `COUNT(*)` inside the gauge callback, which a 1s collector would turn into continuous DB read load. `dotnet-counters monitor --counters Rask.Server,Rask.Jobs,Rask.Outbox,Rask.Mail`.
- [Blazor components](docs/blazor-components.md): a **real Blazor component** as an ordinary Rask component — from a Razor Class Library, MudBlazor, Radzen, any `ComponentBase`. Derive a `partial` class from `BlazorComponent<T>` and place it anywhere the chain goes. **The Razor SDK is neither replaced nor reconfigured**: it compiles `.razor` exactly as it always has, and Rask renders the result — which is why this costs nothing that can rot. **You do not redeclare parameters**: a Blazor component already states its surface, so the chain steps are read from its own `[Parameter]` properties, and `[BlazorParameter("Name")]` renames one whose name collides with a chain entry (`Title`, `Label`, `Form`, `Select`) — no longer a compile error now RASKSUP001 suppresses that CS0108, so the rename is a readability choice rather than a requirement. **Server-rendered into the FIRST response**: the work runs from `OnUpdated`, whose task lands in the page's quiescence scope, so a hosted component awaiting in `OnInitializedAsync` has finished before the HTML is sent rather than arriving a frame later — the whole value claim, and asserted on the real `QuiescentRender` wave path because `Page.Render` is synchronous and could not prove it. **Parameters cross as live CLR objects** through `ParameterView`, not JSON: no wire vocabulary to violate, unlike a `.tsx` island's props. A nullable prop that is null OMITS its key — the OPPOSITE of the islands rule, because `ParameterView` is authoritative and writing null would CLOBBER the component's own default rather than mean "unset". **The hosted component's own `@onclick` fires with NO Blazor circuit**: Blazor assigns a real handler id to every event even in a static render and its own HTML writer simply drops them, so `BlazorFrameWriter` walks the render tree and writes Rask's `data-rask-on-*` instead — the click uses the delegated listener already in the page, travels the socket already open, and comes back through `DispatchEventAsync`. No SignalR, no `blazor.web.js`, no second connection; the same channel the React and Lit islands use. EVERY DOM event is wired and the hosted handler receives REAL args, built without reflection from the same payload a Rask `OnKeyDown(e => …)` reads: `MouseEventArgs`/`PointerEventArgs`/`WheelEventArgs`/`DragEventArgs`, `KeyboardEventArgs` (`e.Key` is the key), `TouchEventArgs`, `FocusEventArgs`/`ClipboardEventArgs`; `ProgressEventArgs`/`ErrorEventArgs` carry only `Type`; a handler taking `EventArgs` or nothing asks the browser for no payload. NOT wired, and so no attribute: an args type outside that set (a library's custom `[EventHandler]` args — one logged warning names the island, event and type) and `@onsubmit`. Each event is one round trip, which matters for `@onpointermove`/`@onwheel`. **A Blazor island is a LEAF**: writing Rask children into a hosted component is a compile error (RASK062) — unlike a JS island, which takes children of its own runtime. No single crossing was right for all four `RenderFragment` shapes, and every wrong one failed silently or at render time. Compose the other way round — Rask chrome around the island. **A statically rendered island is deliberately NOT opaque**, and this is the trap: `FrameDiffer` SKIPS an opaque element's children, so an opaque static island would render new HTML on the server and never ship it — painting once and silently freezing. Opacity is reserved for a future circuit mode where the subtree really would belong to Blazor. Uses `StaticHtmlRenderer`, not `HtmlRenderer`: `HtmlRootComponent` cannot take new parameters, so every prop change would re-run `OnInitializedAsync` and discard state; `RenderRootComponentAsync` keeps one instance across updates (`OnInitialized` once, `OnParametersSet` per change). **BOTH hosts** — `net10.0` and `net10.0-browser`, one code path with no `#if`; only the renderer's source differs (the ASP.NET shared framework on the server, the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web` package in the browser). Trimming was the real constraint: `ParameterView.SetParameterProperties` reaches `[Parameter]` properties by reflection inside `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components`, on the hosted type, so under `PublishTrimmed` (a WASM app's DEFAULT) the trimmer removes the setters and the island renders as an EMPTY `<rask-blazor>` — no analyser warning (the reflection is in another assembly), no exception, nothing in the console, and a green build. `BlazorComponent<TComponent>` annotates its type parameter `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers(All)]` (`All` because `[Inject]` reaches non-public properties), which states the requirement where the concrete type is known. ANNOTATED, NOT GATED END TO END: `TrimmingContractTests` pins the annotation, but nothing in the repository publishes a hosted component trimmed any more, so verify a trimmed app renders content — an empty island passes a presence check. It is opt-in on both hosts: neither `Rask.Server` nor `Rask.Wasm` references it. The hosted type must come from a REFERENCED project or package for its parameters to be read — a `.razor` in the same project is produced by the Razor source generator and one source generator never sees another's output, so it works but unverified (RASK066). Diagnostics RASK061 (must be partial), RASK064 (name collision), RASK066. **Compiling `.razor` INTO the chain was investigated and rejected on facts**: Razor's syntax layer is `internal` in every shipped version (`RazorSyntaxTree.Root` returns a type no third party can name), the .NET 10 SDK compiler exposes neither the intermediate document nor a way to register a pass that would receive one — its 23 `InternalsVisibleTo` friends (`rzc`, Blazor's generator, the VS and VS Code Razor extensions) reach those instead — and the last public extension API is `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Language` 6.0.36, a .NET 6-era package out of support since November 2024. `@bind` round-trips, write-back included: a value-carrying event goes through Rask's INPUT channel (the one that ships the element's value beside the handler id) rather than the DOM-event table; a checkbox's binder receives a `bool` and a `<select multiple>`'s a `string[]` (on the default `change` only — `@bind:event="oninput"` on those two still gets a string). **NO `AddRaskBlazor()` call is needed** — referencing `Rask.Blazor` is the whole setup; `AddRaskBlazor(o => …)` only sets an option (`BaseUri`, `HeadAssets`). `[Inject]` resolves from the app's own container (`IJSRuntime`, your services, Rask's typed browser APIs), and the island supplies the `NavigationManager` a library component expects — a view onto RASK'S ROUTING: `Uri` is the page on screen, `NavigateTo` moves the browser as `Go.To` does, and a Rask navigation raises `LocationChanged`. `OnAfterRenderAsync` fires ONCE, after the island's first paint, and may call `StateHasChanged`.
