NOT SUPPORTED: `ElementReference`/element `@ref` (the frame writer discards the capture, so library JS that bootstraps against an element stays inert), `<Virtualize>`, `<PageTitle>`/`<HeadContent>` (no `HeadOutlet`), any `RenderFragment`/`ChildContent` parameter, a cascading value supplied from Rask, `@rendermode`/a circuit, and fine-grained diffing inside the island (a prop change replaces its DOM, losing scroll and selection).
- [Single-page app front ends](docs/spa.md): an npm-built front end (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular) inside an ASP.NET host — `dotnet build` runs `npm ci` + `npm run build`, `dotnet publish` ships the bundle, `app.MapRaskSpa()` serves it. Package `Rask.Spa.Hosting`; properties `RaskSpaClientDir`, `RaskSpaDistDir`, `RaskSpaBuild`. `rask new Shop --template react|preact|vue|angular|solid|svelte|lit` scaffolds one: a `Rask.Server` host (`RaskApp.Create(args).Serve()`) with that framework's TypeScript + Tailwind app in `client/` (Vite on 5173; Angular is `ng serve` on 4200 with `proxy.conf.json` and `RaskSpaDistDir` = `dist/<app>-client/browser`), the same plain-Tailwind starter in each, sign-in and register screens over `/api/auth`, and (unless `--no-push`) `client/src/push.ts` over the browser `PushManager` and `/_rask/push`.
- [Islands](docs/islands.md): a `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, Angular or Lit file as an **ordinary Rask component** — how React, Vue, Svelte and the rest run in a Rask app. Derive a component from one of SEVEN base classes — `ReactComponent`, `PreactComponent`, `SolidComponent`, `VueComponent`, `SvelteComponent`, `AngularComponent`, `LitComponent` — drop the front-end file beside it (paired by filename, exactly like `Counter.ts` beside `Counter.cs`), and place it anywhere the chain goes: a leaf inside a card, a subtree, or the whole of a `[Route]` page's `Render()`. There is deliberately NO separate page concept — "React owns this route" is the case where the component IS the page root, so replaceability is a property of the COMPONENT rather than of the route and composes at every level of the tree. **An island can also carry the `[Route]` itself**: a `[RouteParam]` is an ordinary prop, its `HeadAssets` sets the title and meta (the runtime script is registered separately, so overriding it is safe), `.Loading(Ui.Skeleton…)` renders plain Rask markup inside the host element for the first response (removed right before the island mounts; first-paint only, no handlers; a routed island sets `Loading` in its constructor), and `<a href data-rask-nav>` inside an island navigates in-app. A JS island is client-rendered — for an SEO-critical page give `Loading` real content, write a Rask page, or use a Blazor island. **The base class IS the declaration**: it names the runtime in the one place that cannot disagree with what actually mounts, which is also what lets a Lit component pair with `./Name.ts` by convention — a Lit file is ordinary TypeScript and no extension distinguishes it, so before this every Lit component had to name its module twice. The cost is the single-inheritance slot (a component already extending another base class cannot also be a `ReactComponent`), and that is the deliberate trade: chrome in Rask comes from the CHAIN, not from inheritance, so the answer is `Ui.Card[ Chart.Series(pts) ]` rather than inheriting both. Override `Module` with a CONSTANT string to point somewhere convention cannot reach — the bundler reads it at build time, so anything computed is RASK059. `partial` is required (RASK056) because the name, the module and the props writer are generated into the same class; a hand-written `Render()` is CS0239, because the base class SEALS it (a rule the type system can state needs no analyzer). **C# owns the props**: ordinary properties, so the chain and RASK001 apply unmodified, serialized by generated `Utf8JsonWriter` code rather than reflection (which is what lets them survive trimming/AOT), over the SAME wire vocabulary the CQRS codecs use — `WireShape` and the TypeScript emitter moved to `Rask.Generators.Shared` so there is one answer to "what does this C# type look like on the wire" instead of two that drift. A prop named after an HTML tag (`Title`, `Label`, `Data`, `Form`) is fine: it hides the chain entry, and RASKSUP001 suppresses the CS0108 that used to make that fatal under -warnaserror — which matters most here, because those are natural prop names for a UI component. **Callbacks re-enter C# over the channel every DOM handler already uses**: `Callback`/`Callback<T>` props (set with any handler shape, sync or async) travel as a handler reference rather than a value, and reach the app over the open WebSocket on the Server host or a direct `[JSExport]` call into this tab's runtime on WASM — never a channel of its own, so on Server a callback inherits sequence stamping, the queue-while-reconnecting and the auth suppression window for free, and the `.tsx` is byte-identical on both hosts. On WASM the page is prerendered, so an island is clickable before .NET boots: a callback fired then is HELD and delivered after the first frame, to the island that fired it. An unwired callback OMITS its key (the front end sees `undefined`); a null DATA prop stays JSON `null`, because "never set" and "set to nothing" differ. **The live diff treats the subtree as opaque** — React reconciles those nodes on its own schedule, and two writers on one subtree does not throw, it corrupts on the next parent re-render. `Component.OpaqueSubtree` rides `RenderFrame` so the differ skips by `SubtreeLength`, AND is written as `data-rask-opaque` so the client morph refuses to descend: both are needed, because the diff and the full-HTML fallback are separate paths to the same DOM, and the morph is the one that bites. `LeanFrame` carries the flag too, or the retained clean-subtree cache would replay a cached component without its boundary. What crosses is props and only props: a change travels as ONE attribute op the client routes to the adapter's `update`, so an update is a reconcile and never a remount (the component keeps scroll, focus, an open dropdown, a half-typed field), and callbacks keep their IDENTITY across updates because React compares props by identity. **A component straight from npm needs no front-end file**: a class whose constant `Module` names a package (`Module => "react-colorful"`, with `Export => "HexColorPicker"` for a named export — the two halves of the `import`; no `#` mini-syntax) is a PACKAGE island; several components from ONE package are declared once — `sealed partial class Mui : ReactPackage { Module => "@mui/material"; Exports => ["Button", "Card"]; }` (one `*Package` base per runtime) — and reached as `Mui.Button`/`Mui.Card` (each export an island `MuiButton` with `MuiButton.props.json` beside the declaration; no bare entry, so `Button` stays the HTML tag), and its props and chain steps are generated from a committed `{Island}.props.json` the build extracts from the package's own TypeScript declarations with a Rask-pinned `typescript` under Node — rewritten with a printed diff when the package changes, locked (RASKISLAND008) under CI, so a fresh clone, the IDE and a build without Node see the same steps. String-literal unions become C# enums, and an unset prop is omitted so the package's own default applies. **An island takes children of ITS OWN RUNTIME, never Rask markup**: a React island accepts React islands, text, numbers and dates (`MuiCard["Revenue ", MuiButton.OnClick(Save)["Save"]]`, `MuiList[_names]`), which travel inside its props as `$c` and its framework renders — so the host element stays empty on the server and a change anywhere in the tree is still ONE attribute op. Every hand-written island accepts children; a package island does when its snapshot says its component takes content. Rask-rendered content handed inside one would still be content Rask owns and updates in nodes it can no longer address — EditOp paths are positional `childNodes` indices, and every one of them is wrong the moment the adapter relocates the nodes — so Rask markup or another runtime's island inside an island is RASK062, reported at the brackets (the island's inherited indexers return a `ref struct` that cannot become a component, but the compiler alone says so late, and never for a `var`). For Rask markup, compose the other way round: the island goes INSIDE the Rask markup. All seven ship. **The base class, never the extension, decides the runtime**: three of them write `.tsx` and two write `.ts`, so an extension names a FAMILY, and the generator carries the declared runtime out of the compilation as a constant for the build to read back — guessing wrong is silent all the way to the browser, where a Solid island handed React's adapter compiles, bundles, ships, loads and mounts nothing. Two runtimes compiling the same extension are scoped to their own island DIRECTORIES and overlapping trees are refused by name; file-level scoping is not enough, because it leaves the modules an island IMPORTS to the other plugin (a helper beside a Solid island came back compiled as Preact — a green build shipping a foreign vnode into Solid's renderer). React beside Preact is refused outright and not by Rask's choice: `@vitejs/plugin-react` resolves Babel 8 where `@preact/preset-vite` pins `@babel/core@"7.x"`, so npm will not install both; `ReactComponent` still covers Preact the old way through a `preact/compat` alias. The prop type-check splits by runtime for the same reason one `jsx` setting cannot serve three JSX dialects and Angular's decorators need an `experimentalDecorators` Lit 3's standard decorators need OFF — merged, the check reported errors that were not in the author's code. Angular's plugin additionally needs `@angular/compiler-cli` and `@angular/build` installed beside it (it imports both, depends on neither), pins TypeScript below 6.1, and must be pointed at a tsconfig RASK writes: the app's own sets `noEmit`, which leaves ngtsc emitting nothing and every `.ts` island without a default export, reported against files that plainly have one. Its bootstrap is also the only asynchronous one, so props arriving before `createApplication()` resolves are held rather than dropped. **`rask dev` serves islands from a Vite dev server on 5174** (not Vite's default 5173) and skips only the production bundle, so an edit hot-replaces: Fast Refresh for React/Preact, `solid-refresh` for Solid, plugin HMR for Vue/Svelte — all keeping component state — while Lit and Angular have no refresh integration upstream and fall back to a page reload, still with no C# rebuild. Hot reload works on Rask.Server and WASM alike (the dev manifest names the loopback dev server under `$dev`), and an app under a path base (`/shop`) loads its island runtime, manifest and chunks under it with nothing to configure. Resolution stays ONE path in dev and production; only the manifest's contents differ. The client runtime imports NO framework at all — each built chunk default-exports its own adapter, three functions wide (`mount`/`update`/`unmount`), so further runtimes are additive. `dotnet build` writes one entry module per component (pairing it with its adapter, so the `.tsx` keeps no Rask import) and hands Vite a generated config that builds a chunk each plus the manifest the runtime resolves names through — read back from the rollup ACTUALLY emitted rather than predicted, so a re-hashed chunk cannot drift from the entry pointing at it. **Node runs only when the project has a package.json**: that single probe is the gate, so an app with none of these never learns this package has a build step. Vite is the ONLY bundler and that is deliberate — an esbuild path with no npm was designed and rejected: esbuild can do the whole job (--splitting for a hashed chunk per component plus a shared one, --metafile for what was ACTUALLY emitted, --jsx=automatic, ~1ms) but two bundlers means two failure modes and "why does it work in project A but not B" forever, and the no-npm audience was narrower than it looked since a real Lit component imports `lit` from npm. Rask ITSELF stays npm-free (#871 fetches esbuild and tsgo as verified binaries); needing React from npm is inherent to asking for a React component. Vite is what made Vue and Svelte cheap, since their SFC compilers ARE Vite plugins; the single-file compilers must be registered BEFORE the React plugin, whose JSX transform is general and would otherwise swallow a `.vue` as `Unexpected JSX expression` at line 1. A `.vue`/`.svelte` cannot be checked by tsgo (no plugin seam), so those go to `vue-tsc`/`svelte-check` from the project's own node_modules — a second and third toolchain accepted because the alternative is not a weaker check but NO check. **What a browser verifies**: on WASM (`WasmIslandsExampleTests`, over the site's islands page) Vue, React, Svelte, Solid and a Lit-runtime element mount, take their C# props, reconcile a prop change without remounting and call back into C# ([JSExport] into this tab's runtime); on Server (`ServerIslandJourneyTests`) only a Lit-runtime island mounting with its props and a Blazor island's own click — the other runtimes are covered there by the Node adapter suites, and Preact and Angular run in no browser test. An earlier browser run on the Server showcase (since deleted) found four faults nothing else could: colliding handler ids putting the callback in a map the dispatcher never reads; HeadAssets being collected only in the serializer's COMPONENT branch, so an element-shaped component rendered an empty <head> and no runtime script; Vite dropping `export default` from application entries without preserveEntrySignatures; and an Action<T> falling to a DynamicInvoke with no arguments, throwing, and taking the page down. Callback arguments are scalars (a record or list argument is RASK057). **A Lit island is written WITHOUT decorators and default-exports its registered tag name** (`static properties` + `customElements.define('my-tag', MyTag)` + `export default 'my-tag'`) — Vite does not lower `@customElement`, and an element whose decorator was not lowered never upgrades. **`rask new Shop --islands react vue lit blazor`** scaffolds a paired `.cs` + front-end file per runtime, the npm dependencies, the tsconfig mapping and the package reference. **An island can live in a shared Razor class library**: the library bundles it, serves it under `/_content/<PackageId>/_rask/external/`, and its host element names that manifest, so one page can carry islands from the app and several libraries. Not yet: Islands load from the page's OWN ORIGIN only: the client refuses a manifest or chunk another origin serves (the loopback `rask dev` island server excepted), so a CDN-hosted bundle is not a supported deployment and an absolute `RaskExternalPublicBase` fails the build. **Navigating from an island** is the C# surface, generated: `import { Routes, Go } from '@rask/routes'` gives `Routes.UserPage({ Id: 42 }).Go()`, `.Go().Replacing()`, `Go.To(route)`, `Go.With('page', '2')`, `Go.Without('page')`, `.Url` and `<a {...Routes.UserPage({ Id: 42 }).Link}>` — page names, nesting and parameter names are the C# `Routes` class's, parameters are one typed object, and there is no string-path navigation. SSR for the bundler-backed runtimes.
- [Batteries dashboard](docs/dashboard.md): the `Rask.Dashboard` package (in `Rask.Server`, on by default) — an operator dashboard at `/_rask` over every DB-backed pillar's own table, no exporter or second datastore. Runs on the `server` template AND on a host serving a single-page app through `MapRaskSpa()` — a Rask WebAssembly app — mounted at `/_rask/{**path}` above the SPA fallback with `app.MapRaskServer<RaskDashboardShell>("/_rask/{**path}")`, since a bundle-serving host owns no component for `MapRaskServer<TApp>` to name. Both halves share `/_rask/a/{hash}`: Rask.Server's endpoint answers a hash its own process never registered from `IWebHostEnvironment.WebRootFileProvider`, and `MapRaskSpa` adds a WebAssembly bundle's `_rask/a/` subtree (and only that) to it. `/_rask` is the framework's own reserved prefix — `/_rask/a/{hash}.{ext}` scoped assets, `/_rask/auth/redeem`, `/_rask/upload/{id}`, `/_rask/download/{id}/{token}` — which are LITERAL routes and so outrank the dashboard's catch-all; a dashboard page named `a`/`auth`/`upload`/`download` would silently 404 (pinned by ReservedPrefixTests). Such a host registers `AddRaskServer()` + `AddRaskSpaHost()` and maps `MapRaskServer<RaskDashboardShell>(…)` + `MapRaskSpa()`, each name saying which host a line belongs to — or, as the wasm-hosted template does, is `RaskApp.Create(args).Serve()`, which does all of it. `RaskApp` registers it with nothing in Program.cs (on by default; `rask new --no-ops` writes `c.Ops.Off()`); a hand-wired host calls `builder.Services.AddRaskDashboard<TContext>()`, which mounts a route chain under a `[Route("_rask")]` layout. Panels: Overview (a tile per queue + a banner the moment any dead letter exists), Queues (outbox/jobs/mail in one view split due/delayed/FAILED/processed, a row's Details sheet shows its last error + stored payload), Cache (keys, sizes, expiry, expired-not-yet-swept), Storage (read-only at `/_rask/storage`: file and byte counts, public count, usage per provider, a searchable recent-files list, and a notice when files sit on disk where no backup covers them; `/_rask/files/…` is reserved for Rask.Storage's file routes), Logs (bounded in-memory tail of the ILogger pipeline — memory-only, gone on restart — plus, when `Rask.Logging` is registered, a **History** mode reading its durable store: paged with level/category/text filters; two modes rather than a merged view because that store's writer flushes on an interval), System (SQLite pragmas read live via the open DbConnection, DB size, recurring-job schedule joined to RecurringJobState). DRAWN WITH Rask.Ui AND NOTHING ELSE: the pages write no class strings (`DashboardIsKitOnlyTests` scans `src/Rask.Dashboard` for `.Class(`/`.Style(`/`UiStyles.`), there is no console stylesheet, and the document inlines only `UiStylesheet.Css`, whose `.rask-ops`-keyed reset is the console's page base; tables are `Ui.DataGrid` (dead letters tinted with `RowTone`, History's pages as `PageHref` links), a gap the kit cannot draw is a new typed kit step, never a class here. A panel appears ONLY when its battery is BOTH registered (its options singleton resolves) AND mapped (Model.FindEntityType) — the second half catches AddRaskX() without modelBuilder.AddRaskX(), where the service resolves but every query throws. FAILED = `ProcessedAt IS NULL AND Attempts >= MaxAttempts`, the inverse of the processors' drain query (there is no status column). SECURITY IS FAIL-CLOSED: pages carry `[Authorize(Policy = RaskDashboardPolicies.Access)]` on the LAYOUT (RouteAuthorizationGuard walks the chain, so it covers every page + re-checks on in-app nav); the default policy is installed with PostConfigure<AuthorizationOptions> so call order is irrelevant and an app-defined policy always wins — undefined => open in Development (with a banner) and DENY-ALL everywhere else. ACTIONS `o.Actions` (default Safe): retry a dead letter / retry all / purge processed / evict a cache key; `RaskDashboardActions.All` adds delete-a-row and flush-the-cache. Each is ONE ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete with the guard in the WHERE clause (never a tracked entity), so the DB evaluates it at write time and the dashboard can't raise a concurrency exception; the retry guard is the inverse of the drain query, so a row in flight is invisible to it and retry is safe against a live queue with no coordination. Panels poll `RefreshInterval` (2s), compare before re-rendering (idle => no diff, no WS traffic), and the loop is BOUNDED by `MaxPollDuration` (5min, then a Resume button) because every open tab competes for SQLite's single write lock. Backup tiles are opt-in via `IDashboardBackupProbe` — referencing Rask.SQLite.Snapshots/Litestream would drag a native SQLitePCLRaw provider bundle into every consumer and tie a provider-agnostic EF dashboard to SQLite.
- [UI kit](docs/ui-kit.md): Flux UI's navigation in C# (`Ui.Navbar`/`Ui.NavbarItem`, `Ui.Navlist`/`Ui.NavlistItem`/`Ui.NavlistGroup`, `Ui.Brand`, `Ui.Profile`, `Ui.Breadcrumbs`/`Ui.BreadcrumbsItem`, `Ui.Avatar`/`Ui.AvatarGroup` — the current item worked out from the route), and the standalone `Rask.Ui` package — EVERY daisyUI component as a typed Rask component, and what the framework's own surfaces (the `/_rask` console, the landing site, the docs showcase) are drawn with. daisyUI 5 is VENDORED at `Styles/daisyui.mjs` and compiled into the package. Multi-targets every shipped target (`net10.0` and `net10.0-browser`), unlike `Rask.Dashboard` which is server-only because its panels read a DbContext; this is markup and nothing else. ONE COMPONENT PER FILE, named after the type, so the file list in `src/Rask.Ui` is the component list. A component that IS one HTML element derives from `UiElement` (an `Element`). `Ui.Button` is the `<button>`, or the `<a>` given `Href`. `Ui.Button` and `Ui.ButtonGroup` are FLUX UI's button and button.group (fluxui.dev/components/button), NOT daisyUI's: `Variant` is `Ui.ButtonVariant` (Outline = default, Primary, Filled, Danger, Ghost, Subtle), `Size` is `Ui.ButtonSize` (Base, Sm, Xs), `Color` is `Ui.Color` (Tailwind's hues) and each value is a step — `Ui.Button.Primary.Sm.Blue["Save"]`. Icons are PROPS: `Ui.Button.Icon(Ui.IconName.Check)["Save"]`, `IconTrailing`, `IconVariant`; an icon with no children is a square, named with `.AriaLabel("Close")` or a `Tooltip`. Also `Square`, `Align`, `Inset(Ui.Inset.All)`, `Tooltip`/`TooltipPosition`/`TooltipKbd`/`Kbd`, `As`, `Type`, `Disabled`, `Command`/`CommandFor`. Full width is `.Class("w-full")`; a pressed toggle is `.AriaPressed(AriaPressed.True)` on `Filled`. It has NO `Tone`, `Block`, `Wide`, `Circle`, `Active` or `AccessibleLabel`. `Ui.Button.Href` and `Ui.Link.Href` take a RouteUrl: a GENERATED route (it carries its PageType, as `Routes.X()` does) writes `data-rask-nav` plus the deploy PathBase, so the runtime navigates in-app exactly as for NavLink; a plain string stays an ordinary full-document link (right for a URL that leaves the app, wrong for one of your own pages), and NewTab(true) is never intercepted. `Ui.Badge` is FLUX's badge (a `<div>`, or a `<button>` with `.As(Ui.BadgeAs.Button)`; `Color(Ui.Color.Lime)` — Tailwind's 17 hues + 5 grays, unset = zinc, NO `Tone`; `.Sm`/`.Lg`; `.Solid`; `.Rounded()`; `Icon`/`IconTrailing`; `Inset(Ui.Inset.Top | Ui.Inset.Bottom)`; removable = a `Ui.BadgeClose.AriaLabel("Remove").OnClick(…)` child, which like Flux's has no accessible name of its own; `.Button`/`.Div` are NOT steps on it and `.Outline`/`.Mini`/`.Micro` set its ICON variant). `Ui.List` is the `<ul>`, or the numbered `<ol>` with `Ordered(true)`. What they show is CHILDREN, not a Label/Message prop: `Ui.Button["Save"]`, `Ui.Badge.Color(Ui.Color.Green)["Live"]`. A `<button>` WAITING ON ITS OWN HANDLER is marked by the RUNTIME (both hosts, not kit script): after 200 ms it gets `data-loading` + `aria-busy="true"`, a second press is dropped until the first render lands, never `disabled`; `Ui.Button` draws a same-width spinner from it, `Ui.Button.Loading(false)` / `data-rask-loading="off"` (on it or any ancestor) opts out, `Loading(true)` forces it from C#. A square or circle icon-only button names itself with `AccessibleLabel`, and the kit's stylesheet sizes an icon nobody sized from the button or badge it sits in. Every element step (`Id`/`Class`/`Style`/`Data`/`Role`/`Aria`/`Attributes`/events) applies unchanged. The kit adds classes and ARIA through `ResolveClass()`/`ResolveAria()`, and the call site's own values win. `Ui.Table` is FLUX UI's table (fluxui.dev/components/table), part for part: `Ui.Table[Ui.TableColumns[Ui.TableColumn["Order"]], Ui.TableRows[Ui.TableRow.Key(id)[Ui.TableCell["#428"]]]]` — never raw `Thead`/`Tr`/`Td` inside it. It always sits in a scroll area; `Class` lands on the `<table>`, `ContainerClass("max-h-80")` on the box, `Bleed()` runs the dividers through the parent's padding (`--ui-bleed`, 1.5rem by default) and `Paginate(pager)` puts a pager under the rows. `Ui.TableColumns.Sticky()` holds the headings; `Ui.TableColumn` takes `.Start`/`.Center`/`.End`, `Sticky()`, and `Sortable().Sorted(bool).Direction(Ui.TableColumnDirection.Asc|Desc).OnSort(handler)` — the table sorts NOTHING, the page reorders its rows when `OnSort` fires. `Ui.TableCell` takes `.End`, `Sticky()` and `Variant(Ui.TableCellVariant.Strong)`; `py-0` on a cell that holds a badge. `Strong` and `Desc` are also HTML tags, so those two values go through `Variant(…)`/`Direction(…)`, not a bare step. Grouped as daisyUI groups them: actions `Ui.Button`/`Ui.ButtonGroup`/`Ui.Dropdown`/`Ui.Menu`/`Ui.Navmenu`/`Ui.Context`/`Ui.Popover`/`Ui.Modal`/`Ui.ModalTrigger`/`Ui.ModalClose`/`Ui.Swap`/`Ui.Fab`; data display `Ui.Accordion`/`Ui.AccordionItem`/`Ui.AccordionHeading`/`Ui.AccordionContent`/`Ui.Aura`/`Ui.Hover3d`/`Ui.HoverGallery`/`Ui.TextRotate`/`Ui.Avatar`/`Ui.Badge`/`Ui.Card`/`Ui.Carousel`/`Ui.ChatBubble`/`Ui.Countdown`/`Ui.Diff`/`Ui.Empty`/`Ui.Kbd`/`Ui.List`/`Ui.Stat`/`Ui.StatusDot`/`Ui.Table`/`Ui.DataGrid`/`Ui.Timeline`; navigation `Ui.Tabs`/`Ui.Tab`/`Ui.TabGroup`/`Ui.TabPanel`/`Ui.Navbar`/`Ui.NavbarItem`/`Ui.Navlist`/`Ui.NavlistItem`/`Ui.NavlistGroup`/`Ui.Brand`/`Ui.Profile`/`Ui.Breadcrumbs`/`Ui.BreadcrumbsItem`/`Ui.Steps`/`Ui.Pagination`/`Ui.Dock`/`Ui.Link`; feedback `Ui.Callout` (Flux UI's callout, which REPLACES `Ui.Alert`: `Ui.Callout.Danger.Icon(Ui.IconName.XCircle).Heading("Payment failed").Text("…")`, or `Ui.CalloutHeading`/`Ui.CalloutText`/`Ui.CalloutLink` as children; variants `.Secondary`/`.Success`/`.Warning`/`.Danger`, `Color(Ui.Color.Blue)` for any Tailwind hue, `Inline()`, and the `Actions(…)`/`Controls(…)` slots — it writes NO role, so a callout that appears because something happened says `.Role("alert")` or `.Role("status")` at the call site)/`Ui.Loading`/`Ui.Progress`/`Ui.Skeleton`/`Ui.SkeletonLine`/`Ui.SkeletonGroup`/`Ui.Toast`/`Ui.ToastGroup`/`Ui.Tooltip`+`Ui.TooltipContent` (Flux's tooltip: `Ui.Tooltip.Content("Settings").Right[trigger]`, its own `Ui.TooltipPosition` Top/Right/Bottom/Left + `Ui.TooltipAlign` Center/Start/End, `Kbd`, `Gap`, `Offset`, `Disabled`, `Interactive`, `Toggleable()` = opens on a click; the trigger is the first child and is wired `aria-describedby`/`aria-labelledby` at render; no script — a `[popover]` on CSS anchor positioning) (`Ui.Progress` and the skeletons are FLUX UI's, measured from its docs: `Ui.Progress.Value(3).Max(7).Color(Ui.Color.Blue)` is a `<div role="progressbar">` with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemax` as given, the bar their ratio clamped 0–100 and exposed as `--ui-progress`/`--ui-progress-percentage`, named by `.Aria("label", …)`, NO radial progress; `Ui.SkeletonGroup.Shimmer[Ui.Skeleton.Class("size-10 rounded-full"), Ui.SkeletonLine, Ui.SkeletonLine.Lg]` — a block the call site sizes, a text line, and a group whose `Shimmer`/`Pulse` reaches every skeleton inside unless it states its own; `--ui-shimmer-color` is the surface behind it); data input `Ui.Input`/`Ui.InputGroup`/`Ui.InputGroupPrefix`/`Ui.InputGroupSuffix`/`Ui.Textarea`/`Ui.Select`/`Ui.SelectOption`/`Ui.SelectGroup`/`Ui.SelectOptionCreate`/`Ui.SelectOptionEmpty`/`Ui.SelectButton`/`Ui.SelectInput`/`Ui.SelectSearch`/`Ui.FileUpload`/`Ui.FileUploadDropzone`/`Ui.FileItem`/`Ui.FileItemRemove`/`Ui.Checkbox`/`Ui.CheckboxGroup`/`Ui.CheckboxAll`/`Ui.CheckboxIndicator`/`Ui.RadioGroup`/`Ui.Radio`/`Ui.RadioIndicator`/`Ui.Switch`/`Ui.Slider`/`Ui.SliderTick`/`Ui.Rating`/`Ui.Field`/`Ui.Label`/`Ui.Description`/`Ui.Error`/`Ui.Fieldset`/`Ui.Legend`/`Ui.Validator`/`Ui.Otp`/`Ui.OtpInput`/`Ui.OtpSeparator`/`Ui.OtpGroup`/`Ui.Filter`/`Ui.Calendar`/`Ui.DatePicker`/`Ui.DatePickerInput`/`Ui.DatePickerButton`/`Ui.TimePicker`; layout `Ui.Header`/`Ui.Main`/`Ui.Sidebar` and its parts/`Ui.Separator`/`Ui.Footer`/`Ui.Hero`/`Ui.Indicator`/`Ui.Join`/`Ui.Stack`/`Ui.Mask`; mockups `Ui.MockupBrowser`/`Ui.MockupCode`/`Ui.MockupPhone`/`Ui.MockupWindow`; plus the chrome the console uses and `Ui.Icon`/`Ui.IconName`, DARK MODE the way Flux UI does it — `Ui.AppearanceScript` in the head assets puts a `dark` class on `<html>` before first paint from a stored `light`/`dark`/`system` (`localStorage` key `rask.appearance`, system = no key, follows `prefers-color-scheme`), and a control sets `Rask.dark = !Rask.dark` or `Rask.appearance = 'system'` with no C# handler; there is no theme list or theme picker, `Ui.Breakpoint` (Sm/Md/Lg/Xl). A SCREEN DRAWN WITH THE KIT WRITES NO CLASS STRINGS, because a library's class names are ones no app's Tailwind can see — so the layout a console needs is a typed step on the component that owns it: `Ui.MetricRow.Columns(2)`; `Ui.Badge.Mono()` (mono, and it WRAPS a long token instead of widening its row); `Ui.Code.Label("Payload")`; `Ui.Empty.Title(...).Detail(...)` (no border of its own — it sits in a card, a grid's `Empty`, or a page); `Ui.Pagination.Href(page => RouteUrl)` (pages become links, counted from one — see PAGINATION below); `Ui.Main` spaces its sections, so `Ui.Header` carries no margin. THREE INDEPENDENT AXES that compose: `Ui.Tone` (Neutral/Primary/Secondary/Accent/Info/Success/Warning/Error — daisyUI's own words, deliberately, so its docs read straight across), `Ui.Variant` (Solid/Outline/Soft/Dash/Ghost/Link) and `Ui.Size` (Default/Xs/Sm/Md/Lg/Xl), plus `Ui.Position` (the side) + `Ui.Align` (along it) — the ONE placing vocabulary: `Ui.Dropdown` has Flux's own `Ui.DropdownPosition`/`Ui.DropdownAlign`, each member a chain step: `Ui.Dropdown.Top.End`, `Ui.ModalPosition` (Right/Left/Bottom) for the edge a flyout modal opens from, events always `On…` (`Ui.Modal.OnClose`, `Ui.Toast.OnDismiss`), and NO kit component carries an outer margin ("we style, you space") —, `Ui.MaskShape`, `Ui.LoadingShape`, `Ui.SwapAnimation`, `Ui.AuraStyle`. A member a component has NO daisyUI class for writes NOTHING, rather than a class that would sit in the markup looking as though it styled something. THE RULE THE KIT RESTS ON: daisyUI emits a component's CSS only where Tailwind can SEE the class name in scanned source, so a name built by concatenation (`"btn-" + tone`) is absent from the sheet and the component renders WITH NO STYLING AT ALL while the build stays green — which is why every class is a complete literal in `UiClassNames.cs`, why the axes are closed enums, and why `Ui.TextRotate` has no Interval property (daisyUI reads its speed from a `duration-*` utility). ONE STYLESHEET PER APP, AS A FLUX APP HAS: an app with a Tailwind build takes the kit in with one line in `Styles/app.css` — `@import "./vendor/rask-ui.css";` (the first at-rule; it REPLACES `@import "tailwindcss"`, the layer statement and any daisyUI `@plugin` line) — and compiles Tailwind, the kit's `@theme` tokens, its `dark` variant, daisyUI and every class the kit's components write INTO ITS OWN SHEET, beside the classes it writes itself. The build writes `Styles/vendor/` (`rask-ui.css`, `rask-ui.kit.css`, `rask-ui.classes.txt`, `daisyui.mjs`; never committed) and the host links `css/app.css` alone; there is NO csproj switch (`RaskUiTailwind` only overrides the detection). NEVER link the kit's precompiled sheet beside an app's own Tailwind output: two sheets are two `@layer utilities` ranked by link order, so an app's `bg-white` beats the kit's `dark:bg-zinc-800` — `<RaskUiWriteStylesheet>true</RaskUiWriteStylesheet>` in such a project is a BUILD ERROR. The PRECOMPILED sheet (`Styles/ui.precompiled.css` -> `obj/$(TargetFramework)/ui.generated.css`, embedded as `Rask.Ui.ui.css`) is for a surface with NO Tailwind build of its own: linked with `UiStylesheet.Href()` after `<RaskUiWriteStylesheet>true</RaskUiWriteStylesheet>`, or inlined from `UiStylesheet.Css` (`Rask.DevTools`). EITHER WAY put `UiStylesheet.ThemeScopeAttribute` (`data-rask-ui`) on an ancestor (`RaskApp` and the WASM host do) — daisyUI paints `:root` by default and the kit confines it, so merely referencing the package cannot repaint an app that wanted a button, and without it every colour resolves to nothing. The kit carries NO preflight and no html/body rules of its own (an app's comes from Tailwind, through `rask-ui.css`). The ONE reset it ships is the console frame's: Tailwind 4's preflight keyed to `[data-rask-ui-document]` (`UiStylesheet.DocumentAttribute`, which a document drawn with the kit alone writes on `<html>`) inside `:where()` in `@layer base` — so a mounted app drawn with the kit (the `/_rask` console, whose own sheet is the kit compiled without Tailwind's preflight) needs no other reset, and a page without the attribute matches none of it (`UiStylesheetTests` asserts no html/body rule or universal reset lacks it). WHO OWNS THE STATE resolves two ways, decided by what the platform can do: the BROWSER declaratively (`Ui.Modal` is FLUX UI's modal, measured against fluxui.dev open as well as loaded by `scripts/flux/parity-modal.mjs`: `Ui.ModalTrigger.Name("edit")[Ui.Button["Edit"]]` + `Ui.Modal.Name("edit").Class("md:w-96")[content]` is a real MODAL `<dialog>` — the trigger makes the button inside it an invoker (`command="show-modal"`), so there is no handler: top layer, inert page behind, Escape, focus back on the trigger — and what Flux adds in script it asks the RUNTIME's hooks for by attribute: `data-rask-modal="any|press|escape|none"` (a click outside, and which dismissals `Dismissible` x `Escapable` allow, all four combinations), `data-rask-lock="scroll"` (the page held still behind it) and the invoker commands themselves where the engine has none, so NO `popover`/`popovertarget` fallback and NO `closedby` is written; `Ui.ModalClose[Ui.Button["Cancel"]]` closes the modal it is in; `.Flyout()` anchors it to an edge (`.Left`/`.Bottom`, Right by default — this REPLACES `Ui.Drawer`), `.Floating` stands a flyout off the edges, `.Bare` draws no panel, `.Scroll(Ui.ModalScroll.Body)` lets a long one run past the screen, `Dismissible`/`Escapable`/`Closable` switches, `OnClose` for any close and `OnCancel` for a dismissal, `Shortcut("mod+k")` on the trigger, the page scroll locked while open; it has NO Title/Footer/Trigger props — what it holds is children; Flux's `Flux::modal()->show()` / `wire:model` is `Ui.Modal.Open(_open).OnClose(() => _open = false)`, the state-driven path, which is the SAME real modal (the dialog says `data-rask-modal-open` and the runtime calls showModal()/close() to match: top layer, `::backdrop`, Escape and a click outside raising `OnCancel` then `OnClose`) — its `OnClose` MUST clear the field, because the corner button and `Ui.ModalClose` close it in the browser; a modal with neither `Name` nor `Open` is open while the page renders it; `Ui.Fab` opens on :focus-within because daisyUI defines no class to force it), or the PAGE in C# (`Ui.Dropdown`, `Ui.Swap`, `Ui.Tabs`, `Ui.Modal.Open` — and `Open` is NULLABLE with three meanings: unset is uncontrolled, and CLOSED writes `dropdown-close` rather than merely omitting `dropdown-open`, because daisyUI also opens on :focus-within). TABS ARE FLUX UI's (`flux:tab.group`/`flux:tabs`/`flux:tab`/`flux:tab.panel`, same props, same look, same keys): `Ui.TabGroup[Ui.Tabs.Bind(() => Tab)[Ui.Tab.Name("profile")["Profile"], Ui.Tab.Name("account").Icon(Ui.IconName.Cog6Tooth)["Account"]], Ui.TabPanel.Name("profile")[…], Ui.TabPanel.Name("account")[…]]`. The SELECTED TAB IS THE ROW's VALUE (the tab's `Name`; Flux's `wire:model`): `Ui.Tabs.Bind(() => Property)`, or `.Value(x).OnChange(name => …)`, or NEITHER — the row then keeps track itself, starting on the tab that says `Selected()` or else the first not disabled; a tab with no `Name` is known by its place (`"0"`, `"1"`). A tab's LABEL IS ITS CHILDREN (there is no `Label` prop; a count is a child: `Ui.Tab["Open", Ui.Badge["12"]]`). `Ui.Tabs` steps: `.Segmented` / `.Pills` (`Ui.TabsVariant`), `.Size(Ui.TabsSize.Sm)` (segmented only), `.Scrollable()`, `.ScrollableFade()`, `.ScrollableScrollbar(Ui.TabsScrollbar.Hide)`; `Ui.Tab` steps: `Icon`/`IconTrailing`/`IconVariant`, `Selected()`, `Disabled()`, `Accent(false)`, `Action().OnClick(…)` (a plain button in the row — "Add tab" — that selects nothing) — and NO `Href`: a tab is a button, and for full-page navigation Flux says to use the navbar (a row that navigates reads its `OnChange` and calls `Go.To(…)`); `Ui.TabGroup.Findable()` makes hidden panels `hidden="until-found"` so find-in-page reaches them and a match selects its tab. A row needs NO group (a segmented List/Board/Timeline is a choice read from `OnChange`); inside a group write the row BEFORE its panels. Markup: `role="tablist"` over `button role="tab"` with `aria-selected`, roving `tabindex` (only the selected tab is a tab stop, so Tab lands in the `role="tabpanel"`), `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` both ways, `data-ui-tab-group`/`data-ui-tabs`/`data-ui-tab`/`data-ui-tab-panel` and `data-selected`. THE KEYBOARD IS THE RUNTIME's, for ANY `role="tablist"` of buttons: ArrowRight/ArrowDown next, ArrowLeft/ArrowUp previous, past `disabled` tabs and around the ends, and the tab arrived at is focused AND clicked (selection follows focus); Home/End are NOT handled, as in Flux. `Ui.Dropdown[trigger, Ui.Menu[rows]]` is FLUX UI's dropdown exactly (`flux:dropdown` + `flux:menu`): the FIRST CHILD is the trigger (a `Button`, a `Ui.Button` — the dropdown adds `popovertarget` and the ARIA), the second a `Ui.Menu` of actions or a `Ui.Navmenu` of links (`Ui.NavmenuItem.Href(...)` — a typed route navigates in the app, a string is the browser's plain link; without an `Href` the row is a `<button>` and `.OnClick(...)` is what it does; no menu roles, no cursor); `Position` (`.Bottom`/`.Top`/`.Right`/`.Left`), `Align` (`.Start`/`.Center`/`.End`), `Gap`, `Offset`, `Hover()` (Flux's `hover`: opens while the pointer is over the trigger or the menu, with no page lock), and `Open(bool)`/`OnToggle` to own the state (mirrored by the runtime through `data-rask-popover-open`). The menu is a `[popover]` (browser owns open/Escape/click-outside; the page behind does not scroll or take the pointer) with Flux's keyboard in C#: opens with focus on the menu and NO row chosen, either arrow starts at the first row, arrows STOP at the ends and skip disabled rows, NO Home/End, type-ahead, ArrowRight/Enter into and ArrowLeft out of a `Ui.MenuSubmenu.Heading("…")` flyout (one lit row for pointer and keyboard — `data-active`, no `:hover`; Flux's safe area and page lock from the runtime's hooks), Enter/Space pick, Tab closes; the row under the cursor has FOCUS (roving focus, `tabindex="0"`, `data-active`). Rows take their words as CHILDREN: `Ui.MenuItem.Icon(…).Kbd("⌘S").OnClick(Save)["Save"]` (Icon, IconTrailing, IconVariant, Kbd, Suffix, `.Danger`, Disabled, KeepOpen, Href), `Ui.MenuCheckbox.Bind(() => m.Draft)["Draft"]` (or `Value`+`OnChange`), `Ui.MenuRadioGroup.Bind(() => m.Sort)[Ui.MenuRadio.Value("name")["Name"], …]`, `Ui.MenuCheckboxGroup`, `Ui.MenuGroup.Heading("…")`, `Ui.MenuSeparator`; a pick CLOSES the menu (checkboxes too) unless `KeepOpen` is on the menu, a submenu, a radio group or the row; hooks `data-active`/`data-checked`/`data-open`. `Ui.Chart.Value(rows)[Ui.ChartSvg[Ui.ChartLine.Field((Row r) => r.Value), Ui.ChartAxis.X.Field((Row r) => r.Date)[Ui.ChartAxisTick], Ui.ChartAxis.Y[Ui.ChartAxisGrid, Ui.ChartAxisTick], Ui.ChartCursor], Ui.ChartTooltip[...]]` is Flux's chart part by part (line, area, point, bar, group, stack, pie/donut, axis + tick/grid/line/mark, zero-line, cursor, tooltip, summary, legend, viewport), drawn as SVG in C# to the numbers Flux's layout arrives at, with no chart library: the chart takes the typed list and each part a selector whose lambda states the row type (`(Row r) => r.Value`), bare numbers need no field, the drawing FILLS its container (`.Class("aspect-3/1")`, `h-64`) and is drawn again for the box the browser measures — on arrival, 100 ms after a resize settles, when a hidden chart is shown — with NO size to state, as Flux has none: it draws nothing until it has been measured (an empty box of the right size, as Flux's first paint), and a page's charts are all measured in one task and drawn by one render, `UiChartFormat` carries Intl's format options over .NET formatting, and the cursor, the ONE tooltip, `Ui.ChartSummaryValue`s and a pie's `data-active` / `data-inactive` slices follow the pointer in the browser through the runtime's plot hook, with no round trip per move. `Ui.Command.Label("Search commands").Shortcut("mod+k")[Ui.MenuItem.OnClick(…)["New invoice"], …]` is a COMMAND PALETTE: a field that opens a modal `<dialog>` (invoker command, as UiModal) whose search box is a combobox over a listbox of the SAME `Ui.MenuItem`s as options — typing filters in C# (accent/case-insensitive; a non-match is not rendered), arrows move the highlight with focus kept in the box, Enter presses it (handler or link) and closes; runtime hooks `data-rask-shortcut` (clicks its element on the combination; `mod` = ⌘ on Mac / Ctrl elsewhere; also sets `data-rask-mac` on `<html>` so ⌘K vs Ctrl K shows), `data-rask-press-active` (Enter clicks the aria-activedescendant) and `data-rask-close-on-pick`. `Ui.Context[area, Ui.Menu[…]]` (Flux's `flux:context`) is the SAME menu opened by a RIGHT-CLICK on its first child, at the pointer — below it, the menu's END edge on it, as Flux places it; `Position` (`.BottomEnd`/`.BottomStart`/`.TopEnd`…), `Gap`, `Offset((x, y))`, `Target("id")` for a `Ui.Menu.Id("id")` written elsewhere, `Detail`, `Disabled`, `Open`/`OnToggle`: the runtime (`data-rask-contextmenu="<popover id>"`) shows the popover at once on either host, pulls it back inside the viewport, and the ContextMenu key/Shift+F10 open it at the focused element. `Ui.Popover` is the same popover machinery with NO menu semantics (`role="dialog"`, ordinary Tab inside) — for a filter panel or a colour picker, which a `role=menu` would mis-announce as a command list and trap the arrows in.  `Ui.Link.External()` writes target=_blank + rel="noopener noreferrer" (ignored for a generated route, which is your own page); `Ui.Card` IS FLUX UI's CARD (fluxui.dev/components/card), part for part: `Ui.Card[Ui.CardHeader[Ui.CardHeading["Profile"], Ui.CardSubheading[…], Ui.CardActions[Ui.Button[…]]], Ui.CardBody[…], Ui.CardFooter[…]]`, plus `Ui.CardBleed` for media that runs to the card's edges (the card and its body set `--ui-bleed-x`/`--ui-bleed-top`/`--ui-bleed-bottom`/`--ui-bleed-top-radius`/`--ui-bleed-bottom-radius`); `Body` (`Ui.CardBodyVariant`: Seamless/Inset/Flush/Divided/Separated) sets the parts apart, `Variant` (`Ui.CardVariant`: Default/Muted/Soft/Outline/Filled) is the surface, `Size` (`Ui.CardSize`: Md/Xs/Sm/Lg) the padding and corners, `Divider(Ui.CardDivider.Inset)` stops a divided card's lines at the content, `Highlight(false)` drops the top-edge highlight — each value is a chain step (`Ui.Card.Inset.Soft.Lg`); parts are optional (anything straight inside is padded evenly); a header or footer OUTSIDE a card takes its own `Size`, INSIDE a `Ui.CardBody` it is a bare sub-section; `Ui.CardHeading` takes `Size` (Base/Lg/Xl) and `Level` (a `<div>` without one). It has NO `Title`/`Action`/`Icon`/`Href`/`TitleLevel`: a title is a `Ui.CardHeading` in a `Ui.CardHeader`, an action goes in `Ui.CardActions`, and a link card is a link AROUND a card — `A.Href(url)[Ui.Card.Xs.Class("hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:hover:bg-zinc-700")[…]]`. KANBAN (Flux UI's `flux:kanban`, fluxui.dev/components/kanban): `Ui.Kanban[Ui.KanbanColumn[Ui.KanbanColumnHeader.Heading("Planned").Count(4).Actions(Ui.Button.Subtle.Sm.Icon(Ui.IconName.Plus)), Ui.KanbanColumnCards[Ui.KanbanCard.Heading("Fix login")], Ui.KanbanColumnFooter[…]]]` — the header also takes `Subheading`; a card takes `Header`/`Footer` (content above/under its heading) and `.As(Ui.KanbanCardAs.Button).OnClick(…)` to be a pressable `<button>`; children replace the heading (and the header's count). It DRAWS a board and moves nothing, as Flux's does: NO drag, NO drop/sort event, no `Draggable` prop — moving a card is the page changing its own lists (the `DragDrop` primitive is separate); columns are 320px and do not shrink, so wrap a wide board in `Div.Class("overflow-x-auto")`. TOASTS (Flux UI's `flux:toast` + `flux:toast.group`): a toast is RAISED, not placed — `Toast.Info("Saved.")` (Flux::toast('…')), `Toast.Success`/`Toast.Warning`/`Toast.Error` (variant success/warning/danger), then `.Heading("…")`, `.Action("Undo", handler)` or `.Action("View", url)`, `.Link("View invoice", url)`, `.For(1.Second)` (duration), `.UntilDismissed()` (duration 0). `Ui.Toast` in the layout is where they appear (`<flux:toast />`; an app that places none gets the host's, moved with `c.Toasts.At(Ui.ToastPosition.TopEnd).For(8.Seconds)` or `Rask:Toasts:Position`/`Duration`): props `Position` (`Ui.ToastPosition` BottomEnd default/BottomCenter/BottomStart/TopEnd/TopCenter/TopStart — chain steps `Ui.Toast.TopEnd`), `Invert()`, `Class`. ONE AT A TIME on its own (a new toast replaces the one showing); `Ui.ToastGroup[Ui.Toast]` STACKS them (three shown as a deck that opens under the pointer; `.Expanded()` always open; `Position`). The old page-owned `Ui.Toast.Message(…).OnDismiss(…)` and `Ui.Toaster` are GONE. Markup: a native `popover="manual"` host with role=status (every variant — no role=alert), each toast `[data-ui-toast-dialog]` `aria-atomic` with `data-variant`. NO KIT SCRIPT: the runtime shows the popover (`data-rask-popover-open`), presses the toast's `[data-rask-dismiss]` close button after `data-rask-dismiss-after="<ms>"` (paused while the pointer is over it), and Escape presses it for a toast on its own (`data-rask-shortcut="escape"`); an action button shows a spinner while its handler runs (`data-loading`). SHIPS NO JAVASCRIPT (the runtime does). Every control takes a REQUIRED label that becomes the accessible name rather than a placeholder. `Ui.Checkbox`, `Ui.Radio` AND `Ui.Switch` ARE FLUX UI's (fluxui.dev/components/checkbox, /radio, /switch — same parts, props, look and `data-ui-*` markers; no daisyUI class; `Ui.Toggle`, `Tone`/`Size`, `Options(...)`, `Layout(Ui.ChoiceLayout.X)` and `CheckAll()` are GONE): `Ui.Checkbox.Bind(() => m.Agreed).Label("I agree")` binds a `bool` or a `bool?` (null draws the dash), `Ui.Checkbox.Checked(on).OnChange(v => on = v)` is the controlled form, `Indeterminate()`, `Disabled()`, `Invalid()`; `Ui.Switch.Bind(() => m.Alerts).Label("Alerts").Description("…")` / `Ui.Switch.Value(on).OnChange(…)`, `.Left` puts it before its label. THE GROUP IS THE FIELD AND THE CHOICES ARE ITS CHILDREN: `Ui.RadioGroup.Bind(() => m.Plan).Label("Plan")[Ui.Radio.Value(Plan.Free).Label("Free"), Ui.Radio.Value(Plan.Pro).Label("Pro").Description("…")]` binds ONE value of any type (controlled: `.Value(x).OnChange(…)`); `Ui.CheckboxGroup.Bind(() => m.Topics).Label("Topics")[Ui.CheckboxAll.Label("Everything"), Ui.Checkbox.Value("news").Label("News"), …]` binds the collection (`List<T>`/`HashSet<T>`/array; controlled: `.Values(list).OnChange(…)`), written in the order the checkboxes are written; `Ui.CheckboxAll` is ticked for all, a dash (`data-indeterminate`, as Flux marks it — no `aria-checked="mixed"`) for some, and pressing it ticks all unless all are. Variants are enum steps on the GROUP: `.Cards`/`.Pills`/`.Buttons`, plus `.Segmented` (with `.Sm`) and `Indicator(false)` on a radio group; a choice takes `Label`, `Description`, `Icon(Ui.IconName.X)`, `Disabled()`; a card's children replace its label (`Ui.Radio.Value(x)[Ui.RadioIndicator, Div[…]]`, `Ui.CheckboxIndicator`); `Class("flex-col")` stacks cards. Every root is a `<label>` (`data-ui-checkbox`/`-radio`/`-switch`, `…-cards`/`-pills`/`-buttons`/`-segmented`) around a REAL `<input>` that is out of sight (never `hidden`) — a switch is `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, which the runtime also flips on Enter as Flux's does — so space, a click on the label, a radio group's arrow keys (move AND choose, wrapping) and the form post are the browser's, with no script; in a browser test click the label/box (`label:has(> #id)`), not the hidden input. `Id` lands on the `<input>`; a choice's id is `{group id}-{value}`; `Name("notify")` on a checkbox, radio, switch or radio group is the `<input>`'s own `name` (a radio group names its radios after its own id unless its `Name` says otherwise; a `Name` on one radio replaces the group's), and `Attributes(("aria-label", "Select row"))` forwards any other attribute to that `<input>` as Flux forwards it to its control. SLIDER AND OTP ARE FLUX UI's (fluxui.dev/components/slider, /otp-input; `Ui.Range` is GONE): `Ui.Slider.Bind(() => m.Amount).Min(0).Max(100).Step(10)` over int/long/float/double/decimal (generic `UiSlider<T>`); it takes NO `Label` — put it in `Ui.Field[Ui.Label["Volume"], Ui.Slider.Bind(…)]` and every thumb is `aria-labelledby` that label; the value follows the thumb WHILE it moves (`OnChange`/the bound member on every step); `BigStep(100)` is Flux's `big-step` — Shift+Arrow and PageUp/PageDown move by it (`data-rask-big-step` on the range input, stepped by the runtime; unset, the Page keys are the browser's tenth of the track); a RANGE is `Ui.Slider.Bind(() => m.Price).Range()` over an ARRAY of two (`int[] Price = [200, 800]`, a NEW array on every change — `Bind`/`Value` open the chain, `Range()` follows), thumbs never cross, `MinStepsBetween(10)` keeps them apart, a press on the track moves the nearer one; ticks are children — `Ui.SliderTick.Value(3)` (a line), `.Dot`, or `Ui.SliderTick.Value(3)["Mid"]`, under the track or on it with `.Inside` (`Ui.SliderTickPosition`), each `data-active`/`data-current`, pressing one moves the thumb; `TrackClass("h-5")`, `ThumbClass("size-6")` (a `size-N` there also sets `--ui-slider-thumb`), `Disabled()`. Each thumb holds a real `<input type="range">` over the track it can reach, so drag, track press, arrows, Home/End are the browser's. No `Tone`/`Size`/`Vertical`. `Ui.Otp.Bind(() => m.Code).Length(6).Label("OTP Code")` is one real text input per character over a `string`; `Mode` `.Alphanumeric`/`.Alpha` (letters upper-cased in the value; digits by default), `Private()` (password cells), `Autocomplete("off")` (first cell is `one-time-code` otherwise), `Name("code")`, `Disabled()`, `OnComplete(code => …)` runs each time the last cell is filled (it stands where Flux's `submit="auto"` submits the form — the form is NOT submitted for you); lay the cells out yourself with `Ui.Otp.Bind(…)[Ui.OtpGroup[Ui.OtpInput, Ui.OtpInput, Ui.OtpInput], Ui.OtpSeparator, Ui.OtpGroup[…]]` (`Length` is then ignored). The keys are Flux's and the runtime's (`data-rask-otp` on the group): a character moves on to the next cell, type-over replaces, Backspace steps back, arrows stop at the first empty cell, a paste fills from the first cell, fast typing drops nothing. The cells are rendered with NO `value` and NO handler and ONE `<input type="hidden">` in the group carries the code — in a browser test type into the cells and read the hidden field or your own state; set the bound string in C# and the cells follow. REMOVED from `Ui.Otp`: `Joined` (→ `Ui.OtpGroup`), `Tone`, `Size`, `Hint` (→ `DescriptionTrailing`), `Description`, `Badge`, `Invalid` (the bound member's message marks the cells), `AccessibleLabel`, required `Length`. `Ui.Input` AND `Ui.Textarea` ARE FLUX UI's (fluxui.dev/components/input, /textarea — same props, look and `data-ui-*` markers; no daisyUI class): `Ui.Input.Bind(() => m.Email).Label("Email").Description("…")` wraps the input in a `Ui.Field` with its `Ui.Error` (`DescriptionTrailing` under the control; `Badge` on a textarea); with none of them it is the control alone — a wrapper `div[data-ui-input]` (`Class`) around the `input[data-ui-control]` (`InputClass`) — and draws NO message, so place it in a `Ui.Field[…, Ui.Error]`. Props: `Size` (`.Sm`/`.Xs`), `Variant` (`.Filled`), `Disabled()`, `ReadOnly()`, `Invalid()`, `Icon`/`IconTrailing` (a `Ui.IconName` OR a component of your own, e.g. a button), `Kbd("⌘K")`, `Clearable()` (button hidden by CSS while empty), `Viewable()` (password reveal), `Mask("(999) 999-9999")` (9 digit / a letter / * either; applied to the drawn and the committed value, NOT per keystroke), `Type(InputType.File)` + `Multiple()` + `OnFiles` (a `<label>` around the real input, "Choose file" and the chosen name), `As(Ui.InputAs.Button)` + `OnClick` (a button drawn as the input, showing `Placeholder`). `Attributes(("aria-label", "Search keys"))` forwards an attribute to the `<input>` itself, as Flux does (how an input with no `Label` is named); `Copyable()` is Flux's copy button (the runtime writes the clipboard in the click, `data-rask-copy`, and the button shows a tick for 2 s); `Clearable()` clears in the click too (`data-rask-clear`) and `Mask` holds every keystroke to its pattern (`data-rask-mask`); Flux's `mask:dynamic` (an Alpine expression) is NOT built. A bound control is invalid by itself while its form holds a message (`aria-invalid` + `data-invalid` + `aria-describedby`); `ShowValidation(false)` leaves the message to your own `Ui.Error`. `Ui.InputGroup[Ui.InputGroupPrefix["https://"], Ui.Input.Bind(…), Ui.InputGroupSuffix[".com"]]` fuses borders; a non-input neighbour joins with `data-ui-group-target`; for a label put the GROUP in a `Ui.Field`. `Ui.Textarea.Bind(() => m.Notes).Rows(2)` (4 by default; `Rows(UiTextareaRows.Auto)` = CSS `field-sizing: content`) with `Resize`: `.Vertical`/`.Horizontal`/`.Both`/`.None` (`Ui.TextareaResize`). REMOVED with daisyUI's input: `Ui.Search` (→ `Ui.Input.Icon(Ui.IconName.MagnifyingGlass)`), floating labels/`Floating`, `Hint` (→ `Description`), `Tone`/`Error("…")` (→ `Invalid()` + `Ui.Error.Message("…")`), `AccessibleLabel`, `ShowValidating`, `AutoSize`, `Ui.Resize`, daisy `Size`/`Variant` on these two. `Ui.Avatar.Src` is OPTIONAL: given a `Name` it draws the INITIALS as Flux does (first letter of the first and LAST words; the first two letters of a single word) — `Ui.Profile` shares it. `Ui.Select` IS FLUX UI'S `flux:select` (fluxui.dev/components/select), AND ITS OPTIONS ARE CHILDREN: `Ui.Select.Bind(() => m.Country).Label("Country").Placeholder("Choose…")[countries.Select(c => Ui.SelectOption.Key(c.Code).Value(c.Code)[c.Name])]` — an option made from a list needs `.Key(…)` (RASK022), an option with no `Value` stands for its own text (`Ui.SelectOption["Photography"]`), and `Ui.Select.Of<string>()` opens one with no binding and no value. Parts: `Ui.SelectOption` (`Value`/`Label`/`SelectedLabel`/`Keywords`/`Icon`/`IconVariant`/`IconClass`/`Avatar`/`Description`/`Disabled()`, or children of its own), `Ui.SelectGroup.Label("Creative")[…]` (an `<optgroup>`, or a headed run of rows), `Ui.SelectOptionCreate.MinLength(2).OnClick(name => Create(name))["Create new"]` (`OnClick` is a `Callback<string>`: the search as typed), `Ui.SelectOptionEmpty.WhenLoading("Loading projects...")["No projects found."]`, and Flux's three slots as children — `Ui.SelectButton`, `Ui.SelectInput`, `Ui.SelectSearch`. THREE VARIANTS (`Ui.SelectVariant`): Default is the browser's own `<select>` (text-only options, no runtime needed); `.Listbox` is a button over a drawn list (icons, descriptions, avatars, custom content, `Prefix("Compare to")`, `Clearable()`, `Searchable()` — a search field over the options, case- and accent-insensitive over text and `Keywords` — and `Multiple()`); `.Combobox` is a text input that filters. `Filter(false)` leaves the filtering to the page, which answers `Ui.SelectInput.OnInput(text => …)` by rendering the options that match. Also `Size` (`.Sm`/`.Xs`), `Empty("…")`, `SelectedSuffix("industries selected")`, `Clear(Ui.SelectClear.Close)`, `Position`/`Align`, `OptionsClass("min-w-72")`, `Disabled()`, `Invalid()`, `Name`; `Label`/`Description`/`DescriptionTrailing`/`Badge` draw the `Ui.Field` around it (`ShowValidation(false)` leaves the message to a `Ui.Error` elsewhere). The drawn list is a native `popover` placed by CSS anchor positioning, no kit script: trigger `role="combobox"` + `aria-haspopup="listbox"`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`aria-activedescendant`, list `role="listbox"` (`aria-multiselectable` only when multiple), rows `role="option"` + `aria-selected`; a named drawn select posts through hidden inputs. Keyboard as recorded on fluxui.dev: Space/ArrowDown/ArrowUp open on the picked option, arrows stop at either end (no wrap), Home/End/PageUp/PageDown do nothing, Enter picks and closes (multiple: switches the row and stays open), a letter on the CLOSED button picks the next option starting with it; the closed listbox button ignores Enter as Flux's does (`data-rask-listbox-button`) and the page behind an open list is locked (`data-rask-lock`); every list says `aria-multiselectable="true"` as Flux's does. GONE, nothing beyond Flux stayed: `.Options(list)` (→ option children), `Ui.MultiSelect`, `Native()`/`Native(false)` (→ `.Listbox`), `OptionTemplate` (→ the option's children/`Icon`/`Avatar`/`Description`), `OptionGroup` (→ `Ui.SelectGroup`), `OptionDisabled` (→ `Ui.SelectOption.Disabled()`), `Filter((v, text) => …)`/`OnSearch`/`Loading` (→ `Filter(false)`), `EmptyText`/`LoadingText` (→ `Empty`), `SelectAll()`, `Chips(n)`, `Floating`, `Tone`, daisy `Variant`/`Size`, `Hint` (→ `Description`), `AccessibleLabel` (→ `Label`).ALL TWELVE DATA-INPUT CONTROLS ARE `IFormControl<T>`: the chain opens on `Bind` (bound), `Value` (controlled) or `Of<T>()` (controlled, no value yet), and that opening step fixes the value type and the mode together — `Ui.Input.Label("Email")` does NOT compile. Generic where the value type varies (`UiInput<T>`/`UiTextarea<T>`/`UiSelect<T>`/`UiFilter<T>`, and `Ui.Select` is BOTH selects under one name: `UiSelect<T>` holds one answer and `UiSelectMultiple<T>` a collection of them, and the chain builds the second when it is opened on a collection — `Bind` over a `List<T>`/`T[]`/`HashSet<T>` (each gets its own kind back), or `Ui.Select.Values(x).OnChange(…)` beside `Ui.Select.Value(x)` for one — where T is the ELEMENT type. Several answers are the listbox's, as on Flux: write `Ui.Select.Bind(() => m.Tags).Listbox.Multiple()[…]`; a collection left on the native variant throws, and so does `Multiple()` on a select that holds one answer. Its list stays OPEN on a pick and the button shows the one picked label or "N selected". `Ui.Autocomplete` and `Ui.Pillbox` are FLUX UI's autocomplete and pillbox (fluxui.dev/components/autocomplete, /pillbox): `Ui.Autocomplete.Bind(() => m.State).Label("State of residence")[states.Select(s => Ui.AutocompleteItem[s])]` is Flux's input over a list of suggestions — it holds the TEXT (free text allowed; for name-shown/id-stored use `Ui.Select.Combobox`), takes the input's props plus `ContainerClass`, and Escape closes AND empties it; `Ui.Pillbox.Bind(() => m.Tags).Placeholder("Choose tags...")[tags.Select(t => Ui.PillboxOption.Value(t.Id)[t.Name])]` holds a COLLECTION (`Bind` over List<T>/T[]/HashSet<T>, or `Values(…)`+`OnChange`), each answer a removable pill: `.Sm`, `Searchable()`/`SearchPlaceholder`, `.Combobox` (input among the pills; Backspace on empty removes the last pill), `Filter(false)`, parts `Ui.PillboxOption` (`Value`/`Label`/`SelectedLabel`/`Disabled()`/`Filterable(false)`), `Ui.PillboxOptionCreate.MinLength(2).OnClick(name => …)`, `Ui.PillboxOptionEmpty.WhenLoading(…)`, `Ui.PillboxSearch`, `Ui.PillboxTrigger`, `Ui.PillboxInput.Value(search).OnInput(…)`. There is no `Ui.MultiSelect` to type and NO `UiCombobox` either: `.Listbox.Searchable()` and `.Combobox` are it), closed where it does not (`Ui.Checkbox`/`Ui.Switch` over bool, `Ui.Rating` over int, `Ui.Otp` over string). `Ui.Radio` binds nothing: it is a CHILD of `Ui.RadioGroup`, which binds the value; CALENDAR, DATE PICKER, TIME PICKER (Flux UI's `flux:calendar`, `flux:date-picker`, `flux:time-picker`; the old `Label`/`Month`/`OnMonth`/`FirstDay`/`Hint` steps and `Ui.DatePicker.Values` are GONE): Flux's `mode` is the STEP THAT OPENS the control and picks the one binding that mode's type — `Ui.Calendar.Bind(() => m.Day)` (no step = Flux's default, single; `Ui.Calendar.Single` is the same) over `DateOnly`/`DateOnly?` one day (a second click clears it), `Ui.Calendar.Multiple.Bind(() => m.DaysOff)` (or `Ui.Calendar.Multiple.Values([...])`) over a collection of days several, `Ui.Calendar.Range.Bind(() => m.Stay)` (or `Ui.Calendar.Range.Value(new UiDateRange(a, b))`) over `UiDateRange(Start, End)`; a collection or a range handed to the bare `Ui.Calendar`/`Ui.DatePicker` does NOT compile; `Ui.Calendar.Mode(Ui.CalendarMode.Range).Bind(…)` takes the mode as a value, and a mode (or Flux's bare `.Multiple()`) that disagrees with what is bound throws InvalidOperationException at render; the date picker has `Ui.DatePicker.Range.Bind(() => m.Stay)` and `Ui.DatePickerMode { Single, Range }` only; a range is drawn over two months and written only once its second click lands (a click before the start restarts; `Count`, `Contains`, `Between`, `Preset`, `UiDateRange.Of(Ui.DateRangePreset.Last7Days, today)`); an unset one opens with `Ui.Calendar.Value(default(DateOnly))` and keeps the pick itself. Steps: `Min`/`Max`/`Unavailable([..])` (DateOnly), `MinRange`/`MaxRange`, `.Xs`/`.Sm`/`.Lg`/`.Xl`/`.Xxl` (`Ui.CalendarSize`), `StartDay(DayOfWeek.Monday)`, `Months(2)`, `OpenTo(day)`/`ForceOpenTo()`, `Navigation(false)`, `Static()`, `WeekNumbers()`, `FixedWeeks()`, `SelectableHeader()`, `WithToday()`, `Locale("ja-JP")` (the app's culture by default). Markup: `role=grid` per month, `gridcell` tds with `aria-selected` and `data-date`/`data-today`/`data-selected`/`data-start`/`data-end`/`data-in-range`/`data-unavailable`, ONE day button with `tabindex=0`; arrows walk days/weeks and the browser focus goes with the day, PageUp/PageDown/Home/End page a month and drop focus to the page (Flux), none of them scrolls the page (runtime hooks `data-rask-contain-keys`/`data-rask-focus-follows`). `Ui.DatePicker.Bind(() => m.Arrival).Label("Arrival")` is the field: a `role=combobox` button showing "Jan 20, 2026" over the calendar in a native `<dialog popover>` (closes on the pick, or on a range's second click) — `DateOnly`, or `UiDateRange` as `Ui.DatePicker.Range.Bind(…)` (several days are `Ui.Calendar.Multiple`'s); it opens with the focus on the popup, not on a control in it; takes the calendar's steps plus `Type(Ui.DatePickerType.Input)` (month/day/year parts typed as ONE field — the runtime's `data-rask-segments` over one hidden `yyyy-MM-dd` field; everything in the trigger but a part opens the calendar), `Placeholder`, `Size`, `WithConfirmation()`, `WithPresets()`/`Presets([Ui.DateRangePreset.Today, …])` (needs `Min` for `AllTime`), `Trigger(…)` built from `Ui.DatePickerInput.Label("Start")`/`Ui.DatePickerButton`, and `Label`/`Description`/`DescriptionTrailing`/`Badge`/`Invalid()`/`Disabled()`. `Ui.TimePicker.Bind(() => m.At)` is generic over what it binds: `TimeOnly?` (one or none), `TimeOnly` (always one), a collection of `TimeOnly` = several (`Ui.TimePicker.Of<List<TimeOnly>>()` opens one empty); steps `Interval(minutes)` (30), `Min`/`Max`/`OpenTo` (TimeOnly), `Unavailable([new TimeOnly(3,0), new UiTimeRange(new(5,30), new(7,29))])`, `.TwelveHour`/`.TwentyFourHour` (culture's clock by default), `Locale`, `.Type(Ui.TimePickerType.Input)` (hour/minute/AM-PM fields; `.Dropdown(false)` removes the list), `.Sm`/`.Xs`, `Placeholder`, `Clearable()`, `Disabled()`, `Invalid()`, and the field shorthand — a `role=combobox` button over a native `popover` listbox; FILE UPLOAD IS FLUX UI's (fluxui.dev/components/file-upload; `Ui.FileInput` and its `Dropzone()` are GONE — a plain file field is `Ui.Input.Of<string>().Type(InputType.File).Label("Logo").OnFiles(…)`): `Ui.FileUpload.Label("Upload files").Multiple().OnFiles(Keep)[Ui.FileUploadDropzone.Heading("Drop files here or click to browse").Text("JPG, PNG, GIF up to 10MB")]`, then one `Ui.FileItem.Heading(name).Size(bytes).Image(url).Actions(Ui.FileItemRemove.OnClick(Remove))` per file the PAGE kept — `OnFiles` (an `IReadOnlyList<IRaskFile>`, each readable only while the handler runs) stands for Livewire's `wire:model`, and the list is the page's own state. `Ui.FileUpload` takes `Name`/`Multiple()`/`Label`/`Description`/`Error`/`Disabled()` (+ the input's `Accept`) and any children — the dropzone or markup of your own; `Ui.FileUploadDropzone` takes `Heading`/`Text`/`Icon`/`Inline()`/`WithProgress()`; `Ui.FileItem` takes `Heading`/`Text`/`Image`/`Size` (162400 → "159 KB")/`Icon`/`Invalid()`/`Actions`; `Ui.FileItemRemove` takes `OnClick`/`AriaLabel`. It is a `<label>` around a real `<input type=file>`: a click anywhere opens the picker, Space/Enter on the focused input too, NO script; while files are dragged over it the runtime sets `data-dragging` on it (`data-rask-dropzone`) and the input is laid over the whole area so the drop is the browser's own; from the moment files are chosen until `OnFiles` has rendered the runtime writes `data-loading` on the upload (`data-rask-loading`, which the upload asks for) and the dropzone shows a spinner, or with `WithProgress()` a bar reading `--ui-file-upload-progress` / `--ui-file-upload-progress-as-string`, which the kit's sheet fills from the runtime's `--rask-progress` pair (`0%` at rest) — the upload request's own progress on the Server host, what the handler has READ through `OpenReadStream` in a WebAssembly app (`0%` if it never opens the files). The field's label is a `<label for>` (a click on it opens the picker, as on Flux) and names the input through `aria-labelledby`. Write the remove handler in the component that holds the list (`OnClick(() => _photos.RemoveAt(index))`): a handler re-renders the component it closes over. The `Ui` prefix is load-bearing, not decorative: in a markup host a bare `X` is the chain's entry for `X`, so `Shell` would collide with `Component.Shell` and `Nav`/`Main`/`Button`/`Select`/`Search` with the HTML tags, and RASK040 then gives NEITHER type an entry across the whole compilation. The NAMESPACE has the same hazard from the other side: `Rask.Ui` is an enclosing namespace of every `Rask.*` compilation, so a type of your own named `Ui` under a `Rask.`-rooted namespace is shadowed by it. Live at `/docs/ui/actions`, `/docs/ui/data-display`, `/docs/ui/navigation`, `/docs/ui/feedback`, `/docs/ui/data-input`, `/docs/ui/layout`. EVERY `rask new` PROJECT ARRIVES WIRED FOR IT: `RaskUiWriteStylesheet=true` plus `RaskUiWriteDaisyUiPlugin=true` in the csproj, and RaskApp and the WASM host write the rest into every document so `App.cs` is only a `Title` and `Render() => Router`: charset + viewport, the kit's sheet FIRST (it declares the `@layer` order for the whole document), the app's `css/app.css` (Rask.Tailwind records it as the assembly's `Rask.Stylesheet` metadata), and `UiStylesheet.ThemeScopeAttribute` on `<html>` through the default `Shell`. `app.Configure(c => c.Ui.Off())` / `host.Configure(c => c.Ui.Off())` leaves the kit out; a hand-wired `AddRask()`/`MapRask<App>()` host and an App that overrides `Shell` write their own. THE PACKAGE ALSO SHIPS daisyUI's PLUGIN BUNDLE (`build/daisyui.mjs`), because the kit's prebuilt sheet carries only the classes the kit's OWN components write — an app writing `card-body` in its own markup gets a correct-looking class naming a rule that exists nowhere. `RaskUiWriteDaisyUiPlugin` copies the bundle beside `Styles/app.css`, which loads it as `@plugin "./vendor/daisyui.mjs"` with `@source not "./vendor"` beside it (the bundle names every daisyUI class, so scanned it is a safelist for the whole library) — no npm, no node_modules, because the standalone Tailwind engine carries no package tree and cannot resolve `@plugin "daisyui"` the Node way. The vendored version is pinned by `DaisyUiVersionPinTests`. An app that references the kit AND compiles its own daisyUI carries two copies — its own at `:root`, the kit's confined to `[data-rask-ui]`; they do not conflict. ALL THREE TEMPLATES (`server`, `wasm`, `wasm-hosted`) DRAW THE SAME STARTER: navbar / hero / card / footer, in identical daisyUI class names. The sign-in pages (`/login`, `/register`, recovery) are SCAFFOLDED by `rask new` into `Features/Auth/` as ordinary app components, so the app's own Tailwind compiles their daisyUI classes; `Rask.Auth` ships no pages and no stylesheet. APPLICATION LAYOUT (Flux UI's two layouts, fluxui.dev/layouts/header and /layouts/sidebar, part for part): `Ui.Header`, `Ui.Sidebar` and `Ui.Main` are SIBLINGS — `[Ui.Sidebar.Sticky().Collapsible(Ui.SidebarCollapsible.Always)[Ui.SidebarHeader[Ui.SidebarBrand.Name("Acme").Href(url), Ui.SidebarCollapse], Ui.SidebarSearch.Placeholder("Search..."), Ui.SidebarNav[Ui.SidebarItem.Icon(Ui.IconName.Home).Href(url)["Home"], Ui.SidebarGroup.Expandable().Heading("Favorites")[...]], Ui.SidebarSpacer, Ui.SidebarProfile.Name("Olivia")], Ui.Header[Ui.SidebarToggle, Ui.Spacer], Ui.Main[Main[Outlet]]]` (`Ui.Main` is Flux's `<div>`; the `<main>` landmark goes inside; one sidebar a page) — and whatever holds the `Ui.Main` (the body, or a wrapper) is the layout grid; a header written before the sidebar runs above it, after it sits beside it. `Collapsible`: `Never` (default) · `Mobile` (slides over the page below `Breakpoint`, default `Lg`) · `Always` (also narrows to a 56px rail of icons). NO SCRIPT: each state is a checkbox in the sidebar and each control a `label[role=button]` the runtime presses on Enter/Space; NEITHER state is a prop (Flux has none): the runtime puts the overlay away on navigation (`data-rask-uncheck-on-navigate`) and remembers the rail in `localStorage` under Flux's key `flux-sidebar-collapsed-desktop` (`data-rask-persist`; `Persist(false)` = Flux's `persist="false"`; a WASM app adds `Ui.SidebarScript` to its head assets so the rail is restored before first paint). `Ui.SidebarProfile` draws `Ui.Avatar` and is a dropdown's trigger: `Ui.Dropdown.Top.Start[Ui.SidebarProfile.Name("Ada"), Ui.Menu[...]]` (so are `Ui.Profile`, a `Ui.NavbarItem` without `Href` and `Ui.Avatar.As(Ui.AvatarAs.Button)`). `Ui.SidebarItem` is a NavLink (`Current` auto from the route → `aria-current="page"`, or stated; `Icon`, `Badge`, `Tooltip`; children are the label); `Ui.SidebarGroup` is a heading or a `<details>` (`Expandable`/`Expanded`/`OnToggle`, `Icon`); `Ui.Main` takes `Container`/`Inset`, `Ui.Header` `Sticky`/`Container`; the ground and borders are YOUR classes (a kit-only document writes `UiStylesheet.DocumentAttribute` on `<html>` instead). `Ui.Shell`, `Ui.TopBar`, `Ui.SidebarFooter` and the page-heading `Ui.Header.Title(...)` are GONE. Outside a sidebar the navigation is `Ui.Navlist` (Flux's navlist: a `<nav>`), `Ui.NavlistItem` and `Ui.NavbarItem` (words are the children: `Ui.NavlistItem.Href(Routes.X())["Orders"]`; a NavLink, so `Current` is auto from the route for a generated link → `aria-current="page"`, stated for a string href or a whole section; `Icon`, `Badge`/`BadgeColor` (a `Ui.Color`), `Accent(false)`), `Ui.NavlistGroup` (`Heading`, or a `<details>` with `Expandable`/`Expanded`/`OnExpandedChange`), `Ui.Navbar` (the row for a header), `Ui.Brand` (`Name`, `Logo` = image URL or content, `Href` default `/`), `Ui.Profile` (a button: `Name`, `Avatar`, `Circle`, `Chevron`), `Ui.Breadcrumbs[Ui.BreadcrumbsItem.Href(u)["Home"], Ui.BreadcrumbsItem["Post"]]`, `Ui.Avatar` (`Src` or initials from `Name`, `Xs`/`Sm`/`Lg`/`Xl`, `Circle`, `Color`/`ColorAuto`, `Badge`, `Tooltip`, `Href`) and `Ui.AvatarGroup`; `Ui.Spacer` (flex-1); `Ui.Separator` is Flux's separator (`Vertical()`, `Text("or")`, `.Subtle`, `Orientation`; `role="none"`, NO outer margin — `Ui.Divider` is gone); `Ui.Heading`, `Ui.Text` and `Ui.Link` are FLUX UI's `flux:heading`/`flux:text`/`flux:link` exactly (props, look, markup; zinc + accent, not daisyUI; each ONE element marked `data-ui-heading`/`data-ui-text`/`data-ui-link`): `Ui.Heading` takes `Size` (`Ui.HeadingSize` Base 14px/Lg 16px/Xl 24px/Xxl 36px = Flux's 2xl), `Level` 1-6 (`<div>` without one) and `Accent()`; `Ui.Text` takes `Size` (`Ui.TextSize` Sm/Default/Lg/Xl), `Variant` (`Ui.TextVariant` Default/Strong/Subtle), `Color` (`Ui.Color`, the 17 chromatic hues of Tailwind's 22; wins over the variant, and a neutral one is the variant's own ink) and `Inline()` (`<span>` instead of `<p>`); `Ui.Link` takes `Href` (RouteUrl), `Variant` (`Ui.LinkVariant` Default underlined/Ghost on hover/Subtle), `External()`, `As` (`Ui.LinkAs` A/Button — `Ui.Link.As(Ui.LinkAs.Button).OnClick(...)` is a `<button type="button">`) and `Accent(false)`; every value is also a step (`Ui.Heading.Xl`, `Ui.Text.Subtle`, `Ui.Link.Ghost`) EXCEPT the three that are also HTML tags — write `Variant(Ui.TextVariant.Strong)` and `As(Ui.LinkAs.Button)`, since `.Strong`/`.Button`/`.A` on a component is the inherited tag entry (CS0176); there is NO `Ui.Subheading` — the line under a heading is a `Ui.Text`. `NavLink` itself now writes `aria-current="page"` when active (empty `ActiveClass` opts out). `Ui.Highlight.Text(value)` renders Rask.Data FullText.Highlight/Snippet output: encoded text with each match (between U+E000 and U+E001) wrapped in <mark> — never raw HTML. FIELDS ARE FLUX UI's (the first family rebuilt on Flux, no daisyUI class): `Ui.Field[Ui.Label.Badge("Required")["Email"], Ui.Input.Bind(() => m.Email).ShowValidation(false), Ui.Error, Ui.Description["…"]]`; `Ui.Field.Inline` puts the label beside a checkbox or switch; `Ui.Label` is a real `<label for>` that inside a field points at the field's control (a kit control by its derived id, a plain element by its `Id`; `For(id)` outside one), with `Badge` and a `Trailing` slot; `Ui.Description` sits under the label when before the control and under the control when after it; `Ui.Error` is an always-rendered `role="alert"` live region, hidden until there is a message, that shows the FIRST message of a bound member — bare inside a field (the control's `Bind`), `For(() => m.Email)` anywhere, `Name("Email")` for a member of the form's model, `Message("…")` for your own text, `Icon(Ui.IconName.InformationCircle)`/`Icon(false)`; `Ui.Fieldset.Legend("…").Description("…")` is a real `<fieldset>`/`<legend>`, or place `Ui.Legend` yourself. `Ui.Fieldset.Text`/`Help` and the old daisyUI `Ui.Label.Text` are gone. Markers `data-ui-field|label|description|error|fieldset|legend` mirror Flux's `data-flux-*`. ACCORDION (Flux UI's `flux:accordion`; `Ui.Collapse`, `Ui.AccordionSection` and `Ui.Marker` are GONE): `Ui.Accordion[Ui.AccordionItem.Heading("Where do you ship?")["…"], …]`, or the two parts `Ui.AccordionHeading[…]` + `Ui.AccordionContent[…]` inside an item; steps `Ui.Accordion.Exclusive()` (one open at a time), `.Transition()` (250 ms height), `.Reverse` (chevron before the heading, `Ui.AccordionVariant`), `Ui.AccordionItem.Expanded()` / `.Disabled()`. An item is a native `<details>` and its heading the `<summary>`, so it opens on click/Enter/Space with NO handler and NO script, `Exclusive()` is the browser's own `<details name>` group, and find-in-page opens the item holding a match. To own an item from C#: `.Expanded(_open).OnToggle(open => _open = open)` (`Callback<bool>`, the state it is now in; the browser toggles first and reports). A single collapsible section is a one-item `Ui.Accordion`. ICONS (Flux UI's `flux:icon`): `Ui.Icon.Name(Ui.IconName.ArrowDownTray)` draws any Heroicon — `Ui.IconName` is ALL of Heroicons under Heroicons' own names in PascalCase (`x-mark` → `XMark`, `magnifying-glass` → `MagnifyingGlass`, `exclamation-triangle` → `ExclamationTriangle`; the kit's old names `Close`/`Search`/`Warning`/`Gear` are GONE), plus `Loading` (Flux's spinner); `.Solid`/`.Mini`/`.Micro` pick the variant (`Ui.IconVariant`; default outline 24px, solid 24px, mini 20px, micro 16px); `.Class("size-8 text-amber-500")` overrides size and colour. `Ui.Editor` is Flux's rich text editor (Tiptap): `Ui.Editor.Bind(() => post.Body).Label("Notes")`, value = HTML string, `.Toolbar("heading | bold italic | link ~ undo redo")`, parts `Ui.EditorToolbar[Ui.EditorBold, Ui.EditorSpacer, Ui.EditorButton.Icon(…).OnClick(…)]` + `Ui.EditorContent`; needs NO setting: the app's build writes the engine to wwwroot/js/rask-ui-editor.js and only a page that mounts an editor fetches it; sanitize the HTML before storing or rendering it. PAGINATION (Flux UI's `flux:pagination`): `Ui.Pagination.Paginator(new UiPaginator { Page = page, PerPage = 15, Total = total }).OnPage(p => …)` — `UiPaginator` stands in for Laravel's paginator object (`Page` counted from one, `PerPage` default 15, `Total`); it draws "Showing 16 to 30 of 240 results" plus Previous/Next and numbered pages (all below 14 pages; from 14 the first two, the last two and the current page ±3 with `...` gaps, ten pages held against either end), and the numbers appear only once the pager's OWN box is 640px wide (a container query) — narrower it is Previous/Next alone, 32px targets below `sm`; leave `Total` unset for the SIMPLE paginator (no summary, no numbers; `HasMore` says whether Next leads anywhere); `OnPage` (a `Callback<int>`) makes pages buttons, `Href(page => RouteUrl)` makes them links and wins when both are given — page-in-the-QUERY-STRING is `Href`: a generated route (`Routes.LogsPage(Page: page)`, or `route with { QueryString = $"?page={page}" }`) is an in-app `NavLink` under the app's path base, a STRING (`$"/logs?page={page}"`) is a plain `<a>` written as given; SERVER-SIDE paging = fetch one page + the count yourself and pass `Page`/`PerPage`/`Total`; there is NO page-size prop (Flux has none): put a `Ui.Select.Value(perPage).OnChange(…)` beside the pager and reset `Page` to 1; under a table it is `Ui.Table.Paginate(Ui.Pagination.Paginator(p).OnPage(…))`; the current page is a `<div aria-current="page">` and a gap says `aria-disabled="true"`; ARIA is Flux's live DOM — a COUNTED pager's arrows are labelled `&laquo; Previous` / `Next &raquo;` (entity as text) and a spent one is a `<div aria-disabled="true">`, the SIMPLE pager's arrows have NO `aria-label` and its spent one is a bare `<div>`; `ScrollTo("body" | "#table")` writes `data-rask-scroll-to`, a generic runtime hook that scrolls that selector into view on a press inside the pager. `Ui.DataGrid` draws this pager under its rows. `Pages`/`Current` are GONE. TIMELINE (Flux UI's `flux:timeline`): `Ui.Timeline[Ui.TimelineItem[Ui.TimelineIndicator[icon or "1"], Ui.TimelineContent[…]]]` is an `<ol>`; `Ui.Timeline.Horizontal()`, `.Lg` (`Ui.TimelineSize`), `.Start`/`.Baseline`/`.Center`/`.End` (`Ui.TimelineAlign`, also per item); `Ui.TimelineItem.Complete`/`.Current`/`.Incomplete` (`Ui.TimelineStatus` — a complete item darkens the line on to the next); `Ui.TimelineIndicator.Color(Ui.Color.Green)` (the 17 chromatic hues; a status is drawn instead), `.Bare` (no circle, for a larger icon), `.Status(…)` (overrides the item's); `Ui.TimelineBlock` is a full-width card as an item and `Ui.TimelineSubgrid` inside it puts its first child in the indicator column and its second in the content column; spacing is `--ui-timeline-item-gap` / `--ui-timeline-content-gap` set from `Class`; baseline alignment reads the indicator's hidden first line, `[data-ui-timeline-baseline]`. `Ui.Timeline.Vertical` is GONE (vertical is the default).
- [Background jobs](docs/jobs.md): the `Rask.Jobs` package (in `Rask.Server`, on by default) — durable background work on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis).
