A job is an `IJob` (: Rask.Cqrs ICommand), enqueued with `Jobs.Enqueue`, run off the request thread by an ordinary `ICommandHandler<TJob>`. `await Jobs.Enqueue(job)` (run asap) / `.In(24.Hours)` / `.At(runAt)` (delayed), with `IJobs` injectable where there is no ambient scope — writes one `Job` row (Type name + JSON payload + RunAt) via IDbContextFactory (its OWN transaction — not atomic with a business change; use Rask.Outbox for that). The hosted `JobProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due jobs (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), dispatches each via IDispatcher.Send((ICommand)job) in a fresh scope, stamps ProcessedAt; on failure Attempts++/Error and pushes RunAt out by exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped at MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 25) → then a dead letter kept for inspection; completed jobs purged after Retention (default 7d, Zero=keep). Durable interval-recurring: `o.Run<T>().Every(1.Hour)` / `.Daily.At(3, 0)` / `.Weekly.On(DayOfWeek.Monday).At(9, 0)` enqueues a fresh job per interval, tracked in a RecurringJobState table so a restart never double-runs it (single catch-up if overdue); read the schedule back from `JobsOptions.RecurringJobs` (public `RecurringJob` Name/Interval/Factory) and join it to RecurringJobState for last-fired, or call Factory() to enqueue an off-schedule run. Each job's outcome is saved on its OWN SaveChanges (not once per batch), so a row edited/deleted underneath the drain costs that one row instead of re-running everything the batch already executed; a failing poll is logged and retried rather than faulting the BackgroundService (which would stop the host). A source generator registers each IJob type (name→Type) at module load for reflection-free rehydration. `RaskApp` wires this (settings: `c.Jobs.Configure(o => …)`). Hand-wired: `services.AddRaskCqrs()` + `services.AddRaskJobs<AppDbContext>(o => { PollInterval; MaxAttempts; Run<T>().Every(...); })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskJobs()` in OnModelCreating (maps Job + RecurringJobState) + `rask db add AddJobs && rask db update`. Server-side. MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE: each processor LEASES the batch it claims — one UPDATE whose predicate re-tests claimability (portable, no SKIP LOCKED, no raw SQL), marking rows with a token + expiry (LeaseDuration, default 5m, must exceed PollInterval). A dead instance's lease simply expires and the work is claimable again — no sweeper. A lease stops one instance overwriting another's outcome; it does NOT make a side effect happen once (an instance overrunning its lease can have its row taken, and an email already sent is out) — at-least-once remains the contract. Attempts now counts attempts STARTED, not failures (the claim increments it), so a job that kills the process still reaches MaxAttempts; a first-time success shows Attempts=1. UPGRADING NEEDS A MIGRATION: `rask db add AddLeases && rask db update` — skip it and the processors throw every poll inside a catch, so the app looks healthy while doing nothing (they detect this case and log the two commands). The tutorial writes the `IJob` record + handler. **THE POLL DOES NOT LOG ITS SQL**: EF Core logs every command at `Information`, and three batteries polling every 5s means an idle app's console is nothing but their claim queries, so the processor's claim/lease/complete/purge (and the mail, outbox, cache-purge, orphan-sweep and session-sweep equivalents, and the log store's own INSERT) run on a context that logs `CommandExecuted` at `Debug` instead — rebuilt from the `DbContextOptions<TContext>` the app registered, lazily, because the outbox can be registered BEFORE the context factory (a hand-wired `Program.cs` calling `AddRaskOutbox` ahead of `AddDbContextFactory`). **The application's own queries are untouched** (turning the `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command` category down in appsettings would have hidden those too, which is the thing worth reading); set that category to `Debug` to watch a battery claim its batch. An app with a hand-written `IDbContextFactory<T>`, or a context that cannot be constructed from options alone, keeps its own factory and its old logging — noisy but correct beats quiet but wrong.
- [Transactional email](docs/mail.md): the `Rask.Mail` package (in `Rask.Server`, on by default) — durable transactional email queued on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Compose with a fluent `Email` builder (`Email.To(addr,name?).AndTo/.Cc/.Bcc/.ReplyTo/.From/.Subject/.Body(Component|string html)/.PlainText/.Attach`); `.Body(Component)` renders a Rask component to HTML IMMEDIATELY (Component.ToHtml()) so the persisted row is self-contained (no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency — nothing is rehydrated at send time). Addresses are validated at the call site (MimeKit MailboxAddress.TryParse) so a malformed address throws on build, not after MaxAttempts. `await Mail.Send(email)` (asap) / `.In(24.Hours)` / `.At(runAt)` (delayed), with `IMail` injectable where there is no ambient scope — writes one `QueuedMail` row (envelope + already-rendered HTML) via IDbContextFactory, defaulting From from MailOptions. The hosted `MailProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due messages (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), delivers each via the registered `IMailSender` resolved per message from a fresh scope (so a custom scoped sender isn't captured), stamps ProcessedAt PER MESSAGE (a save failure re-sends at most that one, never the batch); on failure Attempts++/Error + exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 10) → dead letter; a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per cycle so it never faults the host; sent rows purged after Retention (default 7d) via ExecuteDeleteAsync. `IMailSender` selection in AddRaskMail: `MailOptions.Smtp` set → `MailKitSender` (SMTP via MailKit); else `PickupDirectory` set → `PickupDirectoryMailSender` (writes .eml files); else `LogMailSender` — so it works ZERO-CONFIG in dev with no SMTP. Register your own IMailSender before AddRaskMail (any lifetime) to send via a provider API. `RaskApp` wires this (settings: `c.Mail.Configure(o => …)`). Hand-wired: `services.AddRaskMail<AppDbContext>()` reading `Rask:Mail` (`From`, `PickupDirectory`, `Smtp:{Host,Port,User,Password,Security}` — any `Rask:Mail:Smtp` key turns SMTP on, and the password belongs in `Rask__Mail__Smtp__Password` — `PollInterval`, `MaxAttempts`; an optional callback runs after the section and wins) + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskMail()` in OnModelCreating (maps QueuedMail) + `rask db add AddMail && rask db update`. References Rask.Core (Component.ToHtml) with PrivateAssets=all + MailKit; server-side; self-contained (no Rask.Jobs dependency). MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE: each processor LEASES the batch it claims — one UPDATE whose predicate re-tests claimability (portable, no SKIP LOCKED, no raw SQL), marking rows with a token + expiry (LeaseDuration, default 5m, must exceed PollInterval). A dead instance's lease simply expires and the work is claimable again — no sweeper. A lease stops one instance overwriting another's outcome; it does NOT make a side effect happen once (an instance overrunning its lease can have its row taken, and an email already sent is out) — at-least-once remains the contract. Attempts now counts attempts STARTED, not failures (the claim increments it), so a job that kills the process still reaches MaxAttempts; a first-time success shows Attempts=1. UPGRADING NEEDS A MIGRATION: `rask db add AddLeases && rask db update` — skip it and the processors throw every poll inside a catch, so the app looks healthy while doing nothing (they detect this case and log the two commands). An email body is a Rask component; `RaskApp` registers the battery and `RaskAppDbContext` maps `QueuedMail`, leaving only SMTP config.
- [Cache](docs/cache.md): the `Rask.Cache` package (in `Rask.Server`, on by default) — a developer-facing cache on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Implements the standard `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Distributed.IDistributedCache` (Get/Set/Refresh/Remove + sync/async, `DistributedCacheEntryOptions` absolute/AbsoluteRelativeToNow/sliding) via `RaskDistributedCache<TContext>` — stores one `CacheEntry` row per key (Key PK, Value byte[], AbsoluteExpiration?, SlidingSeconds?, effective ExpiresAt, CreatedAt) through IDbContextFactory; a read past ExpiresAt is a MISS + lazily evicted, a read of a sliding entry RENEWS ExpiresAt (capped by any absolute deadline). Plus a typed `ICache` with a static `Cache` facade over it: `await Cache.Remember(key, load).For(10.Minutes)` / `.Sliding(20.Minutes)` / `.Until(moment)` (the loader runs once on a miss — not a lock, keep it idempotent), `Cache.Get<T>(key)`, `await Cache.Set(key, value).For(...)`, `Cache.Forget(key)`, serializing T with System.Text.Json; the steps are awaitable builders that do NOTHING until awaited, and the reflection path is `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`/`[RequiresDynamicCode]` — name a source-generated context once with `o.Json = AppJson.Default` and every call stays as written (the byte[] IDistributedCache surface is fully trim-safe). The hosted `CachePurger<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer) bulk-deletes rows past ExpiresAt on PurgeInterval (default 5min) via ExecuteDeleteAsync — a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per sweep so it never faults the host. `RaskApp` wires this (settings: `c.Cache.Configure(o => …)`). Hand-wired: `services.AddRaskCache<AppDbContext>(o => { o.PurgeInterval; o.DefaultSlidingExpiration; })` (registers IDistributedCache + ICache + the purger, idempotent) + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskCache()` in OnModelCreating (maps CacheEntry) + `rask db add AddCache && rask db update`. Server-side; one purger per app; no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency. Drops into ASP.NET session state (`AddSession()`) and anything else built on IDistributedCache. No per-instance artifact to scaffold. REDIS: `ICache` works over ANY IDistributedCache — `services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(...)` then the NON-GENERIC `services.AddRaskCache()` (no <TContext>), which registers ONLY ICache: no purger, no CacheEntry table, no migration. It takes NO CacheOptions on purpose — PurgeInterval and DefaultSlidingExpiration are implemented by the EF store, so against Redis they would silently do nothing; expiry is the store's business. There is deliberately NO Rask.Caching.Redis package (Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis is the standard API). Only the cache moves — jobs, mail and the outbox stay on the database because they need transactions.
- [File storage](docs/file-storage.md): the `Rask.Storage` package (ON in `Rask.Server` — `c.Storage.Off()` / `c.Storage.Configure(o => …)`; `rask new --no-storage` leaves it out) — files users upload, kept as bytes in a store (Disk by default, S3-compatible, or Azure Blob) PLUS a `StoredFile` row on the app's own database (Id, Name = sanitized display leaf, ContentType SNIFFED from the bytes, Size, Sha256 hex, Provider, Key, Public, CreatedAt UTC). Server-only (no browser face), never in the browser — but on both templates with an ASP.NET host, `server` and `wasm-hosted` (Rask.Storage references no Rask.Core). `await Files.Save(file.OpenReadStream, file.Name, file.Size).Public()` (`IFiles` injectable where there is no ambient scope) for a picked `IRaskFile` (pass the opener as a METHOD GROUP — storage calls it with its own MaxFileSize as the limit; calling `OpenReadStream()` yourself gets IRaskFile's 512 KB default cap; there is NO `Save(IRaskFile)` overload) or `Files.Save(Stream, name)`, `Files.Get`, `Files.OpenRead`, `Files.Delete` (row first, then bytes), `Url(id)` (NO I/O, safe inside Render; public files only — `{PathBase}/_rask/files/public/{id}` served by the app with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, or `PublicBaseUrl + key`; a private file answers 404; buckets stay private, no object ACLs), `await Files.Share(id).For(5.Minutes)` (any file, lifetime > 0 and ≤ 7 days, null when missing; on S3 and on Azure with an account key it is the PROVIDER's signed URL — straight from the bucket and it CANNOT be revoked before it expires; on disk and SAS-only Azure it is a Data Protection-sealed app route `/_rask/files/{token}` carrying only the id, dead the moment the file is deleted, and expired/tampered/unknown/deleted all answer one identical 404; several instances need a shared key ring, which Rask persists to `/data/keys`), `Download(id)` (an IResult for YOUR endpoint after YOUR authorization check: `app.MapGet("/invoices/{id:guid}", async (Guid id, IFiles files, …) => await CanSee(id) ? files.Download(id) : Results.Forbid())`; 404 when missing; Range, If-None-Match, HEAD). Hand-wired: `builder.Services.AddRaskStorage<AppDbContext>(o => …)` + `modelBuilder.AddRaskStorage()` in OnModelCreating + `rask db add AddStorage && rask db update` + `app.MapRaskStorage()` AFTER `app.MapRask<App>()` (it reads the path base; returns IEndpointConventionBuilder, so `.RequireRateLimiting("files")` chains; the routes AllowAnonymous because the public flag or the token IS the authorization). Missing `modelBuilder.AddRaskStorage()` fails the boot naming the line; a bad config value fails the boot; forgetting `MapRaskStorage()` logs a startup warning. Configuration under `Rask:Storage` like every Rask area (`"Rask": { "Storage": { "Provider": "S3" } }`; the old top-level `Storage` section / `Storage__*` variables are NO LONGER READ; precedence defaults → configuration → the `AddRaskStorage(o => …)` callback → validation at host start, a bad value failing the start naming `Rask:Storage`; every public StorageOptions property binds, incl. `OrphanGracePeriod`, `SweepInterval`, `AllowedTypes`): `Rask__Storage__Provider` (Disk/S3/Azure), `Rask__Storage__MaxFileSize` (52428800), `Rask__Storage__PublicBaseUrl` (absolute https; http only for localhost), `Rask__Storage__Prefix` (`myapp/`, so one bucket holds several apps), `Rask__Storage__Disk__Root` (`/data/files` when the /data deploy volume exists, else `storage/` under the content root; inside wwwroot is REFUSED), `Rask__Storage__S3__{ServiceUrl,Bucket,Region,AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken,UsePathStyle}` (Region default us-east-1, R2 wants `auto`; UsePathStyle default true, R2/MinIO need it; AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Google Cloud Storage via HMAC interop keys), `Rask__Storage__Azure__{ConnectionString,Container}` (AccountName+AccountKey enables provider-signed temporary URLs; `BlobEndpoint=…;SharedAccessSignature=…` is SAS-only so temporary URLs go through the app route; `UseDevelopmentStorage=true` is Azurite). NO cloud SDK: SigV4, Shared Key and service SAS are computed in-process. Secrets via `rask deploy --env Rask:Storage:S3:SecretAccessKey=…`. VALIDATION: the browser's claimed type is IGNORED; sniffing uses magic numbers, WHATWG markup patterns and UTF-8 text; a file extension may only NARROW a sniffed family (text→csv/markdown/json, zip→docx/xlsx/pptx), never promote. `AllowedTypes` ("type/subtype" or "type/*", empty = any) match the sniffed type. Only raster images (png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif), audio (mpeg, aac, ogg, wav, flac, mp4) and video (mp4, quicktime, webm) are served inline; everything else is an attachment, and HTML, SVG and XML are sent as application/octet-stream. Every response: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; sandbox`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, a strong ETag = SHA-256. Names are reduced to a safe leaf and NEVER reach a storage path — keys are `{prefix}{2 hex}/{id}`. The 50 MB cap is checked before reading when the size is declared AND while copying; the transport's own limits apply first (`RaskUploadOptions.MaxFileSize` 50 MB, CQRS `MaxUploadBytes` 32 MB) — raise them alongside. `FileRejectedException : InvalidOperationException` (`Reason` = `FileRejection.TooLarge`/`TypeNotAllowed`, `Size`, `Limit`, `ContentType`): nothing is stored, and the message never repeats the uploaded name. CONSISTENCY: bytes are written before the row; the row commits on its OWN DbContext, NOT inside a transaction your handler has open — a row whose entity you then fail to save is yours to delete. A daily orphan sweep removes bytes with no row older than `OrphanGracePeriod` (24h, min 5 min); it fails closed on any database error, touches only its own key layout under the prefix, and REFUSES (deletes nothing, logs an error) when it would delete more than max(100, 10%) of what it looked at — the signature of the wrong database or two environments sharing a bucket/prefix. Changing `Rask__Storage__Provider` does not move files: old-provider rows make IFiles methods throw naming both providers and the routes 404. DISK FILES ARE NOT BACKED UP — `rask db backup`, Litestream and snapshots cover app.db only, while the rows ARE in app.db, so a restored database can point at missing files — and the disk store is NODE-LOCAL: use S3 or Azure for durability or for more than one instance. No multipart upload (one object ≤ 5 GiB on S3, ≤ 5000 MiB on Azure; a larger MaxFileSize fails at startup), no image resizing or thumbnails. The dashboard has a read-only Storage tab at `/_rask/storage`; `/_rask/files/…` is reserved for the file routes.
- [Data grid](docs/data-grid.md): `UiDataGrid<T>` in `Rask.Ui` — sortable headers, paging, selection, expandable detail rows, multi-level grouping with subtotals, a column chooser, sticky headers, column footers, and a card layout below `sm`. COLUMNS ARRIVE THROUGH A FACTORY: `Ui.DataGrid.Data(rows)[c => [ c.Field(p => p.Name).Title("Product") ]]`, and the lambda parameter is the GRID. That is not a style choice — C# infers a method's type arguments from its own arguments and never from the target type of the indexer it sits in, so `Ui.Column.Field(p => p.Name)` written as a flat child has nothing to tell it what `p` is and fails CS0411. That is why the column-factory indexer is declared on the grid itself — the chain's receiver IS the component, so an indexer declared there is offered on a grid and nowhere else, just as `Form` declares its own submit-state indexer. THREE DATA SOURCES: a list (in memory), an `IQueryable<T>` handed to the SAME `Data` step (ORDER BY/Skip/Take in the store — one step, because an IQueryable IS an IEnumerable and a second name for one slot is a second thing to get wrong), or an awaited `Source(request => Task<UiGridPage<T>>)` opened with `Of<T>()` since a lambda pins no type argument. EVERY STATE AXIS is controlled or uncontrolled independently (sort, page, selection, grouping, hidden columns, column order) — name the state AND its callback to take that one over. A sortable header cycles ascending -> descending -> OFF, the third state being the only way back to the source's own order. SELECTION IS TYPED AND STAGED: `.RowKey(p => p.Id)` pins the chain's key type and the selection steps are declared only over a pinned one, so a grid that cannot name a row is not one whose selection is rejected — it is one where selection is not offered. It is NOT called `Key`: that is the reconciliation identity of the grid itself. BELOW `sm` the table restyles into stacked labelled lines using the SAME markup (`data-label` + `before:content-[attr(data-label)]`), so the phone layout costs only classes; `.Card(p => ...)` replaces it with authored markup and THAT renders both layouts. GROUPING AND THE COLUMN CHOOSER ARE BUTTON-DRIVEN with drag added on top, because HTML5 drag fires on neither touch nor a keyboard. A custom `Cell` does NOT fire `OnRowClick` by default: the client cancels the default action of any click it dispatches, so a link or button inside a clickable cell silently stops working. NEEDS THE RUNTIME — every interaction is a C# handler. FOR A SCREEN THAT CANNOT SHIP ITS OWN CLASSES (a library such as Rask.Dashboard): `c.ShowFrom(Ui.Breakpoint.Md)` hides a column in TABLE mode below md (`sm:max-md:hidden`, a variant — the stacked phone lines still list it, and `Sm` is no change because the table starts there); `c.Mono()` sets the cells, not the title, in mono; `RowTone(r => Ui.Tone?)` tints a row from a complete literal (`RowClass` stays for an app whose own Tailwind sees its classes); `Toolbar(...)` is laid out as one row from sm up and one control per line below it; the pager under the rows is Flux UI's `Ui.Pagination` (summary, Previous/Next, numbered pages from 640px of its own width); `PageHref(page => RouteUrl)` makes the pager's pages LINKS, counted from zero like `Page` — the link navigates, `OnPage` is not called, and the page comes back as `Page` read from `[QueryParam("page")]`.
- [Tree](docs/tree.md): `UiTree<T, TKey>` in `Rask.Ui` — a hierarchy a reader opens, walks with the keyboard and selects from. DATA-DRIVEN, and A NODE'S CHILDREN ARRIVE THROUGH THE INDEXER, because the chain reserves the name `Children` for a component's own content: `Ui.Tree.Roots(files).NodeKey(f => f.Path).Item(f => Span[f.Name]).Label("Files")[f => f.Children]`. `NodeKey`, `Item` and `Label` are required steps; `NodeKey` is not `Key`, the chain's reconciliation identity. EXPANSION AND SELECTION ARE EACH CONTROLLED OR THE TREE'S OWN, one axis at a time, as on `Ui.DataGrid`: pass `Expanded`/`Selected` with `OnExpand`/`OnSelect` to hold an axis, leave them unset and the tree remembers. `ExpandDepth(1)` opens the roots on the FIRST render only (ignored when `Expanded` is controlled). `Selection` is `Ui.TreeSelection.None|One|Many`; passing `Selected`/`OnSelect` with no mode INFERS `One` rather than silently doing nothing. A `Selected` the PAGE changes moves the keyboard cursor to the first key it added, which scrolls it into view (open its ancestors via a controlled `Expanded` in the same render); a selection the reader made and the page echoes back leaves the cursor alone. ONE FOCUSABLE `role=tree` with an `aria-activedescendant` cursor (no roving tabindex, no JavaScript in Rask.Ui): arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, Right opens then descends, Left closes then climbs, `*` opens the row's siblings, Enter/Space select (Enter opens a branch when nothing is selectable), and TYPE-AHEAD over `NodeText` (a repeated letter cycles; a prefix expires after 500 ms). `ItemSize` switches to a VIRTUALIZED flat list over Core's `Virtualize` — fixed row height, `aria-level`/`aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` instead of nesting, `--ui-tree-depth` for the indent; unset renders nested `ul`/`li` that prerender. `OnHover` reports the node under the pointer and `default` on leaving (wired only when set; a touch is not a hover). A key seen twice renders ONCE, which is also what ends a cycle. Rask.Core's `rask-dom.ts` contains the navigation keys while a tree has focus and scrolls the cursor back into view — including to an unrendered row's computed offset in virtualized mode.
- [Logging](docs/logging.md): the `Rask.Logging` package (in `Rask.Server`, on by default) — a DURABLE log store with TWO backends behind one `ILogs`, both configured by `Rask:Logs` then the callback. On PostgreSQL/SQL Server use the APPLICATION DATABASE: `builder.Services.AddRaskLogging<AppDbContext>()` + `modelBuilder.AddRaskLogging()` (an internal `LogEntry` → table `RaskLog`, Category max 512, indexes Timestamp / (Level, Id desc) / (Category, Id desc); create it with a migration; no connection string of its own). There every flush runs on its OWN context + connection from `IDbContextFactory<TContext>`, so a line logged inside a rolled-back transaction is KEPT; a boot check names `modelBuilder.AddRaskLogging();` when the model never mapped it; an AsyncLocal `LogStoreScope` skips whatever EF Core logs on the store's own flow (no self-feeding SQL log) while the app's own EF SQL is still captured; retention reads each page's ids then `ExecuteDelete`s them, so two app instances sweeping at once remove each row once; both stores store NUL as U+FFFD (PostgreSQL rejects NUL in text); a store that keeps failing is reported once, then at most once a minute, and recovery counts only after a successful write; `o.Pragmas`/`o.BusyRetry` are file-store only. The scope filter on BOTH stores matches the JSON-encoded `"key":"value"` pair EXACTLY (`r2` ≠ `r22`; dotted or bracketed keys like `user.id` work; SQL Server compares by collation); Category/Search are case-insensitive substrings, and scopes ARE captured by default (`CaptureScopes`, `MaxScopeValues` 16, `MaxScopeValueLength` 256). On SQLite keep the FILE OF ITS OWN (not the app's DbContext, no migration): `RaskApp` registers it (on by default; `rask new --no-logs` writes `c.Logs.Off()`); by hand it is `builder.Services.AddRaskLogging(configure?)` — connection string `Rask:ConnectionStrings:Logs` (a missing one throws naming the key), options `Rask:Logs` then the callback; it takes a CONNECTION STRING rather than a `TContext`, which is the whole design: log lines arrive at machine rates and would put a high-frequency writer on the app database's single SQLite write lock, and the most valuable line is the one written WHILE A TRANSACTION IS FAILING — on the app's context that line rolls back with the failure. Trade-off, stated in the docs: `logs.db` is NOT covered by `rask db backup` or Litestream, and log lines can contain secrets. Registers a `[ProviderAlias("Rask")] ILoggerProvider` (via TryAddEnumerable, so a repeated call can't double-capture), so it sees exactly what every other sink sees — including the framework's `Rask.Live`/`Rask.Diff`/`Rask.Lifecycle` categories. PATH: a log call formats and `TryWrite`s into a bounded `Channel` (`BoundedChannelFullMode.DropWrite`, `QueueCapacity` 10_000) — it NEVER blocks or throws on the caller's thread; a full buffer DROPS the entry and counts it. The hosted `LogWriter` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer on `FlushInterval` 1s) drains it and inserts up to `BatchSize` (500) rows in ONE `InImmediateTransaction` (Rask.SQLite's non-blocking, thread-yielding busy-retry) with a single re-bound prepared command; `StopAsync` drains what's buffered under `ShutdownDrainTimeout` (5s) before completing the channel, because the lines just before a shutdown are the ones worth keeping. RETENTION every `PurgeInterval` (1h): entries older than `Retention` (14d, `TimeSpan.Zero` = forever) then a trim to the newest `MaxRows` (100_000, 0 = uncapped) — BOTH by default, since age alone can't bound the disk under a storm; deleted in pages of 1000 looping until drained, so the write lock is never held for a whole sweep. SCHEMA is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS RaskLog` (Id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY — a rowid alias, deliberately NOT AUTOINCREMENT; Timestamp TEXT round-trip "O" UTC so range filters are string compares and the file reads in a sqlite3 shell; Level INTEGER; Category; EventId; Message; Exception) + 3 indexes, created once behind a SemaphoreSlim, with the production pragmas (WAL matters: it's what lets the dashboard read while the writer flushes) applied on EVERY open. RE-ENTRANCY: `Rask.Logging*`, `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite*`, `Npgsql*` and `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient*` are ALWAYS excluded from capture whatever `o.ExcludedCategories` says — otherwise a database failure logs a line that fails to write that logs a line. `o.MinimumLevel` is a FLOOR, not an override (the pipeline applies `Logging:LogLevel` first). READ IT with `ILogs`: `Search(LogQuery{MinimumLevel, Category, Search, ScopeKey, ScopeValue, From, To, Page, PageSize})` → `LogPage(Entries newest-first, TotalCount, Page, PageSize, PageCount)`, plus `Categories`/`Count`/`Trim`/`Clear`; LIKE wildcards in user text are escaped, so searching `100%` means a literal percent. METRICS on meter `Rask.Logging`: `rask.logs.written`, `rask.logs.dropped` (THE ONE TO ALERT ON — a full buffer OR a batch whose write failed; it is the only signal that the stored log is incomplete), `rask.logs.purged`, `rask.logs.stored` (sampled by the writer, not per observation). `rask deploy` sets `Rask__ConnectionStrings__Logs=Data Source=/data/logs.db` on the same volume as app.db. In `Rask.Dashboard`, `/_rask/logs` gains a **History** mode (paged, level/category/text filters) beside the always-present in-memory **Live** tail — two modes rather than a merged view because the writer flushes on an interval, so the newest lines are buffered but not yet on disk. No reflection of its own: scope state is encoded with a source-generated `JsonSerializerContext` (the file store is trim/AOT clean; the application-database store is as AOT-ready as EF Core LINQ). The store's own INSERT is logged at `Debug` as well (the same housekeeping context every battery's poll uses), so a 1s FlushInterval does not echo each captured line back to the console as a second line of SQL — this is the CONSOLE half of what `LogStoreScope` already does for capture INTO the store.
- [Mobile & PWA](docs/pwa.md): build installable mobile apps in C#. WASM = full PWA (install, true offline, push, every device API); its service worker keeps the app SHELL offline (navigations, scripts/styles/fonts/images, `_framework/`), never a `no-store`/`private` response, a `fetch`ed API answer only when the server marks it `Cache-Control: public`, and signing out empties the cache — offline DATA belongs in browser SQLite or IndexedDB. Server = installable + push-capable via AddRaskPwa (serves manifest + service worker, auto-registers it, emits the manifest link into the server-rendered head), but NOT an offline app (offline navigations show a static offline.html; no background sync; the install event's `Prompt()` + activation-bound device APIs stay WASM-only, while the declarative `Trigger.Install` works on Server). Typed Web app manifest (WebAppManifest in Rask.Core.Browser; WASM UsePwa / Server AddRaskPwa), default service worker (rask-sw.js; shared push/notificationclick handlers in Rask.Core), the screen wake lock via Rask.Web's `Navigator.WakeLock.Request(WakeLockType.Screen)` (both hosts), Web Push subscription via Rask.Web's MDN PushManager (`(await Navigator.ServiceWorker.Ready).PushManager.Subscribe(…)`; no Rask wrapper), local notifications and the app badge via Rask.Web's Notification.Create / Navigator.SetAppBadge, on by default in every template (`--no-pwa` leaves it out). Sending push from the backend: the `Rask.WebPush` package in `Rask.Server` (`Push.Send(…)`, VAPID RFC 8292 + aes128gcm RFC 8291, zero external deps) — full reference in [Web Push](docs/webpush.md).
- [Web Push (server send)](docs/webpush.md): ON in `Rask.Server` (`c.Push.Off()`). The browsers that subscribed are kept in a `PushSubscriber` table on the app's own database; `await Push.Send(WebPushMessage.Text(title, body, url))` reaches all of them and returns how many were delivered, `.To(userId)` reaches one person's devices (each row records the user signed in when it subscribed), and a subscription the push service answers 404/410 is dropped during the send. Subscribe on the server host with MDN's PushManager from Rask.Web: `await using var w = await Navigator.ServiceWorker.Ready; await using var sub = await w.PushManager.Subscribe(new() { UserVisibleOnly = true, ApplicationServerKey = Base64Url.DecodeFromChars(Push.PublicKey) }); await Push.Subscribe(await sub.ToJSON());` (the PushSubscriptionJSON overload is in Rask.Server); a WASM client or SPA posts `sub.ToJSON()` — MDN's `{endpoint,expirationTime,keys:{p256dh,auth}}`, the flat `{endpoint,p256dh,auth}` is read too — to `POST /_rask/push/subscribe` (key from `GET /_rask/push/key`, `POST /_rask/push/unsubscribe`) — RaskApp maps them; by hand: `AddRaskWebPush<AppDbContext>()` + `modelBuilder.AddRaskWebPush()` + `app.MapRaskPush()`. `PushSubscription(Endpoint, P256dh, Auth, ExpirationTime?)` in Rask.Wire is the record the sender encrypts for. Keys: `Rask:Push` (`VapidKeys:PublicKey`/`PrivateKey` — dev pair in the gitignored appsettings.Development.json, environment when deployed; `Subject` = mailto:/https:); the table and endpoints work without keys, a send without them names the settings. Tests: `using var push = Push.Fake(); … push.Sent().To(userId).WithTitle("…").Once();`. `Push.Send(subscription, message)` / `IWebPush.Send` send to one subscription and return a WebPushResult (IsSuccess / ShouldDelete / ShouldRetry). WebPushMessage fields serialize to the default rask-sw.js JSON {title,body,icon,badge,tag,data.url}; Raw(json) for your own worker; Urgency/Ttl/Topic per RFC 8030; VAPID (RFC 8292) + aes128gcm (RFC 8291) with in-box crypto. `AddRaskWebPush()` (no context) = the sender alone. The subscribe route is open to anyone, so it is bounded: `Rask:Push:MaxAnonymousSubscribers` (10 000 signed-out rows, then 429), ten subscribes a minute per client, `RequireUser` for signed-in-only apps; a send never follows a redirect, refuses a name that resolves to a private/loopback/link-local address, times out after `SendTimeout` (10 s), and a broadcast sends eight at a time.
- [Observability](docs/observability.md): structured logging, the `Rask.Server` meter + activity source, `AddRaskLiveSessions()` health check.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): EVERY server-side Rask setting lives in appsettings.json under `Rask`, and each registration reads its own section itself — nobody writes `GetSection(...).Bind(...)`: `Rask:Live` (RaskLiveOptions), `Rask:Server` (RaskServerOptions, incl. `QuiescenceTimeout` and `CompressPageHtml` — default TRUE: the page HANDLER writes its own document as brotli or gzip per Accept-Encoding (q values honoured), HTTPS included, so the page HTML ships compressed (rask.sh landing: 78,525 B raw → 15,540 B gzip, 0.28 ms brotli per page) — ONLY the page: Rask adds no middleware and no AddResponseCompression, so the app's own endpoints and ResponseCompressionOptions are untouched; the BREACH note: the framework's own secret, `data-rask-root`, is minted FRESH per GET and no antiforgery token is rendered, so set it false only for a page rendering a long-lived app secret beside attacker-influenced input; an app that already compresses is not double-encoded), `Rask:Cultures`, `Rask:Uploads`, `Rask:Auth`, `Rask:Api`, `Rask:Signaling`, `Rask:Ops`, `Rask:Spa`, `Rask:Database`, `Rask:Sqlite`, `Rask:Postgres`, `Rask:SqlServer`, `Rask:Storage`, `Rask:Toasts`, `Rask:Litestream`, `Rask:Snapshots`, `Rask:Cache`, `Rask:Jobs`, `Rask:Logs`, `Rask:Mail`, `Rask:Outbox`, `Rask:Push`, `Rask:Cqrs`, `Rask:Cqrs:Server`, plus `Rask:ConnectionStrings:App`/`Logs` and `Rask:DataProtection:KeyPath`. PRECEDENCE, lowest first: options defaults → RaskApp's development defaults (lowest config source) → appsettings.json → appsettings.{Env}.json → user-secrets → environment variables (`Rask__Mail__From`) → command line → the code callback (`AddRaskMail(o => …)`) → validation; CODE WINS. TimeSpan `"[d.]hh:mm:ss"`, enums by name, arrays by index; lists that start non-empty (Cultures, Logs:ExcludedCategories, Spa:ImmutablePathPrefixes) are APPENDED to. A bad value fails HOST START with `OptionsValidationException` naming the section; a container with no IConfiguration gets defaults + callback; `Rask:Cqrs` is the one section read at registration. Delegates/builders stay code-only (`AuthorizeRoom`, `ExcludeFromFallback`, `OnPrepareResponse`, `Run<T>()`, `AddBehavior`/`AddOpenBehavior`), and browser/WASM apps are code-only. OLD KEYS ARE SILENTLY IGNORED: `ConnectionStrings:App`/`Logs`, `Litestream:ReplicaUrl`, `Sqlite:SnapshotDirectory` (now `Rask:Snapshots:DestinationDirectory`), `WebPush:PublicKey`/`PrivateKey`/`Subject` (now `Rask:Push:VapidKeys:*`/`Subject`), `Mail:PickupDirectory`, flat `Rask:<ServerOption>` (now `Rask:Server:<Option>`); `UseRaskSqlite(sp)`/`UseRaskPostgres(sp)`/`AddRaskSqlite()`/`AddRaskLogging()` lost their connection-string parameter. Also the live/server/upload option tables, shutdown drain, session resume and MaxSessions sizing. `Rask:Database:Provider` (sqlite|postgres|sqlserver) is read at registration by RaskApp, and by `UseRaskDatabase(sp)` when the context options are built.
- [Deployment](docs/deployment.md): containerizing the apps — every template scaffolds, by default (`--no-docker` leaves it out), a production multi-stage Dockerfile (+ `.dockerignore`): the `server` template builds on the .NET SDK image and run on `aspnet:10.0` (non-root, port 8080, `UseHttpsRedirection` no-ops in-container so terminate TLS at the proxy and forward the WebSocket upgrade); the standalone `wasm` bundle publishes then serves from `nginx:alpine` with a bundled `nginx.conf` (SPA `try_files` fallback, `application/wasm` MIME, `gzip_static` for the baked `*.gz`). GitHub Pages / sub-path via `/p:RaskPathBase=`. One-command deploy of that Dockerfile: `rask deploy --host root@box [--domain app.example.com]` builds the image on the box over SSH and runs it — with `--domain` a shared Caddy proxy adds automatic HTTPS and deploys are zero-downtime (blue-green), multiple apps to one host. Point it at a **bare VPS** (root + SSH key, nothing else) and it prepares the box first — Docker, a non-root `deploy` login, ufw, SSH hardening — after showing the plan and asking once, so you never SSH in yourself; `rask deploy --github-actions` writes the workflow that repeats it on every push. ufw alone does **not** filter Docker-published ports (docker writes its own iptables rules), so host setup also writes a `DOCKER-USER` block into `/etc/ufw/after.rules` that default-denies anything forwarded into a Docker bridge except the port this deploy publishes; open another with `ufw route allow`.
- [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md): typed ARIA generated from the WAI-ARIA spec (`.AriaLabel("Close")`, `.AriaExpanded(open)` bool?, `.AriaLive(AriaLive.Polite)` keyword enums, `.AriaLevel(2)`, `.AriaLabelledBy("id")`; `AriaRole.*` constants for `.Role(...)`), the `Aria` dictionary for anything else (a typed step wins over its key; order: aria-* typed, then the bag), `Role`/`TabIndex`, `Lang`/`Dir` for WCAG 3.1.2 (Language of Parts) and `Hidden`/`Inert`, the `Img` alt-text analyzer (RASK023), and automatic navigation a11y on the Server host (SPA route changes show a progress bar, move focus into the new page's `<main>`, and announce the route via `aria-live`).
- [Localization](docs/localization.md): ship in more than one language. Configured in appsettings.json — `"Rask": { "Cultures": [ "en", "hu" ] }` (env `Rask__Cultures__0=en`), the FIRST entry being the default; an `AddRask(configureCulture: c => c.SupportedCultures.Add("hu"))` callback APPENDS to the configured list rather than replacing it; a browser-WASM app has no appsettings and names its languages in code. There is NO --culture flag and no --no-localization (#854): a scaffolded server app already lists "en" there and adding a language is an entry in that list, so a flag would only restate at scaffold time what the file goes on being the truth about. A visitor's language is negotiated `?culture=` → cookie → `Accept-Language`/`navigator.languages` → default, settled BEFORE the first render on both hosts (the server's first HTML byte already carries `lang="hu"`), and then owned by their session rather than the thread — which is why it survives the framework's deliberate `ExecutionContext.SuppressFlow()`. **URLs stay culture-neutral**: one link is the same page for everyone, and the router/`Url()`/`Go()` are untouched. The cookie is ASP.NET's own `.AspNetCore.Culture` in ASP.NET's own format, so an app also calling `UseRequestLocalization()` agrees with it. Text lives in `Resources/Strings.{culture}.json` and compiles to typed members: `Strings.Greeting(name)`, where a typo'd key is CS0117 and a wrong argument count CS1501 — no reflection, no satellite assemblies, so it works under `InvariantGlobalization` too (only date/number formatting falls back). Placeholders are named (`{name}`, `{count:int}`, `{price:decimal:C}`) because other languages reorder arguments; a mismatched placeholder SET is RASK051 (error, it would throw `FormatException` in that one language), a missing translation is RASK052 (warning, neutral text is used — promote it in `.editorconfig` to gate a release). Counts use `{ "$plural": "count", "one": …, "other": … }` with a curated CLDR table; the required fallback is the language's own residual, which is `many` for Polish and Russian rather than `other`, and a language Rask does not carry is a build error naming it. Components read `Culture`/`UICulture`/`IsRightToLeft`, which also marks them so a switch repaints. Wire formats stay invariant on purpose (`<input type=date|number>`, route values, reconciliation keys — the browser localizes typed inputs itself). `<html lang>` follows the session and `dir="rtl"` is emitted only for RTL; an app that names no language renders byte-identical HTML to before. WASM needs `<RaskGlobalization>true</RaskGlobalization>` for ICU (~2.6 MB of `icudt*.dat`; +3.92 MB raw / +1.05 MB brotli on a published bundle once the larger non-invariant runtime is counted), which also clears `PredefinedCulturesOnly` — otherwise `GetCultureInfo("hu-HU")` throws rather than falling back. a browser-WASM app scaffolds NO culture registration and carries `<RaskGlobalization>` COMMENTED OUT with the reason beside it, so shipping a language there is two deliberate edits — uncomment the property, add the languages in Program.cs: catalogs without ICU are a no-op, because the resolver refuses to let a culture pose as supported when the data isn't there, so the app would boot with an EMPTY supported list and warn once at startup (#846 — both WASM generators used to accept `--culture` and emit nothing at all). The framework's own text (picker chrome, 404, error page) translates via a reserved `Resources/RaskStrings.{culture}.json` whose keys are `RaskString` members, registered by a generated module initializer with no wiring. EVERY fixed text the UI kit (`Rask.Ui`) writes is such a key — the pager (`PaginationSummary` = "Showing {0} to {1} of {2} results", `PaginationPrevious`, `PaginationNext`), select (`SelectEmpty`, `SelectLoading`, `SelectSearchPlaceholder`, `SelectClear`, `SelectSelectedSuffix`), date/time pickers (`DatePickerPlaceholder`, `DatePickerRangePlaceholder`, `DatePickerConfirm`, `DatePickerCancel`, `CalendarToday`, `DateRangePreset*`, `TimePickerPlaceholder`), editor toolbar (`Editor*`), input actions (`Input*`), `ModalClose`, `ConfirmLeaveStay`/`ConfirmLeaveLeave`, `OtpCharacter`, `SliderRangeStart`/`End`, `Rating*`, `Sidebar*`, `DataGrid*` — the full table with each English default is in docs/localization.md. Lookup order: the APP's catalog, then the KIT's own translation (Rask.Ui ships Hungarian, `hu`, built in — an app that lists `hu` in `SupportedCultures` gets a Hungarian pager/select/date picker with no catalog; with no `SupportedCultures` the kit stays English whatever the machine's language), then the English literal. A text with values numbers them (`{0}`, `{1:N0}`) so a translation reorders them — read in C# with `RaskStrings.Get(RaskString.PaginationSummary, "Showing {0} to {1} of {2} results", from, to, total)`; a `{3}` the text does not carry or a named `{total}` is build error RASK051; no plural forms. A component library ships its own translations with the same file plus `<RaskStringsLibrary>true</RaskStringsLibrary>` (registered UNDER the app's catalog via `RaskStrings.UseLibrarySource`).
- [Migration from Blazor](docs/migration-from-blazor.md): mapping Blazor concepts to Rask.
- [Diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md): RASK001–101 compile-time diagnostics + fixes (RASK027/030/032/034/042/046/047/048/049/050/054/075/081 retired and never reused; RASK063/065 reserved) and the islands build's RASKISLAND001–018 (each with its fix: Node too old, a props snapshot to refresh, two runtimes sharing a folder), including IDE quick-fixes (lightbulb) for RASK001 (add `required`), RASK014 (rewrite `new Widget()` as the bare entry), RASK023 (append `.Alt("")`), RASK026, RASK071 (swap ASP.NET's `[Route]` for Rask's own — the two differ only by namespace, and the ASP.NET one leaves the page silently unregistered), RASK084 (an error: an entity's or value object's public setter/init/mutable field becomes private — a positional record's init is exempt), RASK085 (an entity's `List<OtherEntity>` becomes a `private readonly` field behind `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`, which EF Core maps through the backing field by convention), RASK095 (a chain that skips a required step — `'Card' needs 'Title' before anything else — write Card.Title(…).Note(…)` — the fix inserts the missing steps), RASK096 (an event declared as `Action<T>`/`Func<T, Task>` must be a non-nullable `Callback<T>`, or its chain setter is unreachable — the fix rewrites the type and `OnSave?.Invoke(x)` → `await OnSave.Invoke(x)`), shipped in `Rask.Generators.CodeFixes`. **CS0108 needs no answer at all**: `RASKSUP001` suppresses it whenever the hidden member is a chain entry, so a property named `Title`, `Label` or `Form` costs you no `new`, while hiding a real member of your own base type still warns. It is the ONE diagnostic Rask does not escalate to an error, because `dotnet format` does not honour suppressors and surfaces it anyway.
- [DevTools](docs/devtools.md): `Rask.DevTools` — an in-page panel for a running app, opened from the **Rask** pill in the page's bottom-left corner or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+D, docked bottom or right. `rask new` apps already reference it; an existing app adds `Rask.DevTools` AND `Rask.Ui` (the panel is drawn with the kit; without it the devtools stay off and a Server host logs a warning). ON ONLY WHEN: a Debug build (`RaskDevTools` defaults to `true` in Debug, `false` otherwise) AND, on Server, the `Development` environment and a loopback client (`RASK_DEVTOOLS_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` allows a remote one), or, on WASM, a page served from a loopback origin. With `RaskDevTools=false` a publish removes the assembly, its scripts and its deps.json entry and FAILS if any remain. **Wire** lists each frame (sent events by `type`, received render frames with their diff op count, size, gap); the panel's own traffic is never recorded. **Tree** shows components NESTED AS ON THE PAGE (the component a child is walked inside, not the one that built it), each row with its key and `Name=value` props read by a build-generated `DescribeProps` override (no reflection, trimmed WASM included); HTML elements between components behind a "Show HTML tags" toggle; ready on open (built from the page's last render) and stable ids keep opened branches open. Pointing at a row draws a labelled box (`TaskRow · 612×44`) around what that component rendered on the page (drawn in the devtools' shadow root; the row carries its DOM place, so no round trip); the **Pick** button puts a glass over the page — point, click, and the tree opens to the nearest component (the element itself with tags shown) and selects it; the click never reaches the app; Esc cancels. Kit components that ARE an element (`Ui.Button`, `Ui.List`, any `UiElement`) are not tree nodes of their own. External islands ARE component rows (badge = runtime: React/Preact/Solid/Vue/Svelte/Angular/Lit) with the C# props passed, no children (their tree lives in the browser); Blazor components are badged `Blazor`. Selecting a row opens a detail pane: key, badge, every prop as name / short type / value (redacted marked), plus context: Provides (type, name, value — redacted when the name or type name contains password/secret/token/apikey/credential/passcode, or is pin/ssn) and Reads (type, name, and the provider = the component the `Context.Provide` sits inside on the page, as a link that selects it, or "none in scope"). Context is recorded only while a panel is open, so it appears from the page's next render after opening. Props named like password/passcode/secret/token/apikey/credential, exactly pin/ssn, or marked `[DataType(DataType.Password)]`/`[PasswordPropertyText]`/`[PersonalData]`/`[ProtectedPersonalData]` are never read and show as `••••`. **Renders** counts only components whose `Render()` RAN (cache-served ones are left out): By component (per instance: renders, reason badges, own Render() time excluding children, last commit; most renders first) or By commit (N of M components rendered, folded `TaskRow ×3`); reasons `mount` (first render the devtools saw), `props`, `state`, `bypass cache` (BypassRenderCache), `context` (read context/culture), `children` (takes children), `uncached`; holds the last 200 commits or 5,000 renders; **Clear** resets. **Flash on the page** (Renders tab, off by default, remembered in the page's localStorage `rask.devtools.flash`): AMBER box + `Type · reason` label around each component that rendered (places recorded only while flashing, posted by the panel after each commit, so slightly after the patch), TEAL box around each node the patch changed (host MutationObserver, instant); amber with no teal inside = a render that changed nothing. Keeps flashing with the drawer closed; after a reload with it on, the panel loads behind the closed drawer. **Perf** lists interactions newest first — trigger (page event + handler's component, `click TaskBoard`; `navigate`; `render` for an unrequested render), handler own time (renders during it excluded), render, diff, frame size ("nothing sent" = no change or the first HTML render), page patch time (the page's own measurement, matched by frame size) and total; p50/p95 server time and p50 patch; plus slowest components by total own Render() time (renders, average, slowest). Keeps 500 interactions; **Clear** resets. **Errors** lists newest first: component exceptions (`render` / `handler` / `lifecycle`) with the innermost exception's type + message, the component path outermost first, "caught by an error boundary" or not, and the stack; and framework `RaskDiagnostics` warnings/errors (Information skipped). A red count of UNSEEN errors (not warnings) on the Errors tab and the pill; opening the tab marks them seen. Diagnostics reported during a page's render/handler belong to that page, others are **app-wide** in every panel (filters: All / This page / App-wide). Consecutive repeats show ×N. **Show in tree** selects the component in the Tree tab. Under hot reload (`rask dev` / `dotnet watch`) the dev-error overlay gets an **Open in DevTools** button. Page-side failures are listed too: uncaught script errors and unhandled promise rejections (`page script`), and island mount/update/unmount/props failures (`island`, under the component the island sits in); counted on the pill immediately, the last 50 held until the panel opens; `console.error` is NOT captured. `rask-external.js` catches a throwing island `update` (it used to escape the page's MutationObserver callback) and logs it. **Report framework bug** appears only when the innermost non-BCL frame is Rask's (namespace `Rask.*` not the app's entry-assembly/component namespace; for page scripts, a Rask script); it opens an EDITABLE draft (exception type, where, component type names, host + Rask/.NET/OS/browser versions, Rask frames with app frames as `[app code]`; NEVER message, props, data or file paths) and a link to a pre-filled `https://github.com/pal-tamas/rask/issues/new?labels=bug` issue (≤8,000-char URL) the developer submits.
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): the `Rask.Testing` package — a page comes from `Page`: **`Page.Visit("/products/new")` opens the app at a URL through the REAL router** and is what a feature test uses, driving it the way a person does with `await page.Type("Tea").Into("Name")`, `await page.Pick("Green").From("Colour")`, `await page.Check("In stock")`, `await page.Click("Save")` (`.In("region")` narrows an ambiguous one), then `page.Shows("Saved")` / `page.DoesNotShow("Loading…")` (both WAIT up to `page.Patience`, 5 s, for async work) and `page.IsAt("/products")`; fields are found by label → placeholder → aria-label, and a lookup that finds nothing or too much throws a `PageException` naming what it did find. `Test` keeps only what is about the test, not the page (`Mail.Fake()`, `Clock.Fake(at)`, `Push.Fake()`, `Test.EditContextProbe`). Underneath: (`Page.Render(component)` → `Page<T>`, adding no markup of its own, and `Page.RenderDocument(app, services?)` when the assertion is about the PAGE — it renders a root the way a host does, document composed around it, so `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html lang>`, the collected `<head>` and `<body class>` are all assertable; `.On(selector).Click()`/`.Input(v)`/`.Change(v)`/`.Submit(form?)`/`.Raise(event, json?)` and `.Invoke(handlerId, json?)` dispatch handlers + re-render; `.Html`/`.HandlerId`/`.Attr` query) for in-process component unit tests, plus Playwright E2E patterns. Render MOUNTS the component (OnMount, OnUpdated, OnFirstRender, OnRendered, OnUnmount all fire) and gives it a render handle, so state set after an await in an async lifecycle hook reaches the markup; for a component that loads in OnMount use `page.Shows("text")` or `page.Shows(html => …)` — synchronous, it re-renders for up to `page.Patience` until it holds and throws a `PageException` carrying what the page shows, rather than a fixed delay. Note `Text` HTML-encodes non-ASCII, so an ellipsis in a placeholder ("Reading…") is NOT a literal substring of `.Html`. **A FLOW ACROSS BATTERIES IN ONE TEST**: every static has a fake (`Mail.Fake()`, `Jobs.Fake()`, `Outbox.Fake()`, `Cache.Fake()`, `Files.Fake()`, `Push.Fake()`) that records and runs nothing until asked — `await outbox.Run(); await jobs.Run();` then `mail.Sent().To("ann@example.com").Once()`; `Run()` executes recorded work through the REAL handlers as the tenant and user who started it.

## More guides
- [Cheat sheet](docs/cheatsheet.md): One dense page of every rask CLI command and flag, a CRUD slice in one place, and the idioms for data, CQRS, jobs, mail, cache, outbox, auth and routing.
- [Recipes](docs/recipes.md): Task-first answers for an existing app: add a CRUD feature, relate entities, require login, run background work, send email, cache queries, deploy and test.
- [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md): What is shipped and what is next for the full-stack .NET web framework: UI hosts, CLI, CQRS, data, jobs, mail, cache, outbox and SQLite, plus known gaps.
- [Ch 1 · Scaffold](docs/tutorial/01-scaffold.md): Create the Shop project with rask new, run it, and tour what the server template generates: an ASP.NET Core app with SQLite, auth and batteries wired.
- [Ch 2 · First feature](docs/tutorial/02-first-feature.md): Build a database-backed Products catalog: declare the aggregate, write its list, create and edit pages, bind Rask.Ui forms, then add the migration.
- [Ch 3 · Orders & auth](docs/tutorial/03-orders-and-auth.md): Add an Orders feature on the same DbContext and SQLite database, then lock down catalog edits with [Authorize] pages and the Authorize component in C#.
- [Ch 4 · Background jobs](docs/tutorial/04-background-jobs.md): Move order processing off the request thread with a durable background job stored in SQLite: write a job and handler, enqueue it, and let it retry on failure.
- [Ch 5 · Email](docs/tutorial/05-email.md): Email customers an order receipt whose body is a C# component. Mail is queued in SQLite and sent over SMTP by a background worker, triggered from a job.
- [Ch 6 · Cache](docs/tutorial/06-cache.md): Cache the product list in a typed, SQLite-backed cache: write an accessor around Cache.Remember, read through it, and forget it when the catalog changes.
- [Ch 7 · Outbox & events](docs/tutorial/07-outbox-events.md): Raise a domain event when an order is placed; each handler runs in memory, or durably through a transactional outbox that survives a crash. C# and EF Core.
- [Ch 8 · Production SQLite](docs/tutorial/08-production-sqlite.md): Make one SQLite file production-safe for a .NET app: WAL, busy-timeout and foreign-key pragmas, scheduled snapshots and off-box backup with Litestream.
- [Ch 9 · Push](docs/tutorial/09-web-push.md): Send Web Push from your own ASP.NET Core server with VAPID keys: the scaffolded wiring, subscribing a browser, and pushing from an outbox handler.
- [Ch 10 · Watching it run](docs/tutorial/10-ops.md): Build an /ops page that reads each pillar's SQLite table to show outbox, job, mail and cache state, make it live, check pragmas, and meet the dashboard.
- [Ch 11 · Deploy](docs/tutorial/11-deploy.md): Ship the app to one Linux server with rask deploy: a Docker image built over SSH, automatic Let's Encrypt HTTPS via Caddy, health-checked swaps, CI deploys.
- [Auth — cookie](docs/authentication-cookie.md): Wire cookie-based login and sessions by hand, for the server-rendered WebSocket host and for a WebAssembly SPA backed by your own ASP.NET Core API.
- [Auth — providers](docs/authentication-providers.md): Sign in through Keycloak, Auth0, AWS Cognito or Duende IdentityServer over OpenID Connect, with Rask still owning the session cookie.
- [Auth — hardening](docs/authentication-hardening.md): Harden authentication for production: session trust model, CSRF protection, reverse proxy forwarded headers, Content-Security-Policy and a security checklist.
- [Composition — callbacks & context](docs/composition-callbacks-context.md): Send events from a child component to its parent with Callback properties that re-render the owner, and pass values down with context, not prop drilling.
- [Composition — lists & more](docs/composition-lists.md): Render windowed lists with Virtualize, keep list identity with keys, and add toast messages, drag-and-drop and error boundaries to C# web components.
- [Forms — validation](docs/forms-validation.md): Validate a form with inline rules on a field or the form, sync or async, or with DataAnnotations. A database unique-constraint error shows under its field.
- [Forms — advanced](docs/forms-advanced.md): Bind and validate nested models and collections, build radio and checkbox groups, keep form state across a redeploy, and write your own form controls in C#.
- [JS interop — runtime](docs/js-interop-runtime.md): Call JavaScript from C# with an injected IJSRuntime, use typed browser APIs and element refs, and wrap a third-party JavaScript library with TypeScript types.
- [Tailwind CSS](docs/tailwind.md): Compile Tailwind CSS and daisyUI with dotnet build: no package.json, node_modules or PostCSS. The build scans your C# for classes, with knobs and fixes.
- [Browser APIs — sharing model](docs/browser-apis-sharing.md): Which typed browser APIs run on server and WASM hosts, declarative Web Share and gesture triggers on the server, and subscriptions that push updates into C#.
- [Browser APIs — reference & demos](docs/browser-apis-reference.md): Runnable demos for the browser APIs, C# source beside the live result: storage, environment, location, sensors, observers, media, crypto and files.
- [Capability matrix](docs/browser-capabilities.md): See which browser and device APIs work from C# on the Server host and on WebAssembly, which need a click-gesture component, and which are WASM-only.
- [IIndexedDb](docs/apis/indexeddb.md): Store strings and byte arrays in IndexedDB from C# through an async key/value store. Works on Server and WebAssembly; bytes are kept as a real Uint8Array.
- [IWebAuthn](docs/apis/webauthn.md): Register and sign in users with passkeys from C# through IWebAuthn, a typed Web Authentication API (WebAuthn) wrapper for Server and WebAssembly hosts.
- [IWebRtc](docs/apis/webrtc.md): Connect two browsers peer-to-peer from C# with IWebRtc: WebRTC data channels with batched messages plus camera, microphone and screen streams.
- [ISignaling](docs/apis/signaling.md): Relay WebRTC offers, answers and ICE candidates between browsers with ISignaling and a WebSocket relay on any ASP.NET host. Authentication is on by default.
- [IBackgroundSync](docs/apis/background-sync.md): Register one-off and periodic Background Sync from C# and get the woken tag in a callback. WASM-only; needs a service worker and runs while a tab is open.
- [Secrets](docs/secrets.md): Keep secrets out of source control: put them in .env.production, deploy with rask deploy --env-file, read them via IConfiguration, and know the limits.
- [Scaling](docs/scaling.md): How far one server goes: measured live sessions per GiB, what survives a restart, the single SQLite writer as the real wall, and running more instances.

## Contributing to Rask itself
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): conventions for AI assistants CONTRIBUTING to Rask + the `.claude/skills/` workflows (app guidance is docs/ai-agents.md).
- [Development workflow](docs/development-workflow.md): the format → warnings-as-errors → tests →
  benchmarks → docs → review gate, landing on main, CI, nightly, analyzers.
- [Code analysis](docs/code-analysis.md): analyzers, adoption, and the SOLID + Clean Code design standard.
- [Public API style](docs/api-style.md): the naming rules every public member obeys, and the PublicAPI.txt gate that enforces them.
- [Repo administration](docs/repo-administration.md): The GitHub settings behind the repository: branch protection on main, required code owner review, why no status checks are required, and workflow secrets.
- [Live-rendering internals](docs/architecture/live-rendering.md): How one C# component tree stays live after first paint: a shared render and diff pipeline, sent over a WebSocket on ASP.NET Core or JSImport on WebAssembly.
- [Live rendering — walk & codec](docs/architecture/live-rendering-codec.md): How a render emits HTML and a frame stream together, how FrameDiffer turns two renders into minimal edit ops, the JSON wire format, and LIS-based keyed moves.
- [Live rendering — cache & dispatch](docs/architecture/live-rendering-runtime.md): Inside a live session: the two-buffer diff baseline, head and query-only navigations, handler ordering on WebSocket and WASM, and slow-connection indicators.
